<h1 id="windmill-api-health">health</h1>

## health status

<a id="opIdgetHealthStatus"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/health/status \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /health/status`

Health status endpoint. Returns cached health status (database connectivity, worker count).
Cache TTL is fixed at 5 seconds. Use force=true query parameter to bypass cache.
Note: This endpoint is intentionally different from Kubernetes probes to avoid confusion.
For k8s liveness/readiness probes, use /version endpoint.


<h3 id="health-status-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|force|query|boolean|false|Force a fresh check, bypassing the cache|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "status": "healthy",
  "checked_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "database_healthy": true,
  "workers_alive": 0
}
```

> 503 Response

```json
{
  "status": "healthy",
  "checked_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "database_healthy": true,
  "workers_alive": 0
}
```

<h3 id="health-status-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|server is healthy or degraded|[HealthStatusResponse](#schemahealthstatusresponse)|
|503|Service Unavailable|server is unhealthy (database unreachable)|[HealthStatusResponse](#schemahealthstatusresponse)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## detailed health status

<a id="opIdgetHealthDetailed"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/health/detailed \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /health/detailed`

Returns detailed health information including database pool stats, worker details, and queue status.
Requires authentication. Use for monitoring dashboards and debugging.
This endpoint always returns fresh data (no caching).


> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "status": "healthy",
  "checked_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "version": "string",
  "checks": {
    "database": {
      "healthy": true,
      "latency_ms": 0,
      "pool": {
        "size": 0,
        "idle": 0,
        "max_connections": 0
      }
    },
    "workers": {
      "healthy": true,
      "active_count": 0,
      "worker_groups": [
        "string"
      ],
      "min_version": "string",
      "versions": [
        "string"
      ]
    },
    "queue": {
      "pending_jobs": 0,
      "running_jobs": 0
    },
    "readiness": {
      "healthy": true
    }
  }
}
```

> 503 Response

```json
{
  "status": "healthy",
  "checked_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "version": "string",
  "checks": {
    "database": {
      "healthy": true,
      "latency_ms": 0,
      "pool": {
        "size": 0,
        "idle": 0,
        "max_connections": 0
      }
    },
    "workers": {
      "healthy": true,
      "active_count": 0,
      "worker_groups": [
        "string"
      ],
      "min_version": "string",
      "versions": [
        "string"
      ]
    },
    "queue": {
      "pending_jobs": 0,
      "running_jobs": 0
    },
    "readiness": {
      "healthy": true
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="detailed-health-status-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|server is healthy or degraded|[DetailedHealthResponse](#schemadetailedhealthresponse)|
|503|Service Unavailable|server is unhealthy (database unreachable)|[DetailedHealthResponse](#schemadetailedhealthresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

<h1 id="windmill-api-documentation">documentation</h1>

## Full-text search across the entire Windmill documentation. Provide one or more keywords; returns the most relevant docs pages, each with its Source URL and short matching snippets. Use this FIRST to find relevant pages by their content (a flag, function, error message, config key or concept). If the snippets answer the question, answer directly; otherwise call readDocsPage with a returned Source URL to read more.

<a id="opIdsearchDocs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'http://localhost:8000/api/docs/search?query=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /docs/search`

<h3 id="full-text-search-across-the-entire-windmill-documentation-provide-one-or-more-keywords-returns-the-most-relevant-docs-pages-each-with-its-source-url-and-short-matching-snippets-use-this-first-to-find-relevant-pages-by-their-content-a-flag-function-error-message-config-key-or-concept-if-the-snippets-answer-the-question-answer-directly-otherwise-call-readdocspage-with-a-returned-source-url-to-read-more-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|query|query|string|true|Keywords to search for in the documentation body, e.g. "chromium worker tag" or "retry exponential backoff". Fewer, more distinctive words match better.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "text": "string",
  "results": [
    {
      "url": "string",
      "title": "string",
      "score": 0,
      "snippets": [
        "string"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="full-text-search-across-the-entire-windmill-documentation-provide-one-or-more-keywords-returns-the-most-relevant-docs-pages-each-with-its-source-url-and-short-matching-snippets-use-this-first-to-find-relevant-pages-by-their-content-a-flag-function-error-message-config-key-or-concept-if-the-snippets-answer-the-question-answer-directly-otherwise-call-readdocspage-with-a-returned-source-url-to-read-more-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|matching documentation pages|Inline|

<h3 id="full-text-search-across-the-entire-windmill-documentation-provide-one-or-more-keywords-returns-the-most-relevant-docs-pages-each-with-its-source-url-and-short-matching-snippets-use-this-first-to-find-relevant-pages-by-their-content-a-flag-function-error-message-config-key-or-concept-if-the-snippets-answer-the-question-answer-directly-otherwise-call-readdocspage-with-a-returned-source-url-to-read-more-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|text|string|true|none|Model-ready rendering of the results|
|results|[object]|true|none|none|
|» url|string|true|none|none|
|» title|string|true|none|none|
|» score|integer|true|none|none|
|» snippets|[string]|true|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

## Fetch the markdown of a single Windmill documentation page. Provide the `url` of a page found via searchDocs (its Source URL). If the page is large, this returns its list of section headings instead of the full content; call again with the `section` argument set to one of those headings to read that section.

<a id="opIdreadDocsPage"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'http://localhost:8000/api/docs/page?url=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /docs/page`

<h3 id="fetch-the-markdown-of-a-single-windmill-documentation-page-provide-the-url-of-a-page-found-via-searchdocs-its-source-url-if-the-page-is-large-this-returns-its-list-of-section-headings-instead-of-the-full-content-call-again-with-the-section-argument-set-to-one-of-those-headings-to-read-that-section-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|url|query|string|true|The docs page to read, as a Source URL returned by searchDocs (e.g. https://www.windmill.dev/docs/core_concepts/jobs). A bare path (e.g. /docs/core_concepts/jobs) is also accepted.|
|section|query|string|false|Optional. A heading title from the page outline to read just that section instead of the full page.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "text": "string",
  "source_url": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="fetch-the-markdown-of-a-single-windmill-documentation-page-provide-the-url-of-a-page-found-via-searchdocs-its-source-url-if-the-page-is-large-this-returns-its-list-of-section-headings-instead-of-the-full-content-call-again-with-the-section-argument-set-to-one-of-those-headings-to-read-that-section-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|documentation page content|Inline|

<h3 id="fetch-the-markdown-of-a-single-windmill-documentation-page-provide-the-url-of-a-page-found-via-searchdocs-its-source-url-if-the-page-is-large-this-returns-its-list-of-section-headings-instead-of-the-full-content-call-again-with-the-section-argument-set-to-one-of-those-headings-to-read-that-section-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|text|string|true|none|none|
|source_url|string|true|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

## list audit logs (requires admin privilege)

<a id="opIdlistAuditLogs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/audit/list \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /w/{workspace}/audit/list`

<h3 id="list-audit-logs-requires-admin-privilege-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|page|query|integer|false|which page to return (start at 1, default 1)|
|per_page|query|integer|false|number of items to return for a given page (default 30, max 100)|
|before|query|string(date-time)|false|filter on started before (inclusive) timestamp|
|after|query|string(date-time)|false|filter on created after (exclusive) timestamp|
|username|query|string|false|filter on exact username of user|
|operation|query|string|false|filter on exact or prefix name of operation|
|operations|query|string|false|comma separated list of exact operations to include|
|exclude_operations|query|string|false|comma separated list of operations to exclude|
|resource|query|string|false|filter on exact or prefix name of resource|
|action_kind|query|string|false|filter on type of operation|
|before_id|query|integer(int64)|false|only return logs with an id strictly lower than this one. Logs are ordered by descending id, so this is a keyset cursor to stream a page in several batches without paying a growing offset.<br>|
|all_workspaces|query|boolean|false|get audit logs for all workspaces|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|action_kind|Create|
|action_kind|Update|
|action_kind|Delete|
|action_kind|Execute|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "workspace_id": "string",
    "id": 0,
    "timestamp": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "username": "string",
    "operation": "jobs.run",
    "action_kind": "Created",
    "resource": "string",
    "parameters": {},
    "span": "string"
  }
]
```

<h3 id="list-audit-logs-requires-admin-privilege-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|a list of audit logs|Inline|

<h3 id="list-audit-logs-requires-admin-privilege-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[[AuditLog](#schemaauditlog)]|false|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

<h3 id="check-if-smtp-is-configured-for-password-reset-responses">Responses</h3>

## list the distinct guests of the trailing window (superadmin only)

<a id="opIdlistGuests"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/users/guests \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /users/guests`

The set the guest allowance is counted on: every distinct email that held a guest session in the last `window_days`, with the workspaces it opened and the days it was first and last seen, most recently seen first. `usage` is the instance's standing against the allowance and the meter.

<h3 id="list-the-distinct-guests-of-the-trailing-window-superadmin-only-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page|query|integer|false|none|
|per_page|query|integer|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "usage": {
    "available": true,
    "guest_count": 0,
    "window_days": 0,
    "free_allowance": 0,
    "metered": true,
    "billable_guests": 0,
    "guest_seats": 0
  },
  "guests": [
    {
      "email": "string",
      "workspaces": [
        "string"
      ],
      "first_seen": "1970-01-01",
      "last_seen": "1970-01-01"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="list-the-distinct-guests-of-the-trailing-window-superadmin-only-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|

bearerAuth, cookieAuth

```json
  ],
```

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/users/login_links \

  -H 'Accept: application/json' \

    "email": "string",
    "expires_in_s": 0,
    "rd": "string",
    "require_login_type": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /users/login_links`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "email": "string",
  "expires_in_s": 0,
  "rd": "string",
  "require_login_type": "string"
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|target account and link options|
|» email|body|string|true|none|

|» rd|body|string|false|same-origin path the browser lands on after login (default /user/workspaces)|

|body|body|object|true|none|
|» email|body|string|true|none|
|» profile|body|object|true|free-form context from the invite, every key optional. The frontend reads `touch_point` (answers onboarding's source question), `company` and `workspace_name` (prefill the first workspace's name), `hub_projects` (slugs surfaced first on an empty workspace), `tools` (integrations, used to pick hub projects when none are named) and `starter_prompts` (`[{label, prompt}]`, replacing the home page's example prompts); unknown keys are kept and ignored|

|200|OK|profile recorded|Inline|

bearerAuth, cookieAuth

## Where a repository's credential comes from

<a id="opIdgetCredentialOrigin"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/git_sync/credential/origin?path=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /w/{workspace}/git_sync/credential/origin`

Whether Windmill holds this repository's access token, and which host it talks to. `held` means this workspace stores it, `borrowed` means an ancestor does and it is not this workspace's to replace. Both absent means the repository authenticates with whatever its URL carries. Returns no secret. Requires workspace admin.

<h3 id="where-a-repositorys-credential-comes-from-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|path|query|string|true|Path of the git repository resource, with or without the `$res:` prefix. A path rather than a URL, because a resource URL may carry a token and a URL in a query string lands in logs.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "origin": "held",
  "provider": "gitlab"
}
```

<h3 id="where-a-repositorys-credential-comes-from-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|where the credential comes from|Inline|

<h3 id="where-a-repositorys-credential-comes-from-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|origin|string|false|none|none|
|provider|string|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|origin|held|
|origin|borrowed|
|provider|gitlab|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

## Store the credential for a git repository

<a id="opIdsetGitCredential"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/git_sync/credential \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "repo_url": "string",
    "token": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /w/{workspace}/git_sync/credential`

Stores the access token a git repository authenticates with, so it does not have to be written into the repository URL or a workspace variable. The token is write-only: it is served only to a git-sync job that presents its own job token, and a fork of this workspace reads this copy instead of holding one of its own. Requires workspace admin.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "repo_url": "string",
  "token": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="store-the-credential-for-a-git-repository-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» repo_url|body|string|true|The repository the credential is for, and the key it is stored under. It is served for this repository and no other, so repointing a resource elsewhere cannot carry the token along.|
|» token|body|string|true|The access token, as pasted|

<h3 id="store-the-credential-for-a-git-repository-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|the credential was stored|Inline|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

## create forked workspace branch with git sync

<a id="opIdcreateWorkspaceForkGitBranch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/workspaces/create_workspace_fork_branch \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "id": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "color": "string",
    "forked_datatables": [
      {
        "name": "string",
        "new_dbname": "string",
        "fork_behavior": "schema_only"
      }
    ],
    "shared_ducklakes": [
      "string"
    ],
    "shared_storages": [
      "string"
    ],
    "is_dev_workspace": true,
    "lock_prod_deploy": true,
    "lock_prod_forking": true,
    "copy_members": true,
    "dev_workspace_label": "dev"
  }'
```

`POST /w/{workspace}/workspaces/create_workspace_fork_branch`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "id": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "color": "string",
  "forked_datatables": [
    {
      "name": "string",
      "new_dbname": "string",
      "fork_behavior": "schema_only"
    }
  ],
  "shared_ducklakes": [
    "string"
  ],
  "shared_storages": [
    "string"
  ],
  "is_dev_workspace": true,
  "lock_prod_deploy": true,
  "lock_prod_forking": true,
  "copy_members": true,
  "dev_workspace_label": "dev"
}
```

<h3 id="create-forked-workspace-branch-with-git-sync-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[CreateWorkspaceFork](#schemacreateworkspacefork)|true|new forked workspace|
|» id|body|string|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|none|
|» color|body|string|false|none|
|» forked_datatables|body|[object]|false|none|
|» » name|body|string|true|Datatable name|
|» » new_dbname|body|string|true|New database name for the fork|
|» » fork_behavior|body|string|false|What the fork request copies into `new_dbname`, which it creates — with the owners and grants of a data table under roles. This server refuses an entry without it; servers predating it expect `new_dbname` created and filled beforehand.|
|» shared_ducklakes|body|[string]|false|Lake names the fork SHARES with the parent (reads and writes the parent's lake directly). Every lake not listed gets the default isolated fork namespace with read-defer to the parent.|
|» shared_storages|body|[string]|false|Workspace storages the fork SHARES with the parent (`_default_` for the primary one): it reads and writes the parent's objects directly. Every storage not listed is isolated: the fork writes under its own prefix and reads through to the parent's objects.|
|» is_dev_workspace|body|boolean|false|Create the fork as a persistent dev workspace (id not required to carry the wm-fork- prefix; at most one per parent)|
|» lock_prod_deploy|body|boolean|false|When creating a dev workspace, lock the parent (prod) against direct deployment|
|» lock_prod_forking|body|boolean|false|When creating a dev workspace, prevent forking the parent (prod)|
|» copy_members|body|boolean|false|Copy the parent's members (users + group memberships) into the fork so the team can work in it|
|» dev_workspace_label|body|string|false|Environment label for the dev workspace: its badge text and the branch it deploys to. Ignored for non-dev forks. Omitted defaults to 'dev'|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » fork_behavior|schema_only|
|» » fork_behavior|schema_and_data|
|» dev_workspace_label|dev|
|» dev_workspace_label|qa|
|» dev_workspace_label|test|
|» dev_workspace_label|uat|
|» dev_workspace_label|staging|
|» dev_workspace_label|demo|
|» dev_workspace_label|sandbox|
|» dev_workspace_label|preprod|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
[
  "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
]
```

<h3 id="create-forked-workspace-branch-with-git-sync-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|forked workspace branch created|Inline|

<h3 id="create-forked-workspace-branch-with-git-sync-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **201**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[string(uuid)]|false|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

```bash
{
```

|» runs|body|boolean|true|Whether operators can view runs|
|» schedules|body|boolean|true|Whether operators can view schedules|
|» resources|body|boolean|true|Whether operators can view resources|
|» variables|body|boolean|true|Whether operators can view variables|
|» assets|body|boolean|true|Whether operators can view assets|
|» audit_logs|body|boolean|true|Whether operators can view audit logs|
|» triggers|body|boolean|true|Whether operators can view triggers|
|» groups|body|boolean|true|Whether operators can view groups page|
|» folders|body|boolean|true|Whether operators can view folders page|
|» workers|body|boolean|true|Whether operators can view workers page|
|» builder_flows|body|boolean|false|Whether operators can compose flows out of existing runnables (consumes a full seat). Omitting the field leaves the stored value unchanged.|
|» builder_apps|body|boolean|false|Whether operators can compose full-code apps out of existing runnables (consumes a full seat). Omitting the field leaves the stored value unchanged.|
|» manage_schedules|body|boolean|false|Whether operators can create, edit and delete schedules. Granted unless withdrawn; omitting the field leaves the stored value unchanged.|
|» manage_triggers|body|boolean|false|Whether operators can create, edit and delete triggers. Granted unless withdrawn; omitting the field leaves the stored value unchanged.|

## List the workspace's roles

<a id="opIdlistWorkspaceRoles"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/workspaces/roles \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /w/{workspace}/workspaces/roles`

The roles members of this workspace can hold, as they apply here (instance definition with the workspace's override applied, then workspace-only roles), the stored overrides, and the caller's own role and capabilities.

`POST /w/{workspace}/workspaces/role_overrides`

Replaces the workspace's overrides of instance roles, and its workspace-only roles (EE). Refuses removing a workspace-only role still held or referenced, and a change exceeding an offline license's seat cap. Requires workspace admin privileges.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "property1": {
    "label": "string",
    "capabilities": {
      "code": true,
      "flows": "none",
      "apps": "none",
      "manage_schedules": true,
      "manage_triggers": true,
      "fork": true,
      "visibility": {
        "property1": true,
        "property2": true
      }
    }
  },
  "property2": {
    "label": "string",
    "capabilities": {
      "code": true,
      "flows": "none",
      "apps": "none",
      "manage_schedules": true,
      "manage_triggers": true,
      "fork": true,
      "visibility": {
        "property1": true,
        "property2": true
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Compare two workspaces

<a id="opIdcompareWorkspaces"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/workspaces/compare/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /w/{workspace}/workspaces/compare/{target_workspace_id}`

Compares the current workspace with a target workspace to find differences in scripts, flows, apps, resources, and variables. Returns information about items that are ahead, behind, or in conflict.

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

## Seed the diff candidate set against an arbitrary workspace

<a id="opIdseedFullDiffScan"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/workspaces/seed_full_diff/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /w/{workspace}/workspaces/seed_full_diff/{target_workspace_id}`

Enumerates every item of both workspaces as an undecided diff candidate so `compareWorkspaces` can compare a pair the fork lineage does not track. Requires being an admin of both workspaces, and is rejected for a pair already linked by the lineage (whose diff is tallied continuously). The comparison itself is what compares the candidates, and is the expensive step.

<h3 id="seed-the-diff-candidate-set-against-an-arbitrary-workspace-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|target_workspace_id|path|string|true|The ID of the workspace to compare with|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "candidates": 0,
  "scanned_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

<h3 id="seed-the-diff-candidate-set-against-an-arbitrary-workspace-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Scan seeded|Inline|

<h3 id="seed-the-diff-candidate-set-against-an-arbitrary-workspace-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|candidates|integer|true|none|Number of candidate items the comparison will evaluate|
|scanned_at|string(date-time)|true|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

## get the workspace's deploy target on another instance, and the caller's connection to it

<a id="opIdgetRemoteDeployTarget"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/remote_deploy/target \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /w/{workspace}/remote_deploy/target`

Once connected, deploy calls aimed at the target go through
`/w/{workspace}/remote_deploy/proxy/{proxy_key}/{route}`, which forwards any method to
`{base_url}/api/w/{target workspace}/{route}` with the caller's stored token.


<h3 id="get-the-workspaces-deploy-target-on-another-instance-and-the-callers-connection-to-it-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "target": {
    "base_url": "string",
    "workspace_id": "string"
  },
  "connection": {
    "remote_email": "string",
    "proxy_key": "string",
    "connected_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="get-the-workspaces-deploy-target-on-another-instance-and-the-callers-connection-to-it-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|remote deploy target and the caller's connection to it|[RemoteDeployStatus](#schemaremotedeploystatus)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

## store the caller's own token for the remote deploy target

<a id="opIdconnectRemoteDeploy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/remote_deploy/connect \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "token": "string",
    "target": {
      "base_url": "string",
      "workspace_id": "string"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /w/{workspace}/remote_deploy/connect`

The token is checked against the target's whoami before it is stored. `target` names the
target the token was obtained for, and the request is refused if the workspace now points
elsewhere, so a token is never sent to an instance it was not meant for.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "token": "string",
  "target": {
    "base_url": "string",
    "workspace_id": "string"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="store-the-callers-own-token-for-the-remote-deploy-target-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» token|body|string|true|none|
|» target|body|[RemoteDeployTarget](#schemaremotedeploytarget)|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "remote_email": "string",
  "proxy_key": "string",
  "connected_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

<h3 id="store-the-callers-own-token-for-the-remote-deploy-target-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|the stored connection|[RemoteDeployConnection](#schemaremotedeployconnection)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/workspaces/edit_slack_command \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "slack_command_script": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /w/{workspace}/workspaces/edit_slack_command`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "slack_command_script": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="edit-slack-command-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|WorkspaceInvite|
|» slack_command_script|body|string|false|none|

<h3 id="edit-slack-command-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|status|Inline|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

## list available teams ids

<a id="opIdlistAvailableTeamsIds"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/workspaces/available_teams_ids \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /w/{workspace}/workspaces/available_teams_ids`

<h3 id="list-available-teams-ids-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|search|query|string|false|Search teams by name. If omitted, returns first page of all teams.|
|next_link|query|string|false|Pagination cursor URL from previous response. Pass this to fetch the next page of results.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "teams": [
    {
      "team_name": "string",
      "team_id": "string"
    }
  ],
  "total_count": 0,
  "per_page": 0,
  "next_link": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="list-available-teams-ids-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|status|Inline|

<h3 id="list-available-teams-ids-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|teams|[object]|false|none|none|
|» team_name|string|false|none|none|
|» team_id|string|false|none|none|
|total_count|integer|false|none|Total number of teams across all pages|
|per_page|integer|false|none|Number of teams per page (configurable via TEAMS_PER_PAGE env var)|
|next_link|string \| null|false|none|URL to fetch next page of results. Null if no more pages.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

|» free_tier|body|[FreeTierInfo](#schemafreetierinfo)|false|Read-only. Present when the workspace has no AI provider of its own and is running on Windmill's free tier. Ignored on write.|
|» model_pricing|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|[ModelPriceOverride](#schemamodelpriceoverride)|false|negotiated rates in USD per million tokens, keyed `provider:model`|
|» context_window_per_model|body|object|false|Context window in tokens per `provider:model`, overriding the built-in table the AI chat uses to decide when to compact its history.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|integer|false|none|
|» copilot_disabled|body|boolean|false|Hides the Windmill AI assistant (chat, sessions, code generation, completion, fixes) from the workspace UI. Read from the workspace's own settings even when the providers served fall back to the instance config. AI agent steps and the AI sandbox in flows are unaffected.|
|» sessions_storage_disabled|body|boolean|false|Stops browsers from backing their AI sessions up to the workspace's object storage. Read from the workspace's own settings like `copilot_disabled`.|
|» sessions_retention_days|body|integer|false|The server deletes the backup of a session no push has reached for this many days. Unset keeps backups until the user deletes the session. Read from the workspace's own settings like `copilot_disabled`.|

## apply a workspace settings document

<a id="opIdapplyWorkspaceSettingsDocument"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/workspaces/settings_document \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "document": {},
    "replace": true,
    "dry_run": true
  }'
```

`POST /w/{workspace}/workspaces/settings_document`

Applies a settings document, each setting through the endpoint that owns it. Admin only.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "document": {},
  "replace": true,
  "dry_run": true
}
```

<h3 id="apply-a-workspace-settings-document-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» document|body|object|true|The settings to apply, in the layout of the document. A secret given as `__SENSITIVE_AND_UNCHANGED__` keeps its stored value; one prefixed with `$encrypted:` is decrypted with the workspace key.|
|» replace|body|boolean|false|Clear the settings `wmill sync push` clears when settings.yaml omits them. Otherwise a setting the document omits is left as it is.|
|» dry_run|body|boolean|false|Only compute the changes, without applying them.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "changes": [
    {
      "key": "string",
      "before": null,
      "after": null
    }
  ],
  "applied": true,
  "warnings": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="apply-a-workspace-settings-document-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|the changes, applied unless dry_run|Inline|

<h3 id="apply-a-workspace-settings-document-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|changes|[object]|true|none|none|
|» key|string|true|none|none|
|» before|object|true|none|none|
|» after|object|true|none|none|
|applied|boolean|true|none|none|
|warnings|[string]|false|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

## choose whether new forks of this workspace start with its admins and developers

<a id="opIdeditAddAdminsAndDevelopersToForks"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/workspaces/edit_add_admins_and_developers_to_forks \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "add_admins_and_developers_to_forks": true
  }'
```

`POST /w/{workspace}/workspaces/edit_add_admins_and_developers_to_forks`

When on, every fork created from this workspace gets the workspace's admins and developers as members, with the role they hold here; operators, disabled users and service accounts are left out. The setting is copied into each fork, so forks of a fork follow it too. Off by default. Workspace-admin gated.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "add_admins_and_developers_to_forks": true
}
```

## set the key guest JWTs are verified against for this workspace

<a id="opIdeditGuestJwtKey"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/workspaces/edit_guest_jwt_key \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "public_key": "string",
    "jwks_url": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /w/{workspace}/workspaces/edit_guest_jwt_key`

A guest JWT (`jwt_guest_`) is minted by the embedding customer's own backend and verified against this key: a PEM public key (RS/ES family, HS* refused) or a JWKS URL, at most one. Both empty clears the workspace key; off cloud, verification then falls back to the instance issuer (`JWT_EXT_JWKS_URL`) if one is set, else no guest JWT is accepted. Workspace-admin gated. The key is validated before it is stored. Setting a key is refused with a 400 where guests are unavailable (the shared cloud); clearing one always works.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "public_key": "string",
  "jwks_url": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="set-the-key-guest-jwts-are-verified-against-for-this-workspace-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|The guest JWT verification key|
|» public_key|body|string|false|A PEM public key (RS or ES family).|
|» jwks_url|body|string|false|A JWKS URL whose keys are fetched and refreshed.|

<h3 id="set-the-key-guest-jwts-are-verified-against-for-this-workspace-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|status|Inline|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

```json
{
```
```json
  "name": "Production Protection",
  "rules": [
    "DisableDirectDeployment"
  ],
  "bypass_groups": [
    "string"
  ],
  "bypass_users": [
    "string"
  ],
  "fork_role_mapping": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-protection-rule-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|New protection rule configuration|
|» name|body|string|true|Unique name for the protection rule|
|» rules|body|[ProtectionRules](#schemaprotectionrules)|true|Configuration of protection restrictions|
|» bypass_groups|body|[RuleBypasserGroups](#schemarulebypassergroups)|true|Groups that can bypass this ruleset|
|» bypass_users|body|[RuleBypasserUsers](#schemarulebypasserusers)|true|Users that can bypass this ruleset|

Unmapped roles carry over unchanged; where two rulesets map the same role, the first by name wins. On update, omitting it leaves the stored mapping unchanged.|

|» rules|DisableWorkspaceForking|
|» rules|RestrictDeployToDeployers|
|» rules|RestrictAnonymousAppDeployment|

|» rules|RestrictGuestAppDeployment|
|» rules|RequireIsolatedForks|

## create a data table role on a Windmill-managed Postgres cluster

<a id="opIdcreateInstanceDatatableRole"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/settings/datatable_roles \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "cluster": "instance",
    "take_over": true
  }'
```

`POST /settings/datatable_roles`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "cluster": "instance",
  "take_over": true
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-data-table-role-on-a-windmill-managed-postgres-cluster-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|none|
|» cluster|body|[DatatableRoleCluster](#schemadatatablerolecluster)|false|The Windmill-managed Postgres cluster a data table role is a login on: Windmill's own (behind `instance` data tables) or the external instance cluster (behind `external_instance` ones). Defaults to `instance`.|
|» take_over|body|boolean|false|manage a Postgres role of that name that already exists on the cluster, replacing its password, instead of refusing it. A role with cluster-wide attributes or memberships is refused either way<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» cluster|instance|
|» cluster|external_instance|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "enabled": true,
  "cluster": "instance",
  "in_use": true
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-data-table-role-on-a-windmill-managed-postgres-cluster-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|the created role|[InstanceDatatableRole](#schemainstancedatatablerole)|
|409|Conflict|a Postgres role of that name already exists on the cluster and take_over was not set|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|seats_used|number|false|none|Author-equivalent seats consumed (authors + 0.5 × operators)|
|seats_cap|integer|false|none|none|
|author_count|integer|false|none|none|
|operator_count|integer|false|none|none|

## test secret backend connection (HashiCorp Vault)

<a id="opIdtestSecretBackend"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/settings/test_secret_backend \
  -X POST \

  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "address": "string",
    "mount_path": "string",
    "kv_secret_path_prefix": "string",
    "jwt_role": "string",
    "jwt_mount_path": "string",
    "approle_role_id": "string",
    "approle_mount_path": "string",
    "namespace": "string",
    "token": "string",
    "skip_ssl_verify": true
  }'
```

`POST /settings/test_secret_backend`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "address": "string",
  "mount_path": "string",
  "kv_secret_path_prefix": "string",
  "jwt_role": "string",
  "jwt_mount_path": "string",
  "approle_role_id": "string",
  "approle_mount_path": "string",
  "namespace": "string",
  "token": "string",
  "skip_ssl_verify": true
}
```

<h3 id="test-secret-backend-connection-hashicorp-vault-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[VaultSettings](#schemavaultsettings)|true|Vault settings to test|
|» address|body|string|true|HashiCorp Vault server address (e.g., https://vault.company.com:8200)|
|» mount_path|body|string|false|KV v2 secrets engine mount path (e.g., windmill). Empty to test the connection used for `$external:vault://` references, which checks only that Vault accepts Windmill's token.|
|» kv_secret_path_prefix|body|string|false|Optional path prefix inserted between the KV data/metadata segment and the workspace id (e.g., "apps/windmill"). When set, secrets are stored at `<mount>/data/<prefix>/<workspace>/<secret>`, allowing a Vault policy scoped to exactly `<mount>/data/<prefix>/*`.|
|» jwt_role|body|string|false|Vault JWT auth role name for Windmill (optional, if not provided token auth is used)|
|» jwt_mount_path|body|string|false|Mount path for the JWT auth method in Vault (optional, defaults to "jwt"). Set this when the JWT auth method is mounted at a non-default path, e.g. via `vault auth enable -path=<mount> jwt`.|
|» approle_role_id|body|string|false|AppRole role_id (optional). When set and no static token is given, Windmill logs in with AppRole; the secret_id is read from the `VAULT_APPROLE_SECRET_ID` environment variable of servers and workers.|
|» approle_mount_path|body|string|false|Mount path of the AppRole auth method (optional, defaults to "approle").|
|» namespace|body|string|false|Vault Enterprise namespace (optional)|
|» token|body|string|false|Static Vault token for testing/development (optional, if provided this is used instead of JWT authentication)|
|» skip_ssl_verify|body|boolean|false|Skip TLS certificate verification when connecting to Vault. Only use for self-signed certificates in development environments.|

<h3 id="test-secret-backend-connection-hashicorp-vault-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|connection successful|Inline|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

|» mount_path|body|string|false|KV v2 secrets engine mount path (e.g., windmill). Empty to test the connection used for `$external:vault://` references, which checks only that Vault accepts Windmill's token.|
|» kv_secret_path_prefix|body|string|false|Optional path prefix inserted between the KV data/metadata segment and the workspace id (e.g., "apps/windmill"). When set, secrets are stored at `<mount>/data/<prefix>/<workspace>/<secret>`, allowing a Vault policy scoped to exactly `<mount>/data/<prefix>/*`.|
|» jwt_role|body|string|false|Vault JWT auth role name for Windmill (optional, if not provided token auth is used)|
|» jwt_mount_path|body|string|false|Mount path for the JWT auth method in Vault (optional, defaults to "jwt"). Set this when the JWT auth method is mounted at a non-default path, e.g. via `vault auth enable -path=<mount> jwt`.|
|» approle_role_id|body|string|false|AppRole role_id (optional). When set and no static token is given, Windmill logs in with AppRole; the secret_id is read from the `VAULT_APPROLE_SECRET_ID` environment variable of servers and workers.|
|» approle_mount_path|body|string|false|Mount path of the AppRole auth method (optional, defaults to "approle").|
|» namespace|body|string|false|Vault Enterprise namespace (optional)|
|» token|body|string|false|Static Vault token for testing/development (optional, if provided this is used instead of JWT authentication)|
|» skip_ssl_verify|body|boolean|false|Skip TLS certificate verification when connecting to Vault. Only use for self-signed certificates in development environments.|

<h1 id="windmill-api-datametric">data_metric</h1>

## list declared measures and dimensions on DuckLake tables

<a id="opIdlistDataMetrics"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/data_metrics/list \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /w/{workspace}/data_metrics/list`

Call this before writing any aggregate query over a DuckLake table. A declared measure is the canonical definition of that number, and reproducing it yourself will silently disagree with it (a `revenue` measure typically excludes refunds or test rows). Filter by `table` for one table's declarations, or by `path_prefix` (e.g. `f/analytics`) for everything declared under a folder; omit both to browse the whole catalog. Results are keyset-paged: a full page may mean more remain, so continue with the `cursor_*` params rather than assuming a measure does not exist. Use each returned `expr` verbatim, and when a measure has a `filter` write it as `expr FILTER (WHERE filter)` so measures with different predicates can share one GROUP BY. If a number you need has no declared measure, write your own aggregate as usual. Results are limited to declarations whose producing script the caller can read.


<h3 id="list-declared-measures-and-dimensions-on-ducklake-tables-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|table|query|string|false|DuckLake table path, with or without the `ducklake://` scheme|
|path_prefix|query|string|false|Producing script path prefix, e.g. `f/analytics`|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Results per page, capped at 1000 (default 1000)|
|cursor_table|query|string|false|Keyset cursor. To page, pass the previous response's `next_cursor` fields back as `cursor_*`; all four move together, and are omitted for the first page. Continue whenever `next_cursor` is present. Every returned row is one the caller may read, so the cursor never names a hidden row.<br>|
|cursor_kind|query|string|false|none|
|cursor_name|query|string|false|none|
|cursor_script|query|string|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "metrics": [
    {
      "script_path": "string",
```

## create variable

<a id="opIdcreateVariable"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/variables/create \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "path": "string",
    "value": "string",
    "is_secret": true,
    "description": "string",
    "account": 0,
    "is_oauth": true,
    "expires_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "value_valid_until": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "labels": [
      "string"
    ],
    "ws_specific": true
  }'
```

`POST /w/{workspace}/variables/create`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "path": "string",
  "value": "string",
  "is_secret": true,
  "description": "string",
  "account": 0,
  "is_oauth": true,
  "expires_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "value_valid_until": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "labels": [
    "string"
  ],
  "ws_specific": true
}
```

<h3 id="create-variable-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|already_encrypted|query|boolean|false|whether the variable is already encrypted (default false)|
|body|body|[CreateVariable](#schemacreatevariable)|true|new variable|
|» path|body|string|true|The path to the variable|
|» value|body|string|true|The value of the variable. For a secret, `$external:vault://<path>#<key>` stores a reference to an existing secret in the instance's external HashiCorp Vault (path as `vault kv get` takes it) instead of a value; without `#<key>` it reads the whole secret as a JSON object of its fields. It is resolved on each read, only under the path prefixes a superadmin allowed for the workspace, and is returned as-is when the secret is not decrypted.<br>|
|» is_secret|body|boolean|true|Whether the variable is a secret|
|» description|body|string|true|The description of the variable|
|» account|body|integer|false|**Deprecated.** Ignored. A variable is linked to an OAuth account only when `createAccount` creates both.|
|» is_oauth|body|boolean|false|Whether the variable is an OAuth variable|
|» expires_at|body|string(date-time)|false|When to garbage-collect the variable. Used for ephemeral secrets; the variable is deleted once this is reached. Not the value's expiry — see value_valid_until.<br>|
|» value_valid_until|body|string(date-time)|false|When the value stored in this variable stops working. Triggers the workspace's variable expiration handler ahead of it, by the handler's `notify_before_secs` (1 day by default); never causes the variable to be deleted.<br>|
|» labels|body|[string]|false|none|
|» ws_specific|body|boolean|false|none|

<h3 id="create-variable-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|variable created|Inline|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

```json
      "string"
```
```bash
    ],
    "ws_specific": true
```
```json
  }
```
```json
}
```

<h3 id="create-oauth-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|code endpoint|
|» refresh_token|body|string|true|OAuth refresh token. For authorization_code flow, this contains the actual refresh token. For client_credentials flow, this must be set to an empty string.|
|» expires_in|body|integer|true|none|
|» client|body|string|true|none|
|» grant_type|body|string|false|none|
|» cc_client_id|body|string|false|OAuth client ID for resource-level credentials (client_credentials flow only)|
|» cc_client_secret|body|string|false|OAuth client secret for resource-level credentials (client_credentials flow only)|
|» cc_instance|body|string|false|Instance name for built-in providers whose client-credentials token URL is instance-templated; substituted into the fixed-host registry template server-side (client_credentials flow only). The token URL is never caller-supplied.|
|» cc_token_url|body|string|false|Bring-your-own token endpoint override (client_credentials flow only). Only honored together with cc_client_id/cc_client_secret and mutually exclusive with cc_instance; ignored/rejected on the shared-instance path.|
|» mcp_server_url|body|string|false|MCP server URL for MCP OAuth token refresh|
|» scopes|body|[string]|false|OAuth scopes to use for token refresh. Overrides instance-level scopes.|
|» variable|body|[CreateVariable](#schemacreatevariable)|false|The variable holding this account's access token. It is created with the account, in one transaction and with the same checks as createVariable, and linked to it so it refreshes through it.|

<h3 id="create-oauth-account-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|account set|Inline|

bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

```bash
  ],
```

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|path|string|true|none|none|
|description|string|false|none|none|
|resource_type|string|true|none|none|
|value|object|false|none|none|
|is_oauth|boolean|true|none|none|
|extra_perms|object|false|none|none|
|» **additionalProperties**|boolean|false|none|none|

|refresh_error|string|false|none|none|
|is_linked|boolean|true|none|none|
|is_refreshed|boolean|true|none|none|

|labels|[string]|false|none|none|
|inherited_labels|[string]|false|none|Labels inherited from the parent folder, computed at read time. Read-only — edit them on the folder.<br>|
|ws_specific|boolean|false|none|none|
|draft_only|boolean|false|none|True when this row is a per-user draft with no deployed<br>resource at the same path. Frontend renders a "Draft" badge.<br>|
|is_draft|boolean|true|none|True when the authed user has a per-user draft at this path<br>(over a deployed row or a synthesized draft-only row).<br>Frontend appends a `*` to the displayed name.<br>|
|agent_memory|object|false|none|For an `ai_agent` resource only, its `memory` setting: the one part<br>of the value a listing returns, since it decides whether the agent<br>keeps a conversation.<br>|
|draft_path|string|false|none|On a draft-only row, the path its editor has staged when it<br>differs from the storage path (e.g. a never-deployed item parked at<br>`u/{user}/draft_{uuid}`).<br>|
|is_draft|boolean|true|none|none|
|draft_saved_at|string(date-time)|false|none|none|
|draft_base|string|false|none|The deployed version the draft forked from, as text whatever the<br>kind (script hash, flow version id, app version id). Compare to the<br>deployed head to tell a draft that is behind. Absent when there is<br>no draft or it was never forked from a deploy.<br>|
|no_deployed|boolean|false|none|none|
|draft|object|false|none|none|
|other_drafts_users|[object]|false|none|Other workspace users (and the legacy NULL-email row, if any)<br>with a saved draft at the same path. Populated only on the<br>authed user's "get by path" responses for kinds the editor<br>surfaces a fork banner for (script, flow, app, raw_app).<br>Empty / omitted for kinds without that UI.<br>|
|» username|string \| null|false|none|Workspace username of the draft owner. `null` represents<br>the legacy workspace-level (NULL-email) row. Emails never<br>leave the server.<br>|
|» draft_saved_at|string(date-time)|true|none|When this user's draft was last saved (`draft.created_at`),<br>surfaced in the fork modal as "Last updated".<br>|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

<h3 id="get-hub-integration-metadata-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|app|string|true|none|none|
|display_name|string|true|none|none|
|description|string \| null|false|none|none|
|docs_url|string \| null|false|none|none|
|curated|boolean \| null|false|none|whether the script set was pruned to idiomatic actions rather than generated one per endpoint; null when nobody has assessed it, which is distinct from a stated false|
|metadata_source|string|false|none|whether the provider knowledge was authored (curated) or inferred from the shipped scripts (derived)|
|meta|object \| null|false|none|the integration's authored meta.json verbatim; the content repo owns its schema, so it is passed through unvalidated|
|meta_updated_at|string \| null|false|none|none|
|derived|object|false|none|facts computed from the integration's shipped scripts|
|» api_hosts|[object]|true|none|none|
|» » host|string|true|none|none|
|» » count|number|true|none|none|
|» style|string|true|none|none|
|» languages|object|true|none|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|number|false|none|none|
|» script_counts|object|true|none|none|
|» » total|number|true|none|none|
|» » by_kind|object|true|none|none|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|number|false|none|none|
|» top_scripts|[object]|true|none|none|
|» » path|string|true|none|none|
|» » ask_id|number|false|none|none|
|» » version_id|number|false|none|none|
|» » summary|string|true|none|none|
|» » description|string \| null|false|none|none|
|» » kind|string|true|none|none|
|» » language|string \| null|false|none|none|
|» » views|number|false|none|none|
|» » votes|number|false|none|none|
|resource_types|[object]|false|none|none|
|» id|number|false|none|none|
|» name|string|true|none|none|
|» description|string \| null|false|none|none|
|» schema|object|true|none|the resource type's JSON schema; the hub stores it as text and returns it as a JSON string, so a client must be ready for either that or an object|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|metadata_source|curated|
|metadata_source|derived|
|» style|fetch|
|» style|sdk|
|» style|mixed|
|» style|unknown|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/flows/list \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /w/{workspace}/flows/list`

<h3 id="list-all-flows-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|page|query|integer|false|which page to return (start at 1, default 1)|
|per_page|query|integer|false|number of items to return for a given page (default 30, max 100)|
|order_desc|query|boolean|false|order by desc order (default true)|
|created_by|query|string|false|filter by exact matching user creator. Supports comma-separated list (e.g. 'alice,bob') and negation by prefixing all values with '!' (e.g. '!alice,!bob')|
|path_start|query|string|false|mask to filter matching starting path|
|path_exact|query|string|false|mask to filter exact matching path|
|show_archived|query|boolean|false|(default false)<br>show only the archived files.<br>when multiple archived hash share the same path, only the ones with the latest create_at<br>are displayed.<br>|
|starred_only|query|boolean|false|(default false)<br>show only the starred items<br>|
|include_draft_only|query|boolean|false|(default false)<br>include items that have no deployed version<br>|
|with_deployment_msg|query|boolean|false|(default false)<br>include deployment message<br>|
|without_description|query|boolean|false|(default false)<br>If true, the description field will be omitted from the response.<br>|
|dedicated_worker|query|boolean|false|(default regardless)<br>If true, show only flows with dedicated_worker enabled.<br>If false, show only flows with dedicated_worker disabled.<br>|
|label|query|string|false|Filter by label|

```json
          "id": "string",

          },

            "skip_if_stopped": true,
            "expr": "string",
            "error_message": "string",
            "error_include_result": true
          },
          "skip_if": {
            "expr": "string"
          },
          "sleep": {
            "value": null,
            "type": "static"
          },
          "cache_ttl": 0,
          "cache_ignore_s3_path": true,
          "timeout": {
            "value": null,
            "type": "static"
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|All flow|Inline|

<h3 id="list-all-flows-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[object]|false|none|none|
|» summary|string|true|none|Short description of what this flow does|
|» description|string|false|none|Detailed documentation for this flow|
|» value|[FlowValue](#schemaflowvalue)|true|none|The flow structure containing modules and optional preprocessor/failure handlers|
|» schema|object|false|none|JSON Schema for flow inputs. Use this to define input parameters, their types, defaults, and validation. For resource inputs, set type to 'object' and format to 'resource-<type>' (e.g., 'resource-stripe')|
|» on_behalf_of_email|string|false|none|Address of the account the flow runs on behalf of. Derived from on_behalf_of on read; accepted on write, where it is resolved to the account it names.|
|» on_behalf_of|string|false|none|The flow runs with the permissions of this identity: u/{username}, g/{group}, or a bare email when the username is itself email-shaped. The only stored half of the identity; on_behalf_of_email is derived from it. Omit it when writing and it is resolved from that address instead.|
|» workspace_id|string|false|none|none|
|» path|string|true|none|none|
|» edited_by|string|true|none|none|
|» edited_at|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|» archived|boolean|true|none|none|
|» extra_perms|[ExtraPerms](#schemaextraperms)|true|none|none|
|» starred|boolean|false|none|none|
|» draft_only|boolean|false|none|none|
|» tag|string|false|none|none|
|» ws_error_handler_muted|boolean|false|none|none|
|» priority|integer|false|none|none|
|» dedicated_worker|boolean|false|none|none|
|» timeout|number|false|none|none|
|» visible_to_runner_only|boolean|false|none|none|
|» on_behalf_of_email|string|false|none|none|
|» on_behalf_of|string|false|none|Authorization identity the runnable runs as: u/{username}, g/{group}, or a bare email when the username is itself email-shaped. The only stored half of the identity; on_behalf_of_email is derived from it.|
|» labels|[string]|false|none|none|
|» job_token_scopes|[string]|false|none|Scopes the token of every job of this runnable is restricted to (domain:action[:resource], e.g. oidc:write). Jobs it starts, flow steps and AI agent tools inherit the restriction. Unset, the job token carries the full permissions of the identity the job runs as; an empty list leaves it no API access beyond its own job.|
|» inherited_labels|[string]|false|none|Labels inherited from the parent folder, computed at read time. Read-only — edit them on the folder.<br>|
|» lock_error_logs|string|false|none|none|
|» version_id|number|false|none|none|
|» draft_only|boolean|false|none|none|
|» chat_input_enabled|boolean|false|none|`chat_input_enabled` of the flow's value,<br>projected so the list can mark flows that open<br>as a chat. Omitted when the value has no such<br>field.<br>|
|» is_draft|boolean|false|none|True when the authed user has a draft for this<br>flow — either no deployed row exists at this<br>path (draft-only) or the user saved a per-user<br>draft on top of the deployed row.<br>|
|» draft_path|string|false|none|User-typed path the editor has staged but not<br>yet deployed. Sourced from the draft JSON's<br>`draft_path` field (the editor only writes it<br>when the typed path differs from the deployed<br>one). Lets the home list render the meaningful<br>name instead of the autogenerated<br>`u/{user}/draft_{uuid}` URL path. Omitted when<br>unchanged.<br>|
|» draft_users|[object]|false|none|Workspace users (including the authed user, and<br>the legacy NULL-email row if any) who have a<br>per-user draft at this path. Drives the home<br>page's user-avatar circles inside the Draft<br>badge. Omitted when no drafts exist.<br>|
|» » username|string \| null|false|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

## get flow history by path

<a id="opIdgetFlowHistory"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/flows/history/p/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /w/{workspace}/flows/history/p/{path}`

<h3 id="get-flow-history-by-path-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|path|path|string|true|none|
|page|query|integer|false|which page to return (start at 1, default 1)|
|per_page|query|integer|false|number of items to return for a given page (default 30, max 100)|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "id": 0,
    "created_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "deployment_msg": "string",
    "created_by": "string"
  }
]
```

<h3 id="get-flow-history-by-path-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Flow history|Inline|

<h3 id="get-flow-history-by-path-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[[FlowVersion](#schemaflowversion)]|false|none|none|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|flow details|Inline|

<h3 id="get-flow-by-path-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|summary|string|true|none|Short description of what this flow does|
|description|string|false|none|Detailed documentation for this flow|
|value|[FlowValue](#schemaflowvalue)|true|none|The flow structure containing modules and optional preprocessor/failure handlers|
|schema|object|false|none|JSON Schema for flow inputs. Use this to define input parameters, their types, defaults, and validation. For resource inputs, set type to 'object' and format to 'resource-<type>' (e.g., 'resource-stripe')|
|on_behalf_of_email|string|false|none|Address of the account the flow runs on behalf of. Derived from on_behalf_of on read; accepted on write, where it is resolved to the account it names.|
|on_behalf_of|string|false|none|The flow runs with the permissions of this identity: u/{username}, g/{group}, or a bare email when the username is itself email-shaped. The only stored half of the identity; on_behalf_of_email is derived from it. Omit it when writing and it is resolved from that address instead.|
|workspace_id|string|false|none|none|
|path|string|true|none|none|
|edited_by|string|true|none|none|
|edited_at|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|archived|boolean|true|none|none|
|extra_perms|[ExtraPerms](#schemaextraperms)|true|none|none|
|starred|boolean|false|none|none|
|draft_only|boolean|false|none|none|
|tag|string|false|none|none|
|ws_error_handler_muted|boolean|false|none|none|
|priority|integer|false|none|none|
|dedicated_worker|boolean|false|none|none|
|timeout|number|false|none|none|
|visible_to_runner_only|boolean|false|none|none|
|on_behalf_of_email|string|false|none|none|
|on_behalf_of|string|false|none|Authorization identity the runnable runs as: u/{username}, g/{group}, or a bare email when the username is itself email-shaped. The only stored half of the identity; on_behalf_of_email is derived from it.|
|labels|[string]|false|none|none|
|job_token_scopes|[string]|false|none|Scopes the token of every job of this runnable is restricted to (domain:action[:resource], e.g. oidc:write). Jobs it starts, flow steps and AI agent tools inherit the restriction. Unset, the job token carries the full permissions of the identity the job runs as; an empty list leaves it no API access beyond its own job.|
|inherited_labels|[string]|false|none|Labels inherited from the parent folder, computed at read time. Read-only — edit them on the folder.<br>|
|lock_error_logs|string|false|none|none|
|version_id|number|false|none|none|
|is_draft|boolean|true|none|none|
|draft_saved_at|string(date-time)|false|none|none|
|draft_base|string|false|none|The deployed version the draft forked from, as text whatever the<br>kind (script hash, flow version id, app version id). Compare to the<br>deployed head to tell a draft that is behind. Absent when there is<br>no draft or it was never forked from a deploy.<br>|
|no_deployed|boolean|false|none|none|
|draft|object|false|none|none|
|other_drafts_users|[object]|false|none|Other workspace users (and the legacy NULL-email row, if any)<br>with a saved draft at the same path. Populated only on the<br>authed user's "get by path" responses for kinds the editor<br>surfaces a fork banner for (script, flow, app, raw_app).<br>Empty / omitted for kinds without that UI.<br>|
|» username|string \| null|false|none|Workspace username of the draft owner. `null` represents<br>the legacy workspace-level (NULL-email) row. Emails never<br>leave the server.<br>|
|» draft_saved_at|string(date-time)|true|none|When this user's draft was last saved (`draft.created_at`),<br>surfaced in the fork modal as "Last updated".<br>|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

<h3 id="create-flow-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|Partially filled flow|
|» summary|body|string|true|Short description of what this flow does|
|» description|body|string|false|Detailed documentation for this flow|
|» value|body|[FlowValue](#schemaflowvalue)|true|The flow structure containing modules and optional preprocessor/failure handlers|
|» schema|body|object|false|JSON Schema for flow inputs. Use this to define input parameters, their types, defaults, and validation. For resource inputs, set type to 'object' and format to 'resource-<type>' (e.g., 'resource-stripe')|
|» on_behalf_of_email|body|string|false|Address of the account the flow runs on behalf of. Derived from on_behalf_of on read; accepted on write, where it is resolved to the account it names.|
|» on_behalf_of|body|string|false|The flow runs with the permissions of this identity: u/{username}, g/{group}, or a bare email when the username is itself email-shaped. The only stored half of the identity; on_behalf_of_email is derived from it. Omit it when writing and it is resolved from that address instead.|
|» path|body|string|true|none|
|» tag|body|string|false|none|
|» ws_error_handler_muted|body|boolean|false|none|
|» priority|body|integer|false|none|
|» dedicated_worker|body|boolean|false|none|
|» timeout|body|number|false|none|
|» visible_to_runner_only|body|boolean|false|none|
|» on_behalf_of_email|body|string|false|none|
|» on_behalf_of|body|string|false|Authorization identity to run as: u/{username}, g/{group}, or a bare email when the username is itself email-shaped. Supply this or on_behalf_of_email; when only the address is given it is resolved to the account it names, and an address naming nobody is rejected. A pair that disagrees is rejected.|
|» preserve_on_behalf_of|body|boolean|false|When true and the caller is a member of the 'wm_deployers' group, preserves the original on_behalf_of_email / on_behalf_of pair instead of overwriting it with the caller's own identity.|
|» labels|body|[string]|false|none|
|» job_token_scopes|body|[string]|false|Scopes the token of every job of this runnable is restricted to (domain:action[:resource], e.g. oidc:write). Jobs it starts, flow steps and AI agent tools inherit the restriction. Unset, the job token carries the full permissions of the identity the job runs as; an empty list leaves it no API access beyond its own job. Omitting the field keeps the deployed value; null clears it.|
|» deployment_message|body|string|false|none|
|» skip_draft_deletion|body|boolean|false|When true (set by the CLI / git sync), deploying this flow does not delete an existing user draft at the same path.|

<h3 id="create-flow-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|flow created|Inline|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

<h3 id="update-flow-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|path|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|Partially filled flow|
|» summary|body|string|true|Short description of what this flow does|
|» description|body|string|false|Detailed documentation for this flow|
|» value|body|[FlowValue](#schemaflowvalue)|true|The flow structure containing modules and optional preprocessor/failure handlers|
|» schema|body|object|false|JSON Schema for flow inputs. Use this to define input parameters, their types, defaults, and validation. For resource inputs, set type to 'object' and format to 'resource-<type>' (e.g., 'resource-stripe')|
|» on_behalf_of_email|body|string|false|Address of the account the flow runs on behalf of. Derived from on_behalf_of on read; accepted on write, where it is resolved to the account it names.|
|» on_behalf_of|body|string|false|The flow runs with the permissions of this identity: u/{username}, g/{group}, or a bare email when the username is itself email-shaped. The only stored half of the identity; on_behalf_of_email is derived from it. Omit it when writing and it is resolved from that address instead.|
|» path|body|string|false|none|
|» tag|body|string|false|none|
|» ws_error_handler_muted|body|boolean|false|none|
|» priority|body|integer|false|none|
|» dedicated_worker|body|boolean|false|none|
|» timeout|body|number|false|none|
|» visible_to_runner_only|body|boolean|false|none|
|» on_behalf_of_email|body|string|false|none|
|» on_behalf_of|body|string|false|Authorization identity to run as: u/{username}, g/{group}, or a bare email when the username is itself email-shaped. Supply this or on_behalf_of_email; when only the address is given it is resolved to the account it names, and an address naming nobody is rejected. A pair that disagrees is rejected.|
|» preserve_on_behalf_of|body|boolean|false|When true and the caller is a member of the 'wm_deployers' group, preserves the original on_behalf_of_email / on_behalf_of pair instead of overwriting it with the caller's own identity.|
|» labels|body|[string]|false|none|
|» job_token_scopes|body|[string]|false|Scopes the token of every job of this runnable is restricted to (domain:action[:resource], e.g. oidc:write). Jobs it starts, flow steps and AI agent tools inherit the restriction. Unset, the job token carries the full permissions of the identity the job runs as; an empty list leaves it no API access beyond its own job. Omitting the field keeps the deployed value; null clears it.|
|» deployment_message|body|string|false|none|
|» skip_draft_deletion|body|boolean|false|When true (set by the CLI / git sync), deploying this flow does not delete an existing user draft at the same path.|

<h3 id="update-flow-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|flow updated|Inline|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

## whether the app behind a custom path admits guests

<a id="opIdgetGuestEntryByCustomPath"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/apps_u/guest_entry_by_custom_path/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /apps_u/guest_entry_by_custom_path/{custom_path}`

The custom-path counterpart of `getGuestEntry`. Unauthenticated; 404 unless the app's execution mode is `guest`, and never on a deployment where guests are unavailable (the shared cloud). Returns the workspace too, since a custom URL may not carry it.

<h3 id="whether-the-app-behind-a-custom-path-admits-guests-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|custom_path|path|string|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "workspace_id": "string",
  "app_path": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="whether-the-app-behind-a-custom-path-admits-guests-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|the app is open to guests|[GuestEntry](#schemaguestentry)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

## whether the app behind a share secret admits guests

<a id="opIdgetGuestEntry"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/apps_u/guest_entry/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /w/{workspace}/apps_u/guest_entry/{path}`

Unauthenticated: what a signed-out visitor reads to learn that signing in would let them in. 404 unless the app's execution mode is `guest`, and never on a deployment where guests are unavailable (the shared cloud), so it says nothing about apps that are not open to guests. Discloses only the app path, to a caller already holding the share secret.

```json
  "app_path": "string"
}
```

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|the app is open to guests|[GuestEntry](#schemaguestentry)|
