<h3 id="update-app-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|path|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|update app|
|» path|body|string|false|none|
|» summary|body|string|false|none|
|» value|body|object|false|none|
|» policy|body|[Policy](#schemapolicy)|false|none|
|» execution_mode|body|string|false|Changes who may open the app and leaves the rest of the deployed policy, its run-as user included, as it is. Applied under the same lock as a deploy, so neither overwrites the other. Cannot be sent with `policy`, which states its own mode. When the app runs as another user, refused to a caller who is neither an admin nor in 'wm_deployers', and to an operator with builder rights even in 'wm_deployers'; they change the mode by deploying.|
|» deployment_message|body|string|false|none|
|» custom_path|body|string|false|none|
|» preserve_on_behalf_of|body|boolean|false|When true and the caller is a member of the 'wm_deployers' group, preserves the original on_behalf_of value in the policy instead of overwriting it.|
|» labels|body|[string]|false|none|
|» skip_draft_deletion|body|boolean|false|When true (set by the CLI / git sync), deploying this app does not delete an existing user draft at the same path.|
|» allow_kind_change|body|boolean|false|When true, this deploy may switch the app between low-code and raw. Without it, deploying a value to an app of the other kind is refused so an app is never converted by accident.|

|Parameter|Value|

|» execution_mode|viewer|
|» execution_mode|publisher|
|» execution_mode|guest|
|» execution_mode|anonymous|

```json
}
```

## list all scripts

<a id="opIdlistScripts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/scripts/list \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /w/{workspace}/scripts/list`

<h3 id="list-all-scripts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|page|query|integer|false|which page to return (start at 1, default 1)|
|per_page|query|integer|false|number of items to return for a given page (default 30, max 100)|
|order_desc|query|boolean|false|order by desc order (default true)|
|created_by|query|string|false|filter by exact matching user creator. Supports comma-separated list (e.g. 'alice,bob') and negation by prefixing all values with '!' (e.g. '!alice,!bob')|
|path_start|query|string|false|mask to filter matching starting path|
|path_exact|query|string|false|mask to filter exact matching path|
|first_parent_hash|query|string|false|mask to filter scripts whom first direct parent has exact hash|
|last_parent_hash|query|string|false|mask to filter scripts whom last parent in the chain has exact hash.<br>Beware that each script stores only a limited number of parents. Hence<br>the last parent hash for a script is not necessarily its top-most parent.<br>To find the top-most parent you will have to jump from last to last hash<br> until finding the parent<br>|
|parent_hash|query|string|false|is the hash present in the array of stored parent hashes for this script.<br>The same warning applies than for last_parent_hash. A script only store a<br>limited number of direct parent<br>|
|show_archived|query|boolean|false|(default false)<br>show only the archived files.<br>when multiple archived hash share the same path, only the ones with the latest create_at<br>are<br>ed.<br>|
|include_without_main|query|boolean|false|(default false)<br>include scripts without an exported main function<br>|
|include_draft_only|query|boolean|false|(default false)<br>include scripts that have no deployed version<br>|
|is_template|query|boolean|false|(default regardless)<br>if true show only the templates<br>if false show only the non templates<br>if not defined, show all regardless of if the script is a template<br>|
|kinds|query|string|false|(default regardless)<br>script kinds to filter, split by comma<br>|
|starred_only|query|boolean|false|(default false)<br>show only the starred items<br>|
|with_deployment_msg|query|boolean|false|(default false)<br>include deployment message<br>|
|languages|query|string|false|Filter to only include scripts written in the given languages.<br>Accepts multiple values as a comma-separated list.<br>|
|without_description|query|boolean|false|(default false)<br>If true, the description field will be omitted from the response.<br>|
|dedicated_worker|query|boolean|false|(default regardless)<br>If true, show only scripts with dedicated_worker enabled.<br>If false, show only scripts with dedicated_worker disabled.<br>|
|label|query|string|false|Filter by label|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "workspace_id": "string",
    "hash": "string",
    "path": "string",
    "parent_hashes": [
      "string"
    ],
    "summary": "string",
    "description": "string",
    "content": "string",
    "created_by": "string",
    "created_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "archived": true,
    "schema": {},
    "deleted": true,
    "is_template": true,
    "extra_perms": {
      "property1": true,
      "property2": true
    },
    "lock": "string",
    "lock_error_logs": "string",
    "language": "python3",
    "kind": "script",
    "starred": true,
    "tag": "string",
    "draft_only": true,
    "envs": [
      "string"
    ],
    "concurrent_limit": 0,
    "concurrency_time_window_s": 0,
    "concurrency_key": "string",
    "debounce_key": "string",
    "debounce_delay_s": 0,
    "debounce_args_to_accumulate": [
      "string"
    ],
    "max_total_debouncing_time": 0,
    "max_total_debounces_amount": 0,
    "cache_ttl": 0,
    "cache_ignore_s3_path": true,
    "dedicated_worker": true,
    "ws_error_handler_muted": true,
    "priority": 0,
    "restart_unless_cancelled": true,
    "timeout": 0,
    "delete_after_secs": 0,
    "visible_to_runner_only": true,
    "auto_kind": "string",
    "codebase": "string",
    "has_preprocessor": true,
    "on_behalf_of_email": "string",
    "on_behalf_of": "string",
    "modules": {
      "property1": {
        "content": "string",
        "language": "python3",
        "lock": "string"
      },
      "property2": {
        "content": "string",
        "language": "python3",
        "lock": "string"
      }
    },
    "labels": [],
    "job_token_scopes": [
      "string"
    ],
    "inherited_labels": [
      "string"
    ],
    "is_draft": true,
    "draft_path": "string",
    "draft_users": [
      {
        "username": "string"
      }
    ]
  }
]
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|All scripts|Inline|

<h3 id="list-all-scripts-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[object]|false|none|none|
|» workspace_id|string|false|none|none|
|» hash|string|true|none|none|
|» path|string|true|none|none|
|» parent_hashes|[string]|false|none|The first element is the direct parent of the script, the second is the parent of the first, etc<br>|
|» summary|string|true|none|none|
|» description|string|true|none|none|
|» content|string|true|none|none|
|» created_by|string|true|none|none|
|» created_at|string(date-time)|true|none|none|

|» lock|string|false|none|none|
|» lock_error_logs|string|false|none|none|
|» language|[ScriptLang](#schemascriptlang)|true|none|none|
|» kind|string|true|none|none|
|» starred|boolean|true|none|none|
|» tag|string|false|none|none|
|» draft_only|boolean|false|none|none|
|» envs|[string]|false|none|none|
|» concurrent_limit|integer|false|none|none|
|» concurrency_time_window_s|integer|false|none|none|
|» concurrency_key|string|false|none|none|
|» debounce_key|string|false|none|none|
|» debounce_delay_s|integer|false|none|none|
|» debounce_args_to_accumulate|[string]|false|none|none|
|» max_total_debouncing_time|integer|false|none|none|
|» max_total_debounces_amount|integer|false|none|none|
|» cache_ttl|number|false|none|none|
|» cache_ignore_s3_path|boolean|false|none|none|
|» dedicated_worker|boolean|false|none|none|
|» ws_error_handler_muted|boolean|false|none|none|
|» priority|integer|false|none|none|
|» restart_unless_cancelled|boolean|false|none|none|
|» timeout|integer|false|none|none|
|» delete_after_secs|integer|false|none|If set, delete the job's args, result and logs after this many seconds following job completion|
|» visible_to_runner_only|boolean|false|none|none|
|» auto_kind|string|false|none|none|
|» codebase|string|false|none|none|
|» has_preprocessor|boolean|true|none|none|
|» on_behalf_of_email|string|false|none|none|
|» on_behalf_of|string|false|none|Authorization identity the runnable runs as: u/{username}, g/{group}, or a bare email when the username is itself email-shaped. The only stored half of the identity; on_behalf_of_email is derived from it.|
|» modules|object \| null|false|none|Additional script modules keyed by relative file path|
|» » **additionalProperties**|[ScriptModule](#schemascriptmodule)|false|none|An additional module file associated with a script|
|» labels|[string]|false|none|none|
|» job_token_scopes|[string]|false|none|Scopes the token of every job of this runnable is restricted to (domain:action[:resource], e.g. oidc:write). Jobs it starts, flow steps and AI agent tools inherit the restriction. Unset, the job token carries the full permissions of the identity the job runs as; an empty list leaves it no API access beyond its own job.|
|» inherited_labels|[string]|false|none|Labels inherited from the parent folder, computed at read time. Read-only — edit them on the folder.<br>|
|» is_draft|boolean|false|none|True when the authed user has a draft for this<br>script — either no deployed row exists at this<br>path (draft-only) or the user saved a per-user<br>draft on top of the deployed row.<br>|
|» draft_path|string|false|none|User-typed path the editor has staged but not<br>yet deployed. Surfaced for draft-only rows so<br>the home list can render the meaningful name<br>instead of the autogenerated<br>`u/{user}/draft_{uuid}` URL path. Omitted<br>when unchanged.<br>|
|» draft_users|[object]|false|none|Workspace users (including the authed user, and<br>the legacy NULL-email row if any) who have a<br>per-user draft at this path. Drives the home<br>page's user-avatar circles inside the Draft<br>badge. Omitted when no drafts exist.<br>|
|» » username|string \| null|false|none|none|

`POST /w/{workspace}/scripts/create`

Creates a new script at a path that does not already hold one.
Supplying `parent_hash` instead deploys a new version of the script that hash names, and a `path` differing from that version's moves the script there. `POST /w/{workspace}/scripts/update/{path}` does the same, naming the superseded version in its URL.


> Body parameter

```json
  "path": "string",
  "parent_hash": "string",
  "auto_parent": true,
  "summary": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "content": "string",
  "schema": {},
  "is_template": true,
  "lock": "string",
  "language": "python3",
  "kind": "script",
  "tag": "string",
  "envs": [
    "string"
  ],
  "concurrent_limit": 0,
  "concurrency_time_window_s": 0,
  "cache_ttl": 0,
  "cache_ignore_s3_path": true,
  "dedicated_worker": true,
  "ws_error_handler_muted": true,
  "priority": 0,
  "restart_unless_cancelled": true,
  "timeout": 0,
  "delete_after_secs": 0,
  "deployment_message": "string",
  "concurrency_key": "string",
  "debounce_key": "string",
  "debounce_delay_s": 0,
  "debounce_args_to_accumulate": [
    "string"
  ],
  "max_total_debouncing_time": 0,
  "max_total_debounces_amount": 0,
  "visible_to_runner_only": true,

      "content": "string",

      "lock": "string"

      "lock": "string"
    }

  ],

}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[NewScript](#schemanewscript)|true|Partially filled script|
|» path|body|string|true|none|
|» parent_hash|body|string|false|The hash of the version this one supersedes: deploying with it archives that version and chains the new one onto its history, and a `path` differing from the superseded version's moves the script there.|
|» auto_parent|body|boolean|false|When true, the backend resolves the parent to the current deployed head for this path within the transaction (ignoring parent_hash), instead of failing with a "lineage must be linear" error when the supplied parent_hash is stale.|
|» summary|body|string|true|none|
|» description|body|string|false|none|
|» content|body|string|true|none|
|» schema|body|object|false|JSON Schema of the arguments of `main`, which is what a run form and an MCP tool offer. Omitted (or `{}`), it is inferred from `content` for TypeScript, Python, Go, Bash, PowerShell, SQL, GraphQL and Ansible scripts. For other languages, or code that does not parse, a new script gets none. A new version of an existing script also keeps what the previous version's schema says about each argument, or that whole schema when nothing can be inferred. A dbt script always takes its schema from its descriptor, whatever is sent.|
|» is_template|body|boolean|false|none|

|» has_preprocessor|body|boolean|false|none|

|» on_behalf_of|body|string|false|Authorization identity to run as: u/{username}, g/{group}, or a bare email when the username is itself email-shaped. Supply this or on_behalf_of_email; when only the address is given it is resolved to the account it names, and an address naming nobody is rejected. A pair that disagrees is rejected.|
|» preserve_on_behalf_of|body|boolean|false|When true and the caller is a member of the 'wm_deployers' group, preserves the original on_behalf_of_email / on_behalf_of pair instead of overwriting it with the caller's own identity.|
|» assets|body|[object]|false|none|
|» » path|body|string|true|none|
|» » kind|body|[AssetKind](#schemaassetkind)|true|none|
|» » access_type|body|string|false|none|
|» » alt_access_type|body|string|false|none|

|» » **additionalProperties**|body|[ScriptModule](#schemascriptmodule)|false|An additional module file associated with a script|

|» job_token_scopes|body|[string]|false|Scopes the token of every job of this runnable is restricted to (domain:action[:resource], e.g. oidc:write). Jobs it starts, flow steps and AI agent tools inherit the restriction. Unset, the job token carries the full permissions of the identity the job runs as; an empty list leaves it no API access beyond its own job. Omitting the field keeps the deployed value; null clears it.|

`POST /w/{workspace}/scripts/update/{path}`

Deploys a new version of the script at `path`, which must already hold one.
The body's `path` is the destination: the same path leaves the script where it
is, a different one moves it there and archives the old path.

## check a script's asset references against captured producer schemas

<a id="opIdcheckSchemaContracts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/scripts/check_schema_contracts \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "language": "python3",
    "content": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /w/{workspace}/scripts/check_schema_contracts`

Save-time schema-contract check for data pipelines: validates the given
script content's asset references (body column reads, `// column` lineage,
`// data_test relationships`) against the latest captured producer schemas
and returns warnings. Warnings never block a save/deploy; an asset whose
producer declares `on_schema_change=ignore` is suppressed to a single
informational entry.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "language": "python3",
  "content": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="check-a-scripts-asset-references-against-captured-producer-schemas-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» language|body|[ScriptLang](#schemascriptlang)|true|none|
|» content|body|string|true|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» language|python3|
|» language|deno|
|» language|go|
|» language|bash|
|» language|powershell|
|» language|postgresql|
|» language|mysql|
|» language|bigquery|
|» language|snowflake|
|» language|mssql|
|» language|oracledb|
|» language|graphql|
|» language|nativets|
|» language|bun|
|» language|php|
|» language|rust|
|» language|ansible|
|» language|csharp|
|» language|nu|
|» language|java|
|» language|ruby|
|» language|rlang|
|» language|duckdb|
|» language|bunnative|
|» language|dbt|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "warnings": [
    {
      "kind": "missing_column",
      "asset_path": "string",
      "column": "string",
      "expected_type": "string",
      "found_type": "string",
      "schema_version": 0,
      "captured_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "message": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="check-a-scripts-asset-references-against-captured-producer-schemas-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|contract warnings (empty when all references match)|Inline|

<h3 id="check-a-scripts-asset-references-against-captured-producer-schemas-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|warnings|[[ContractWarning](#schemacontractwarning)]|true|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

## list runnables (scripts, flows, apps, agents) merged, ordered and keyset-paginated

<a id="opIdlistRunnables"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/runnables/list \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /w/{workspace}/runnables/list`

<h3 id="list-runnables-scripts-flows-apps-agents-merged-ordered-and-keyset-paginated-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|order_by|query|string|false|sort key: 'updated' (default) or 'name'|
|order_desc|query|boolean|false|order by desc order (default true)|
|kinds|query|string|false|comma-separated subset of script,flow,app,agent (default all)|
|show_archived|query|boolean|false|none|
|include_without_main|query|boolean|false|include library scripts (no runnable main)|
|path_start|query|string|false|restrict to paths under this prefix|
|label|query|string|false|none|
|search|query|string|false|case-insensitive fuzzy match on "summary (path)": the query is split into terms on runs of anything but ASCII letters, digits and apostrophes, and each of the first 8 must appear whole and in order, with anything in between. Terms past the 8th are ignored, so an over-long query matches more rows rather than fewer. Omitted or empty filters nothing; a query holding no ASCII-alphanumeric character at all (a lone space, "_", or text in a non-Latin script) yields no terms and matches nothing, mirroring the homepage, whose matcher discards those queries too.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|number of items to return for a given page (default 30, max 100)|
|cursor|query|string|false|opaque keyset cursor from a previous page's next_cursor|
|include_draft_only|query|boolean|false|also list the caller's drafts at paths with no deployed row, sorted and paginated with the deployed ones. Ignored for operators, in the archived view, and under a label filter (a draft carries no labels).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|order_by|updated|
|order_by|name|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "type": "script",
      "path": "string",
      "summary": "string",

        "property2": true
      },
      "starred": true,
      "archived": true,
      "is_draft": true,
      "draft_only": true,

        {}
      ],
      "labels": [
        "string"
      ],
      "inherited_labels": [
        "string"
      ],
      "ws_error_handler_muted": true,
      "edited_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "hash": "string",
      "language": "string",
      "kind": "string",
      "auto_kind": "string",
      "use_codebase": true,
      "has_deploy_errors": true,
      "chat_input_enabled": true,
      "raw_app": true,
      "execution_mode": "string",
      "id": 0,
      "version": 0,

    }
  ],

}
```

## list every draft the current user has in this workspace, across all kinds

<a id="opIdlistDrafts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/drafts/list \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /w/{workspace}/drafts/list`

<h3 id="list-every-draft-the-current-user-has-in-this-workspace-across-all-kinds-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|all_users|query|boolean|false|List every draft in the workspace (all users), not just the current user's own + legacy rows. Other users' rows come back with `mine=false` (view-only).|
|compare_to_workspace|query|string|false|A fork passes its parent workspace id here to have each row flagged with `unchanged_from_parent`. Ignored unless it is exactly this workspace's parent.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "kind": "script",
    "path": "string",
    "summary": "string",
    "draft_path": "string",
    "draft_only": true,
    "legacy_draft": true,
    "created_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "can_write": true,
    "mine": true,
    "unchanged_from_parent": true,
    "draft_users": [
      {
        "username": "string"
      }
    ]
  }
]
```

<h3 id="list-every-draft-the-current-user-has-in-this-workspace-across-all-kinds-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|the user's drafts|Inline|

<h3 id="list-every-draft-the-current-user-has-in-this-workspace-across-all-kinds-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[object]|false|none|none|
|» kind|[UserDraftItemKind](#schemauserdraftitemkind)|true|none|Closed set of item kinds a user can autosave as a draft. Mirrors the<br>Postgres `DRAFT_KIND` enum and the backend `UserDraftItemKind`.<br>|
|» path|string|true|none|none|
|» summary|string|false|none|Best-effort, read from the draft JSON's `summary` field when the editor shape carries one.|
|» draft_path|string|false|none|User-typed friendly path from the draft JSON's `draft_path`, when set and different from the storage path (e.g. a never-deployed item parked at `u/{user}/draft_{uuid}`).|
|» draft_only|boolean|true|none|No deployed counterpart exists at this path — the draft is the whole item.|
|» legacy_draft|boolean|true|none|The listed draft is a legacy workspace-level row (email NULL) predating the per-user drafts migration. Only true when no per-user draft exists at this path.|
|» created_at|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|» can_write|boolean|true|none|Whether the current user may deploy/discard this draft (same check the deploy/discard endpoints enforce).|
|» mine|boolean|true|none|The row belongs to the current user (own draft or the legacy no-owner row) and is therefore actionable. Always true in the default listing; with `all_users=true`, other users' rows are false (view-only).|
|» unchanged_from_parent|boolean|false|none|Only present when `compare_to_workspace` was passed. True when this draft is identical to the parent's draft at the same path/kind/owner (cloned in on fork and never edited here).|
|» draft_users|[object]|false|none|Draft authors at this (path, kind) — the legacy NULL-email row surfaced as a null username.<br>Populated only for the shared full-page-editor kinds (script/flow/app/raw_app); omitted for<br>drawer kinds, which keep their drafts private. Feeds the Draft badge's owner-avatar circles.<br>|
|» » username|string \| null|false|none|none|

|» kind|flow|
|» kind|app|
|» kind|raw_app|

|» kind|variable|

## upsert (or clear) the current user's draft at a path

<a id="opIdupdateDraft"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/drafts/update/script/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "value": null,
    "last_sync": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "force": true,
    "legacy": true,
    "created_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  }'
```

`POST /w/{workspace}/drafts/update/{kind}/{path}`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "value": null,
  "last_sync": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "force": true,
  "legacy": true,
  "created_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

<h3 id="upsert-or-clear-the-current-users-draft-at-a-path-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|kind|path|[UserDraftItemKind](#schemauserdraftitemkind)|true|none|
|path|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» value|body|object \| null|false|Draft content to save. `null` (or omitted) signals a delete — the row is removed under the same conflict rules.|
|» last_sync|body|string(date-time)|false|Server timestamp of the client's last known sync for this draft. Omit on first save.|
|» force|body|boolean|false|Skip the conflict check and overwrite the server copy.|
|» legacy|body|boolean|false|Delete-only. Target the legacy workspace-level row (email NULL) instead of the current user's row. Used to discard a legacy draft from the review page.|
|» created_at|body|string(date-time)|false|Upsert-only override for the stored creation timestamp. Normal saves omit it (stamped server-side); the localStorage→DB migration passes the draft's original write time so migrated drafts keep their age.|

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

## move the current user's draft-only item to another path

<a id="opIdmoveDraft"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/drafts/move/script/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "new_path": "string",
    "summary": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /w/{workspace}/drafts/move/{kind}/{path}`

Relocates the authed user's own draft row, along with both path keys inside its value (the typed path and the mirror the editors keep beside it). Only for draft-only items — a deployed item must be moved through its own deploy endpoint, which carries every draft with it. Restricted to script, flow, app and raw_app; any other kind is rejected with 400, because only these keep their deploy target where this endpoint rewrites it.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "new_path": "string",
  "summary": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="move-the-current-users-draft-only-item-to-another-path-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|kind|path|string|true|script, flow, app or raw_app only.|
|path|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» new_path|body|string|true|none|
|» summary|body|string|false|Also restate the draft's summary.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|kind|script|
|kind|flow|
|kind|app|
|kind|raw_app|

```bash
  -d '{}'
```

`POST /w/{workspace}/jobs/run/p/{path}`

> Body parameter

```json
{}
```

<h3 id="run-script-by-path-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|path|path|string|true|none|
|scheduled_for|query|string(date-time)|false|when to schedule this job (leave empty for immediate run)|
|scheduled_in_secs|query|integer|false|schedule the script to execute in the number of seconds starting now|
|skip_preprocessor|query|boolean|false|skip the preprocessor|
|parent_job|query|string(uuid)|false|The parent job that is at the origin and responsible for the execution of this script if any|
|tag|query|string|false|Override the tag to use|
|cache_ttl|query|string|false|Override the cache time to live (in seconds). Can not be used to disable caching, only override with a new cache ttl|
|job_id|query|string(uuid)|false|The job id to assign to the created job. if missing, job is chosen randomly using the ULID scheme. If a job id already exists in the queue or as a completed job, the request to create one will fail (Bad Request)|
|retry|query|string|false|JSON-encoded retry policy (same shape as a schedule's retry) re-running the job when it fails. The returned id is the first attempt's; each retry is a job of its own, recorded as a child of the first attempt. Not supported for hub scripts, with invisible_to_owner, or for a script whose preprocessor would run.|
|invisible_to_owner|query|boolean|false|make the run invisible to the the script owner (default false)|
|body|body|[ScriptArgs](#schemascriptargs)|true|script args|

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|job created|Inline|

bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

## mint a read-only share token for a job

<a id="opIdgetJobViewToken"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/jobs/job_view_token/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /w/{workspace}/jobs/job_view_token/{id}`

Returns a stateless `{job_id}.{hmac}` token that grants an authenticated workspace member read access to this job (and its flow subtree) via a `view_token` query param or `X-View-Token` header. Only callable by a user who can already read the job.


<h3 id="mint-a-read-only-share-token-for-a-job-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|

<h3 id="mint-a-read-only-share-token-for-a-job-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|the share read token|Inline|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

<h3 id="restart-a-completed-flow-at-a-given-step-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|scheduled_for|query|string(date-time)|false|when to schedule this job (leave empty for immediate run)|
|scheduled_in_secs|query|integer|false|schedule the script to execute in the number of seconds starting now|
|parent_job|query|string(uuid)|false|The parent job that is at the origin and responsible for the execution of this script if any|
|tag|query|string|false|Override the tag to use|
|job_id|query|string(uuid)|false|The job id to assign to the created job. if missing, job is chosen randomly using the ULID scheme. If a job id already exists in the queue or as a completed job, the request to create one will fail (Bad Request)|
|include_header|query|string|false|List of headers's keys (separated with ',') whove value are added to the args<br>Header's key lowercased and '-'' replaced to '_' such that 'Content-Type' becomes the 'content_type' arg key<br>|
|invisible_to_owner|query|boolean|false|make the run invisible to the the flow owner (default false)|
|body|body|object|true|restart flow parameters|
|» step_id|body|string|true|top-level step id to restart the flow from (or the outermost container when restarting at a nested step)|
|» branch_or_iteration_n|body|integer|false|for branchall or loop at the top level, the iteration at which the flow should restart (optional)|
|» flow_version|body|integer|false|specific flow version to use for restart (optional, uses current version if not specified)|
|» nested_path|body|[object]|false|path of additional steps to descend into AFTER `step_id`. Each entry represents one level of nesting inside the spawned child of the previous level's container (BranchOne / sequential ForLoop iteration / Subflow). |» » step_id|body|string|true|step id at this nesting level|
|» » branch_or_iteration_n|body|integer|false|for ForLoop containers, the iteration to restart at (0-based; iterations 0..n-1 are preserved)|

<h3 id="run-flow-preview-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|include_header|query|string|false|List of headers's keys (separated with ',') whove value are added to the args<br>Header's key lowercased and '-'' replaced to '_' such that 'Content-Type' becomes the 'content_type' arg key<br>|
|invisible_to_owner|query|boolean|false|make the run invisible to the the script owner (default false)|
|job_id|query|string(uuid)|false|The job id to assign to the created job. if missing, job is chosen randomly using the ULID scheme. If a job id already exists in the queue or as a completed job, the request to create one will fail (Bad Request)|
|memory_id|query|string|false|Memory id for the flow's AI agent steps. A uuid is used as is; any other string is hashed within the workspace and flow, so the same string always names the same memory of that flow.|
|body|body|[FlowPreview](#schemaflowpreview)|true|preview|
|» value|body|[FlowValue](#schemaflowvalue)|true|The flow structure containing modules and optional preprocessor/failure handlers|
|» path|body|string|false|none|
|» args|body|[ScriptArgs](#schemascriptargs)|true|The arguments to pass to the script or flow|
|» tag|body|string|false|none|
|» restarted_from|body|[RestartedFrom](#schemarestartedfrom)|false|none|
|» temp_script_refs|body|object \| null|false|Map of relative-import script path -> temp storage hash, propagated to each flow step so inline-script relative imports resolve from not-yet-deployed local content instead of the deployed script|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» on_behalf_of|body|string \| null|false|Run the preview as this identity (an email, `u/<username>` or `g/<group>`) instead of the caller. Naming anyone other than yourself requires being an admin or a member of wm_deployers.|

<h3 id="run-flow-preview-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|job created|Inline|
|409|Conflict|Chat-enabled flow only: the conversation named by `memory_id` is still answering a message. The body is JSON: `{ "error": string, "running_turn": { "job_id", "user_seq" } }`.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

## run a saved AI agent

<a id="opIdrunAgent"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/jobs/run/agent/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "user_message": "string",
    "user_attachments": [
      null
    ],
    "previous_messages": [
      null
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /w/{workspace}/jobs/run/agent/{path}`

Runs the `ai_agent` resource at `path` as stored, for any caller who can read it
(operators included). The run is the caller's, or the agent's `on_behalf_of` when its
`run_on_behalf_of` is set; the caller's inputs may then not reference variables or
resources. With `memory_id`, the run is a turn
of the caller's conversation with the agent; without, a single run.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "user_message": "string",
  "user_attachments": [
    null
  ],
  "previous_messages": [
    null
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="run-a-saved-ai-agent-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|path|path|string|true|none|
|memory_id|query|string|false|The conversation this turn belongs to. A uuid is used as is; any other string is hashed within the workspace and agent.|
|body|body|object|true|the run's inputs|
|» user_message|body|string|false|none|
|» user_attachments|body|[object]|false|none|
|» previous_messages|body|[object]|false|The history to answer from, as chat messages, when the agent's memory is off.<br>An agent with managed memory reads its conversation instead and ignores this.<br>|

<h3 id="run-a-saved-ai-agent-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|job created|Inline|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

```json
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "on_behalf_of": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="run-flow-preview-and-wait-for-result-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|memory_id|query|string|false|Memory id for the flow's AI agent steps. A uuid is used as is; any other string is hashed within the workspace and flow, so the same string always names the same memory of that flow.|
|body|body|[FlowPreview](#schemaflowpreview)|true|preview|
|» value|body|[FlowValue](#schemaflowvalue)|true|The flow structure containing modules and optional preprocessor/failure handlers|
|» path|body|string|false|none|
|» args|body|[ScriptArgs](#schemascriptargs)|true|The arguments to pass to the script or flow|
|» tag|body|string|false|none|
|» restarted_from|body|[RestartedFrom](#schemarestartedfrom)|false|none|
|» temp_script_refs|body|object \| null|false|Map of relative-import script path -> temp storage hash, propagated to each flow step so inline-script relative imports resolve from not-yet-deployed local content instead of the deployed script|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» on_behalf_of|body|string \| null|false|Run the preview as this identity (an email, `u/<username>` or `g/<group>`) instead of the caller. Naming anyone other than yourself requires being an admin or a member of wm_deployers.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
null
```

<h3 id="run-flow-preview-and-wait-for-result-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|job result|Inline|
|409|Conflict|Chat-enabled flow only: the conversation named by `memory_id` is still answering a message. The body is JSON: `{ "error": string, "running_turn": { "job_id", "user_seq" } }`.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

## list all queued jobs

<a id="opIdlistQueue"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/jobs/queue/list \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /w/{workspace}/jobs/queue/list`

<h3 id="list-all-queued-jobs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|order_desc|query|boolean|false|order by desc order (default true)|
|created_by|query|string|false|filter by exact matching user creator. Supports comma-separated list (e.g. 'alice,bob') and negation by prefixing all values with '!' (e.g. '!alice,!bob')|
|parent_job|query|string(uuid)|false|The parent job that is at the origin and responsible for the execution of this script if any|
|worker|query|string|false|filter by worker this job ran on. Supports comma-separated list (e.g. 'worker-1,worker-2') and negation by prefixing all values with '!' (e.g. '!worker-1,!worker-2')|
|script_path_exact|query|string|false|filter by exact matching script path. Supports comma-separated list (e.g. 'f/script1,f/script2') and negation by prefixing all values with '!' (e.g. '!f/script1,!f/script2')|
|script_path_start|query|string|false|filter by script path prefix. Supports comma-separated list (e.g. 'f/folder1,f/folder2') and negation by prefixing all values with '!' (e.g. '!f/folder1,!f/folder2')|
|schedule_path|query|string|false|mask to filter by schedule path|
|trigger_path|query|string|false|filter by trigger path. Supports comma-separated list (e.g. 'f/trigger1,f/trigger2') and negation by prefixing all values with '!' (e.g. '!f/trigger1,!f/trigger2')|
|trigger_kind|query|string|false|filter by trigger kind. Supports comma-separated list (e.g. 'schedule,webhook') and negation by prefixing all values with '!' (e.g. '!schedule,!webhook')|
|script_hash|query|string|false|mask to filter exact matching path|
|started_before|query|string(date-time)|false|filter on started before (inclusive) timestamp|
|started_after|query|string(date-time)|false|filter on started after (exclusive) timestamp|
|success|query|boolean|false|filter on successful jobs|
|scheduled_for_before_now|query|boolean|false|filter on jobs scheduled_for before now (hence waitinf for a worker)|
|job_kinds|query|string|false|filter by job kind. Supports comma-separated list of values ('preview', 'script', 'dependencies', 'flow') and negation by prefixing all values with '!' (e.g. '!preview,!dependencies')|
|suspended|query|boolean|false|filter on suspended jobs|
|running|query|boolean|false|filter on running jobs|
|args|query|string|false|filter on jobs containing those args as a json subset (@> in postgres)|
|result|query|string|false|filter on jobs containing those result as a json subset (@> in postgres)|
|allow_wildcards|query|boolean|false|allow wildcards (*) in the filter of label, tag, worker|
|tag|query|string|false|filter by tag/worker group. Supports comma-separated list (e.g. 'gpu,highmem') and negation by prefixing all values with '!' (e.g. '!gpu,!highmem')|
|page|query|integer|false|which page to return (start at 1, default 1)|
|per_page|query|integer|false|number of items to return for a given page (default 30, max 100)|
|all_workspaces|query|boolean|false|get jobs from all workspaces (only valid if request come from the `admins` workspace)|
|is_not_schedule|query|boolean|false|is not a scheduled job|

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

## get the ids of all jobs matching the given filters

<a id="opIdlistFilteredJobsUuids"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/jobs/list_filtered_uuids \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /w/{workspace}/jobs/list_filtered_uuids`

<h3 id="get-the-ids-of-all-jobs-matching-the-given-filters-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|order_desc|query|boolean|false|order by desc order (default true)|
|created_by|query|string|false|filter by exact matching user creator. Supports comma-separated list (e.g. 'alice,bob') and negation by prefixing all values with '!' (e.g. '!alice,!bob')|
|label|query|string|false|filter by exact matching job label. Supports comma-separated list (e.g. 'deploy,release') and negation by prefixing all values with '!' (e.g. '!deploy,!release')|
|worker|query|string|false|filter by worker this job ran on. Supports comma-separated list (e.g. 'worker-1,worker-2') and negation by prefixing all values with '!' (e.g. '!worker-1,!worker-2')|
|parent_job|query|string(uuid)|false|The parent job that is at the origin and responsible for the execution of this script if any|
|script_path_exact|query|string|false|filter by exact matching script path. Supports comma-separated list (e.g. 'f/script1,f/script2') and negation by prefixing all values with '!' (e.g. '!f/script1,!f/script2')|
|script_path_start|query|string|false|filter by script path prefix. Supports comma-separated list (e.g. 'f/folder1,f/folder2') and negation by prefixing all values with '!' (e.g. '!f/folder1,!f/folder2')|
|schedule_path|query|string|false|mask to filter by schedule path|
|script_hash|query|string|false|mask to filter exact matching path|
|started_before|query|string(date-time)|false|filter on started before (inclusive) timestamp|
|started_after|query|string(date-time)|false|filter on started after (exclusive) timestamp|
|created_before|query|string(date-time)|false|filter on created before (inclusive) timestamp|
|created_after|query|string(date-time)|false|filter on created after (exclusive) timestamp|
|completed_before|query|string(date-time)|false|filter on started before (inclusive) timestamp|
|completed_after|query|string(date-time)|false|filter on started after (exclusive) timestamp|
|created_before_queue|query|string(date-time)|false|filter on jobs created before X for jobs in the queue only|
|created_after_queue|query|string(date-time)|false|filter on jobs created after X for jobs in the queue only|
|running|query|boolean|false|filter on running jobs|
|scheduled_for_before_now|query|boolean|false|filter on jobs scheduled_for before now (hence waitinf for a worker)|
|job_kinds|query|string|false|filter by job kind. Supports comma-separated list of values ('preview', 'script', 'dependencies', 'flow') and negation by prefixing all values with '!' (e.g. '!preview,!dependencies')|
|suspended|query|boolean|false|filter on suspended jobs|
|args|query|string|false|filter on jobs containing those args as a json subset (@> in postgres)|
|tag|query|string|false|filter by tag/worker group. Supports comma-separated list (e.g. 'gpu,highmem') and negation by prefixing all values with '!' (e.g. '!gpu,!highmem')|
|result|query|string|false|filter on jobs containing those result as a json subset (@> in postgres)|
|page|query|integer|false|which page to return (start at 1, default 1)|
|per_page|query|integer|false|number of items to return for a given page (default 30, max 100)|
|is_skipped|query|boolean|false|is the job skipped|
|resolved|query|boolean|false|filter on whether a failed or canceled run has been marked as handled. true keeps only resolved runs, false hides them|
|is_flow_step|query|boolean|false|is the job a flow step|
|has_null_parent|query|boolean|false|has null parent|
|success|query|boolean|false|filter on successful jobs|
|status|query|string|false|filter on the exact completed job status. Unlike `success=true` (which also matches `skipped`), `status=success` matches only `success`.|
|all_workspaces|query|boolean|false|get jobs from all workspaces (only valid if request come from the `admins` workspace)|
|is_not_schedule|query|boolean|false|is not a scheduled job|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|status|success|
|status|failure|
|status|canceled|
|status|skipped|

```json
]
```

## start a queued job scheduled for later now

<a id="opIdrunQueuedJobNow"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/jobs/queue/run_now/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /w/{workspace}/jobs/queue/run_now/{id}`

Moves the start of a queued job that is waiting for a future time (scheduled, debounced,
re-scheduled by a concurrency limit, or a flow step waiting on a sleep or a retry delay)
to now, keeping the same job id. A job with a
concurrency limit is still checked against its limit when it is pulled. A schedule's
upcoming tick is refused, since the schedule would queue that tick again.


<h3 id="start-a-queued-job-scheduled-for-later-now-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|

<h3 id="start-a-queued-job-scheduled-for-later-now-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|job id|Inline|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

## list all jobs

<a id="opIdlistJobs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/jobs/list \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /w/{workspace}/jobs/list`

<h3 id="list-all-jobs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|created_by|query|string|false|filter by exact matching user creator. Supports comma-separated list (e.g. 'alice,bob') and negation by prefixing all values with '!' (e.g. '!alice,!bob')|
|label|query|string|false|filter by exact matching job label. Supports comma-separated list (e.g. 'deploy,release') and negation by prefixing all values with '!' (e.g. '!deploy,!release')|
|worker|query|string|false|filter by worker this job ran on. Supports comma-separated list (e.g. 'worker-1,worker-2') and negation by prefixing all values with '!' (e.g. '!worker-1,!worker-2')|
|parent_job|query|string(uuid)|false|The parent job that is at the origin and responsible for the execution of this script if any|
|script_path_exact|query|string|false|filter by exact matching script path. Supports comma-separated list (e.g. 'f/script1,f/script2') and negation by prefixing all values with '!' (e.g. '!f/script1,!f/script2')|
|script_path_start|query|string|false|filter by script path prefix. Supports comma-separated list (e.g. 'f/folder1,f/folder2') and negation by prefixing all values with '!' (e.g. '!f/folder1,!f/folder2')|
|schedule_path|query|string|false|mask to filter by schedule path|
|script_hash|query|string|false|mask to filter exact matching path|
|started_before|query|string(date-time)|false|filter on started before (inclusive) timestamp|
|started_after|query|string(date-time)|false|filter on started after (exclusive) timestamp|
|created_before|query|string(date-time)|false|filter on created before (inclusive) timestamp|
|created_after|query|string(date-time)|false|filter on created after (exclusive) timestamp|
|completed_before|query|string(date-time)|false|filter on started before (inclusive) timestamp|
|completed_after|query|string(date-time)|false|filter on started after (exclusive) timestamp|
|created_before_queue|query|string(date-time)|false|filter on jobs created before X for jobs in the queue only|
|created_after_queue|query|string(date-time)|false|filter on jobs created after X for jobs in the queue only|
|running|query|boolean|false|filter on running jobs|
|scheduled_for_before_now|query|boolean|false|filter on jobs scheduled_for before now (hence waitinf for a worker)|
|job_kinds|query|string|false|filter by job kind. Supports comma-separated list of values ('preview', 'script', 'dependencies', 'flow') and negation by prefixing all values with '!' (e.g. '!preview,!dependencies')|
|suspended|query|boolean|false|filter on suspended jobs|
|args|query|string|false|filter on jobs containing those args as a json subset (@> in postgres)|
|tag|query|string|false|filter by tag/worker group. Supports comma-separated list (e.g. 'gpu,highmem') and negation by prefixing all values with '!' (e.g. '!gpu,!highmem')|
|result|query|string|false|filter on jobs containing those result as a json subset (@> in postgres)|
|allow_wildcards|query|boolean|false|allow wildcards (*) in the filter of label, tag, worker|
|per_page|query|integer|false|number of items to return for a given page (default 30, max 100)|
|trigger_kind|query|string|false|filter by trigger kind. Supports comma-separated list (e.g. 'schedule,webhook') and negation by prefixing all values with '!' (e.g. '!schedule,!webhook')|
|is_skipped|query|boolean|false|is the job skipped|
|resolved|query|boolean|false|filter on whether a failed or canceled run has been marked as handled. true keeps only resolved runs, false hides them|
|is_flow_step|query|boolean|false|is the job a flow step|
|has_null_parent|query|boolean|false|has null parent|
|success|query|boolean|false|filter on successful jobs|
|status|query|string|false|filter on the exact completed job status. Unlike `success=true` (which also matches `skipped`), `status=success` matches only `success`.|
|all_workspaces|query|boolean|false|get jobs from all workspaces (only valid if request come from the `admins` workspace)|
|is_not_schedule|query|boolean|false|is not a scheduled job|
|excludes_entrypoint_override|query|boolean|false|exclude jobs that were started with a `_ENTRYPOINT_OVERRIDE` arg (e.g. dynamic-select helper runs and preprocessor previews)|
|broad_filter|query|string|false|broad search across multiple fields (case-insensitive substring match on path, tag, schedule path, trigger kind, label)|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|status|success|
|status|failure|
|status|canceled|
|status|skipped|

## whether the worker running this job is draining

<a id="opIdworkerIsDraining"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/jobs/worker_is_draining/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /w/{workspace}/jobs/worker_is_draining/{id}`

True once the worker running the job has received its shutdown signal. The worker
still waits for the job to finish, so a long-running job can poll this to exit early.
False when the job is not currently running on a worker.


<h3 id="whether-the-worker-running-this-job-is-draining-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
true
```

<h3 id="whether-the-worker-running-this-job-is-draining-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|whether the worker running this job is draining|Inline|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

`GET /w/{workspace}/jobs_u/get_flow_all_logs_structured/{id}`

<h3 id="get-all-logs-for-a-flow-job-in-a-structured-format-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|structured logs of all flow steps, one entry per job|Inline|

<h3 id="get-all-logs-for-a-flow-job-in-a-structured-format-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[object]|false|none|none|
|» job_id|string|true|none|none|
|» label|string|true|none|human-readable label describing the job's position in the flow tree|
|» kind|string|true|none|job kind (script, flow, forloopflow, ...)|
|» flow_step_id|string \| null|false|none|none|
|» step_path|string \| null|false|none|materialized step path (e.g. "a/b")|
|» depth|integer|true|none|depth in the flow tree (0 for the root flow job)|
|» parent_module_type|string \| null|false|none|parent module type (forloopflow, branchall, ...)|
|» sibling_index|integer|true|none|1-based index of this job among siblings sharing the same step|
|» sibling_count|integer|true|none|total number of siblings sharing the same step|
|» logs|string|true|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

## get statuses and truncated results for all jobs of a flow job's execution tree

<a id="opIdgetFlowAllResults"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/jobs_u/get_flow_all_results/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /w/{workspace}/jobs_u/get_flow_all_results/{id}`

<h3 id="get-statuses-and-truncated-results-for-all-jobs-of-a-flow-jobs-execution-tree-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|max_result_len|query|integer|false|per-entry cap (in characters of JSON text) on result_prefix (default 2000, max 30000)|
|step|query|string|false|step address to resolve to a single job instead of enumerating the tree: "b", "b/c", "b[12]" (1-based iteration/branch), composable as "b[12]/c"|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "enclosing_job": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "entries": [
    {
      "job_id": "string",
      "label": "string",
      "kind": "string",
      "flow_step_id": "string",
      "step_path": "string",
      "depth": 0,
      "parent_module_type": "string",
      "sibling_index": 0,
      "sibling_count": 0,
      "status": "success",
      "success": true,
      "duration_ms": 0,
      "started_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "result_prefix": "string",
      "result_length": 0
    }
  ],
  "truncated": true,
  "scope_filtered": true,
  "step_error": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="get-statuses-and-truncated-results-for-all-jobs-of-a-flow-jobs-execution-tree-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|per-job statuses and truncated results of the flow's execution tree, or the single resolved entry when step is provided|Inline|

<h3 id="get-statuses-and-truncated-results-for-all-jobs-of-a-flow-jobs-execution-tree-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enclosing_job|string(uuid)|false|none|set when the requested job is itself a step of a larger flow run; id of the flow run directly enclosing it|
|entries|[object]|true|none|none|
|» job_id|string|true|none|none|
|» label|string|true|none|human-readable label describing the job's position in the flow tree|
|» kind|string|true|none|job kind (script, flow, forloopflow, ...)|
|» flow_step_id|string \| null|false|none|none|
|» step_path|string \| null|false|none|materialized step path (e.g. "a/b")|
|» depth|integer|true|none|depth in the flow tree (0 for the root flow job)|
|» parent_module_type|string \| null|false|none|parent module type (forloopflow, branchall, ...)|
|» sibling_index|integer|true|none|1-based index of this job among siblings sharing the same step|
|» sibling_count|integer|true|none|total number of siblings sharing the same step|
|» status|string|true|none|none|
|» success|boolean|false|none|none|
|» duration_ms|integer(int64)|false|none|none|
|» started_at|string(date-time)|false|none|none|
|» result_prefix|string|false|none|result JSON text truncated to the per-entry budget; absent until the job has completed|
|» result_length|integer|false|none|full length in characters of the result JSON text (greater than the prefix length when truncated)|
|truncated|boolean|false|none|true when the tree has more jobs than the entry cap; entries then hold the depth-first prefix|
|scope_filtered|boolean|false|none|true when the caller's token is tag-scoped; steps running on other tags are omitted|
|step_error|string|false|none|set when step was provided but could not be resolved; a diagnostic listing available step ids or iteration statuses|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|» status|success|
|» status|failure|
|» status|canceled|
|» status|skipped|
|» status|suspended|
|» status|running|
|» status|queued|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

<a id="opIdgetCompletedJobLogsTail"></a>

## list asset-trigger dispatch events for a producer job

<a id="opIdlistDispatchEvents"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/jobs_u/dispatch_events/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /w/{workspace}/jobs_u/dispatch_events/{id}`

Returns the chronological log of decisions the asset-trigger dispatcher made after this producer job completed. Each row is one (subscriber, asset write) decision: `dispatched` (with `child_job_id`), `join_pending` (with `received_inputs` / `required_inputs` / `partition`), or `skipped` (with `reason`). Rows are reaped automatically when the producer's `v2_job` row is deleted by the retention sweep.


<h3 id="list-asset-trigger-dispatch-events-for-a-producer-job-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "subscriber_path": "string",
    "asset_kind": "s3object",
    "asset_path": "string",
    "outcome": "dispatched",
    "child_job_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "partition": "string",
    "received_inputs": 0,
    "required_inputs": 0,
    "debounce_s": 0,
    "reason": "string",
    "created_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  }
]
```

<h3 id="list-asset-trigger-dispatch-events-for-a-producer-job-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|dispatch events for this producer job|Inline|

<h3 id="list-asset-trigger-dispatch-events-for-a-producer-job-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[object]|false|none|none|
|» subscriber_path|string|true|none|none|
|» asset_kind|string|true|none|none|
|» asset_path|string|true|none|none|
|» outcome|string|true|none|none|
|» child_job_id|string(uuid)|false|none|none|
|» partition|string|false|none|none|
|» received_inputs|integer|false|none|none|
|» required_inputs|integer|false|none|none|
|» debounce_s|integer|false|none|none|
|» reason|string|false|none|none|
|» created_at|string(date-time)|true|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|» asset_kind|s3object|
|» asset_kind|resource|
|» asset_kind|variable|
|» asset_kind|ducklake|
|» asset_kind|datatable|
|» asset_kind|volume|
|» asset_kind|dbt|
|» outcome|dispatched|
|» outcome|join_pending|
|» outcome|skipped|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

## list asset-cascade producer→child job edges for a folder

<a id="opIdlistAssetDispatchEdges"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/jobs/asset_dispatch_edges?path_start=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /w/{workspace}/jobs/asset_dispatch_edges`

Returns the `dispatched` asset-trigger edges (producer job → child job) whose subscriber lives under `path_start`. Lets a pipeline view reconstruct the cascade tree of a folder by job id and group connected runs. Visibility follows the producer job's RLS.


<h3 id="list-asset-cascade-producerchild-job-edges-for-a-folder-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|path_start|query|string|true|Folder path prefix the children live under, e.g. `f/orders/`.|
|created_after|query|string(date-time)|false|Only edges dispatched at/after this instant.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "producer_job_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "child_job_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "subscriber_path": "string",
    "outcome": "dispatched",
    "asset_kind": "s3object",
    "asset_path": "string",
    "created_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  }
]
```

<h3 id="list-asset-cascade-producerchild-job-edges-for-a-folder-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|asset-cascade edges for the folder|Inline|

<h3 id="list-asset-cascade-producerchild-job-edges-for-a-folder-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[object]|false|none|none|
|» producer_job_id|string(uuid)|true|none|none|
|» child_job_id|string(uuid)|false|none|Set for `dispatched`; absent for `join_pending` inputs.|
|» subscriber_path|string|true|none|none|
|» outcome|string|true|none|none|
|» asset_kind|string|true|none|none|
|» asset_path|string|true|none|none|
|» created_at|string(date-time)|true|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|» outcome|dispatched|
|» outcome|join_pending|
|» asset_kind|s3object|
|» asset_kind|resource|
|» asset_kind|variable|
|» asset_kind|ducklake|
|» asset_kind|datatable|
|» asset_kind|volume|
|» asset_kind|dbt|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

## mark failed or canceled jobs as resolved

<a id="opIdresolveCompletedJobs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/jobs/completed/resolve \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "job_ids": [
      "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
    ],
    "note": "string",
    "superseded_by": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
  }'
```

`POST /w/{workspace}/jobs/completed/resolve`

Marks failed or canceled jobs as handled so triage surfaces stop showing them as unhandled. The job status itself is unchanged. Returns the ids actually resolved: ids that are not visible to the caller or neither failed nor were canceled are silently skipped.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "job_ids": [
    "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
  ],
  "note": "string",
  "superseded_by": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
}
```

<h3 id="mark-failed-or-canceled-jobs-as-resolved-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» job_ids|body|[string(uuid)]|true|none|
|» note|body|string|false|a person's explanation of why the failure is considered handled. Enterprise-only: ignored outside enterprise|
|» superseded_by|body|string(uuid)|false|id of a later successful run of the same runnable that supersedes the failure. Verified server-side, and the resulting note is the server's own wording, so it is recorded regardless of licence. A claim that cannot be verified resolves nothing|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
]
```

<h3 id="mark-failed-or-canceled-jobs-as-resolved-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|ids of the jobs that were resolved|Inline|

<h3 id="mark-failed-or-canceled-jobs-as-resolved-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[string(uuid)]|false|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

`GET /w/{workspace}/jobs_u/flow/approval_info/{job_id}`

Get approval info for a suspended flow/WAC job. Returns form schema, approval rules, and whether the current user can approve. Either a valid token query parameter or an authenticated session is required.


<h3 id="get-approval-info-for-a-suspended-flowwac-job-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|job_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|token|query|string|false|approval token for unauthenticated access|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "flow_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "form_schema": null,
  "description": null,
  "approval_conditions": {
    "user_auth_required": true,
    "user_groups_required": [
      "string"
    ],
    "self_approval_disabled": true
  },
  "can_approve": true,
  "user_auth_required": true,
  "hide_cancel": true,
  "skin": "detailed",
  "step_summary": "string",
  "flow_summary": "string",
  "approvers": [
    {
      "resume_id": 0,
      "approver": "string"
    }
  ],
  "view_token": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="get-approval-info-for-a-suspended-flowwac-job-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|approval info|Inline|

<h3 id="get-approval-info-for-a-suspended-flowwac-job-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|flow_id|string(uuid)|true|none|none|
|form_schema|object|false|none|form schema for the approval step|
|description|object|false|none|description of the approval step|
|approval_conditions|object|false|none|none|
|» user_auth_required|boolean|true|none|none|
|» user_groups_required|[string]|true|none|none|
|» self_approval_disabled|boolean|true|none|none|
|can_approve|boolean|true|none|whether the current user/token holder can approve|
|user_auth_required|boolean|true|none|whether user authentication is required to approve|
|hide_cancel|boolean|false|none|whether to hide the cancel button in the UI|
|skin|string|true|none|how the approval page presents the request|
|step_summary|string|false|none|summary of the approval step, for the page title|
|flow_summary|string|false|none|summary of the flow or workflow the approval belongs to|
|approvers|[object]|true|none|none|
|» resume_id|integer|true|none|none|
|» approver|string|true|none|none|
|view_token|string|false|none|Share-read-link token for the flow. An authenticated workspace member can append it as a `view_token` query param on the run page to read a flow they don't otherwise have access to.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|skin|detailed|
|skin|minimal|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

## Whether a dbt retry by this caller would resume this run

<a id="opIdgetDbtResumable"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/jobs/dbt_resumable/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /w/{workspace}/jobs/dbt_resumable/{id}`

One failed run is saved per script per execution principal, so a `retry` resumes that one — not necessarily the run being looked at. Answers about THIS run alone: its own id when a retry submitted by this caller would resume it, null otherwise (a later run holds the state, the run left nothing to rebuild, or the caller's runs execute as another principal). Authorized through the job, like `run_progress`.


<h3 id="whether-a-dbt-retry-by-this-caller-would-resume-this-run-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|The job whose script and principal decide the saved failure|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
```

<h3 id="whether-a-dbt-retry-by-this-caller-would-resume-this-run-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|this job's id when a retry would resume it, or null|Inline|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

## Which run a dbt retry of this script would resume for the caller

<a id="opIdgetDbtResumableForScript"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/jobs/dbt_resumable_script/p/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /w/{workspace}/jobs/dbt_resumable_script/p/{path}`

A `retry` requires `dbt_retry_job`, and the run form has no job id to hand. Returns the one the caller's own retry would land on — the saved failure for the principal the run would execute as, which is the script's author for an `on_behalf_of` script and the caller otherwise — and only when that run is one the caller may read. Null when there is nothing to resume, or nothing this caller may be told about.


<h3 id="which-run-a-dbt-retry-of-this-script-would-resume-for-the-caller-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|path|path|string|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
```

<h3 id="which-run-a-dbt-retry-of-this-script-would-resume-for-the-caller-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|the job id a retry would resume, or null|Inline|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

## Get the asset graph as one run saw it

<a id="opIdgetDbtRunGraph"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/jobs/dbt_graph/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /w/{workspace}/jobs/dbt_graph/{id}`

The workspace asset graph with its dbt half pinned to what a single run built. Only a dynamic descriptor (a `{{ }}` placeholder in `vars`) leaves a per-run snapshot; without one for this job the pinned version's own graph answers, so a run page may use this route unconditionally. Authorized through the job, the same gate as `run_progress` — pinning to a run is job-scoped, which is why `assets/graph` cannot do it.


<h3 id="get-the-asset-graph-as-one-run-saw-it-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|The job whose graph to render|
|asset_kinds|query|string|false|Filter by asset kinds (comma-separated list)|
|folder|query|string|false|Scope the graph to runnables in a single folder|
|dbt_script_hash|query|string|false|Fallback only, for a job that names no deployed script — a preview or a flow. For a script job the version comes from the job row itself, so this is ignored: which deploy's models, SQL and `ref()` lineage are shown is not the caller's to choose.<br>|

> 200 Response

```json
    }
  ],
  "runnables": [
    {
      "path": "string",
      "usage_kind": "script",

      "macros": [
        {
          "name": "string",

        }
      ],

        "model_count": 0
      }
    }
  ],
```

## Get relations' project column lineage as one run saw it

<a id="opIdgetDbtRunColumnLineage"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/jobs/dbt_column_lineage/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08?asset_path=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /w/{workspace}/jobs/dbt_column_lineage/{id}`

The same answer as `assets/column_lineage`, for the project version a single job ran — including the dbt editor's parse of its own buffer, whose graph belongs to that job and is reachable no other way. One project answers here, the one the run is of, since the graph this annotates is that project's too. Authorized through the job, the same gate as `dbt_graph`. Reaching the run is not on its own enough to read the project: a caller with no access to the script gets its relations and `ref()` edges from `dbt_graph` and an empty answer here, exactly as that endpoint redacts the model's SQL.


<h3 id="get-relations-project-column-lineage-as-one-run-saw-it-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|The job whose graph the lineage is read from|
|asset_path|query|[string]|true|The `dbt://` relations whose lineage to return. Repeated, once per relation, and answered as one union. At least one, and at most 1000 — a request naming none, or more than that, is refused rather than answered with an empty component.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "edges": [
    {
      "from_asset_path": "string",
      "from_column": "string",
      "to_asset_path": "string",
      "to_column": "string",
      "kind": "string"
    }
  ],
  "truncated": true
}
```

<h3 id="get-relations-project-column-lineage-as-one-run-saw-it-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|the relations' column-level lineage|[DbtColumnLineage](#schemadbtcolumnlineage)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

`GET /w/{workspace}/jobs/run_progress/{id}`

Live materialization state for the relations a single job writes, keyed by relation. Polled while a run is in flight so a graph can move a node as its model completes. ## List the assets a run touched at runtime

<a id="opIdlistRunAssets"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/jobs/run_assets/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /w/{workspace}/jobs/run_assets/{id}`

Assets detected while the run executed (SDK S3 calls, resources passed as arguments), aggregated over the job and all of its child jobs so a flow or workflow-as-code run reports what its steps and tasks touched. Authorized through the job, the same gate as `run_progress`. Recording is asynchronous, so an asset can take a few minutes after the run to appear, and only the most recent runs that touched an asset keep that record. A run that fans out can touch more assets than one response should carry, so the list is capped and `truncated` says when it was cut.


<h3 id="list-the-assets-a-run-touched-at-runtime-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|The job whose runtime assets to read|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "truncated": true,
  "assets": [
    {
      "path": "string",
      "kind": "s3object",
      "access_type": "r"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="list-the-assets-a-run-touched-at-runtime-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|assets this run and its child jobs touched|Inline|

<h3 id="list-the-assets-a-run-touched-at-runtime-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|truncated|boolean|true|none|whether the run touched more assets than are listed|
|assets|[object]|true|none|none|
|» path|string|true|none|none|
|» kind|[AssetKind](#schemaassetkind)|true|none|none|
|» access_type|[AssetUsageAccessType](#schemaassetusageaccesstype)|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|» kind|s3object|
|» kind|resource|
|» kind|ducklake|
|» kind|datatable|
|» kind|volume|
|» kind|dbt|
|» access_type|r|
|» access_type|w|
|» access_type|rw|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:

</aside>

## one text completion with the workspace's AI config

<a id="opIdcompleteAi"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/ai/complete \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \

  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \

    "user": "string",
```

`POST /w/{workspace}/ai/complete`

Sends a system and a user message to the configured provider and returns the text of the answer, with no tools and no streaming. For callers that do not speak a provider's own API through the proxy, such as the CLI and jobs.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "system": "string",
  "user": "string",
  "model": {
    "model": "string",
    "provider": "openai"
  },
  "max_tokens": 0
}
```

|» user|body|string|true|none|
|» model|body|[AIProviderModel](#schemaaiprovidermodel)|false|defaults to the AI config's default model|
|» max_tokens|body|integer|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "text": "string",
  "model": {
    "model": "string",
```

## share an AI session artifact with the workspace

<a id="opIdshareAiArtifact"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/ai/shared_artifacts/share \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \

    "artifact_id": "string",
```
