`POST /w/{workspace}/ai/shared_artifacts/share`

Stores a read-only copy that any member of the workspace can open by id. Sharing the same artifact again updates that copy, keeps its id, and restarts its retention window.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "artifact_id": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "kind": "md",
  "version": 1,
  "content": "string"
```

## share an AI session transcript by link

<a id="opIdshareAiSession"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/ai/shared_sessions/share \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "session_id": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "is_public": true,
    "message_count": 0,
    "snapshot": {}
  }'
```

`POST /w/{workspace}/ai/shared_sessions/share`

Stores a read-only snapshot of the session that members of the workspace can open by id, or anyone with the link once it is public. Sharing the same session again updates that snapshot and keeps its id.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "session_id": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "is_public": true,
  "message_count": 0,
  "snapshot": {}
}
```

<h3 id="share-an-ai-session-transcript-by-link-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» session_id|body|string|true|the session's id in the author's browser|
|» name|body|string|true|none|
|» is_public|body|boolean|false|left as it is on an existing share when absent; a new share starts private|
|» message_count|body|integer|true|none|
|» snapshot|body|object|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "name": "string",
  "is_public": true,
  "message_count": 0,
  "created_by": "string",
  "shared_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

<h3 id="share-an-ai-session-transcript-by-link-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|the shared snapshot|[SharedAiSessionInfo](#schemasharedaisessioninfo)|

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|path|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|updated eval dataset|
|» path|body|string|false|Renames the dataset. Its cases and experiments follow through the foreign keys, so a rename keeps the history it already has.<br>|
|» summary|body|string|false|Left out to keep the stored summary; sent as "" to clear it.|
|» scorers|body|[[Scorer](#schemascorer)]|false|Left out to keep the dataset's columns as they are; sent to replace them wholesale.<br>|
|» cases|body|[[SaveEvalCase](#schemasaveevalcase)]|false|The cases as they should stand afterwards: all of them, each carrying its id if the dataset already has it. Sent with the rest of an edit so that a rename the dataset refuses refuses the case edits with it.<br>|

## record what a run produced, so it outlives the jobs that produced it

<a id="opIdcollectExperiment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/ai_evals/experiments/collect?id=497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08' \

```

`POST /w/{workspace}/ai_evals/experiments/collect`

<h1 id="windmill-api-pathautocomplete">path_autocomplete</h1>

## list all paths in a workspace for client-side autocomplete

<a id="opIdlistPathAutocompletePaths"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/path_autocomplete/list_paths \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /w/{workspace}/path_autocomplete/list_paths`

Returns the flat list of all item paths visible to the caller across
scripts, flows, apps, raw apps, variables, and resources. Intended to
feed an entirely client-side path autocomplete UI: the frontend fetches
once (server caches per caller for 60s) and performs all prefix/segment
computation locally. Capped at 20,000 paths (5,000 per table).


<h3 id="list-all-paths-in-a-workspace-for-client-side-autocomplete-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|force|query|boolean|false|bypass the server-side cache and re-query the DB, refreshing the<br>cache. Used right after a deploy so the new path appears immediately.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "paths": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="list-all-paths-in-a-workspace-for-client-side-autocomplete-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|deduplicated path list, sorted lexicographically|Inline|

<h3 id="list-all-paths-in-a-workspace-for-client-side-autocomplete-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|paths|[string]|true|none|none|

bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

|per_page|query|integer|false|number of items to return for a given page (default 30, max 100)|
|order_desc|query|boolean|false|order by desc order (default true)|

Synthesized rows carry `draft_only: true`<br>so the home page can render a "Draft" badge. Gated to<br>non-operators + page 0 + no narrowing filters on the backend so<br>picker callers stay deployed-only and pagination stays clean.<br>|

<h3 id="create-schedule-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[NewSchedule](#schemanewschedule)|true|new schedule|
|» path|body|string|true|The unique Windmill path for this schedule. Must be of the form `u/<user>/<path>` or `f/<folder>/<path>`.|
|» schedule|body|string|true|Cron expression with 6 fields (seconds, minutes, hours, day of month, month, day of week). Example '0 0 12 * * *' for daily at noon|
|» timezone|body|string|true|IANA timezone for the schedule (e.g., 'UTC', 'Europe/Paris', 'America/New_York')|
|» script_path|body|string|true|Path to the script or flow to execute when triggered|
|» is_flow|body|boolean|true|True if script_path points to a flow, false if it points to a script|
|» args|body|[ScriptArgs](#schemascriptargs)|true|The arguments to pass to the script or flow|
|» enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether the schedule is currently active and will trigger jobs|
|» on_failure|body|string \| null|false|Path to a script or flow to run when the scheduled job fails|
|» on_failure_times|body|number \| null|false|Number of consecutive failures before the on_failure handler is triggered (default 1)|
|» on_failure_exact|body|boolean \| null|false|If true, trigger on_failure handler only on exactly N failures, not on every failure after N|
|» on_failure_extra_args|body|[ScriptArgs](#schemascriptargs)|false|The arguments to pass to the script or flow|
|» on_recovery|body|string \| null|false|Path to a script or flow to run when the schedule recovers after failures|
|» on_recovery_times|body|number \| null|false|Number of consecutive successes before the on_recovery handler is triggered (default 1)|
|» on_recovery_extra_args|body|[ScriptArgs](#schemascriptargs)|false|The arguments to pass to the script or flow|
|» on_success|body|string \| null|false|Path to a script or flow to run after each successful execution|
|» on_success_extra_args|body|[ScriptArgs](#schemascriptargs)|false|The arguments to pass to the script or flow|
|» ws_error_handler_muted|body|boolean|false|If true, the workspace-level error handler will not be triggered for this schedule's failures|
|» retry|body|[Retry](#schemaretry)|false|Retry configuration for failed module executions|
|» no_flow_overlap|body|boolean|false|If true, skip this schedule's execution if the previous run is still in progress (prevents concurrent runs)|
|» summary|body|string \| null|false|Short summary describing the purpose of this schedule|
|» description|body|string \| null|false|Detailed description of what this schedule does|
|» tag|body|string \| null|false|Worker tag to route jobs to specific worker groups|
|» paused_until|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|ISO 8601 datetime until which the schedule is paused. Schedule resumes automatically after this time|
|» cron_version|body|string \| null|false|Cron parser version. Use 'v2' for extended syntax with additional features|
|» dynamic_skip|body|string \| null|false|Path to a script that validates scheduled datetimes. Receives scheduled_for datetime and returns boolean to skip (true) or run (false)|
|» permissioned_as|body|string|false|The user or group this schedule runs as. Used during deployment to preserve the original schedule owner.|
|» preserve_permissioned_as|body|boolean|false|When true and the caller is a member of the 'wm_deployers' group, preserves the original permissioned_as value instead of overwriting it.|
|» labels|body|[string]|false|none|

|timezone|string|true|none|IANA timezone for the schedule (e.g., 'UTC', 'Europe/Paris', 'America/New_York')|
|enabled|boolean|true|none|Whether the schedule is currently active and will trigger jobs|
|script_path|string|true|none|Path to the script or flow to execute when triggered|
|is_flow|boolean|true|none|True if script_path points to a flow, false if it points to a script|
|args|[ScriptArgs](#schemascriptargs)|false|none|The arguments to pass to the script or flow|
|extra_perms|object|true|none|Additional permissions for this schedule|
|» **additionalProperties**|boolean|false|none|none|
|email|string|true|none|Email of the user who owns this schedule, used for permissioned_as|
|permissioned_as|string|true|none|The user or group this schedule runs as (e.g., 'u/admin' or 'g/mygroup')|
|error|string \| null|false|none|Last error message if the schedule failed to trigger|
|on_failure|string \| null|false|none|Path to a script or flow to run when the scheduled job fails|
|on_failure_times|number \| null|false|none|Number of consecutive failures before the on_failure handler is triggered (default 1)|
|on_failure_exact|boolean \| null|false|none|If true, trigger on_failure handler only on exactly N failures, not on every failure after N|
|on_failure_extra_args|[ScriptArgs](#schemascriptargs)|false|none|The arguments to pass to the script or flow|
|on_recovery|string \| null|false|none|Path to a script or flow to run when the schedule recovers after failures|
|on_recovery_times|number \| null|false|none|Number of consecutive successes before the on_recovery handler is triggered (default 1)|
|on_recovery_extra_args|[ScriptArgs](#schemascriptargs)|false|none|The arguments to pass to the script or flow|
|on_success|string \| null|false|none|Path to a script or flow to run after each successful execution|
|on_success_extra_args|[ScriptArgs](#schemascriptargs)|false|none|The arguments to pass to the script or flow|
|ws_error_handler_muted|boolean|false|none|If true, the workspace-level error handler will not be triggered for this schedule's failures|
|retry|[Retry](#schemaretry)|false|none|Retry configuration for failed module executions|
|summary|string \| null|false|none|Short summary describing the purpose of this schedule|
|description|string \| null|false|none|Detailed description of what this schedule does|
|no_flow_overlap|boolean|false|none|If true, skip this schedule's execution if the previous run is still in progress (prevents concurrent runs)|
|tag|string \| null|false|none|Worker tag to route jobs to specific worker groups|
|paused_until|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|ISO 8601 datetime until which the schedule is paused. Schedule resumes automatically after this time|
|cron_version|string \| null|false|none|Cron parser version. Use 'v2' for extended syntax with additional features|
|dynamic_skip|string \| null|false|none|Path to a script that validates scheduled datetimes. Receives scheduled_for datetime and returns boolean to skip (true) or run (false)|
|labels|[string]|false|none|none|
|draft_only|boolean|false|none|True when this row is a per-user draft with no deployed<br>schedule at the same path. Frontend renders a "Draft" badge.<br>|
|is_draft|boolean|true|none|True when the authed user has a per-user draft at this path<br>(over a deployed row or a synthesized draft-only row).<br>Frontend appends a `*` to the displayed name.<br>|
|inherited_labels|[string]|false|none|Labels inherited from the parent folder, computed at read time. Read-only — edit them on the folder.<br>|
|is_draft|boolean|true|none|none|
|draft_saved_at|string(date-time)|false|none|none|
|draft_base|string|false|none|The deployed version the draft forked from, as text whatever the<br>kind (script hash, flow version id, app version id). Compare to the<br>deployed head to tell a draft that is behind. Absent when there is<br>no draft or it was never forked from a deploy.<br>|
|no_deployed|boolean|false|none|none|
|draft|object|false|none|none|
|other_drafts_users|[object]|false|none|Other workspace users (and the legacy NULL-email row, if any)<br>with a saved draft at the same path. Populated only on the<br>authed user's "get by path" responses for kinds the editor<br>surfaces a fork banner for (script, flow, app, raw_app).<br>Empty / omitted for kinds without that UI.<br>|
|» username|string \| null|false|none|Workspace username of the draft owner. `null` represents<br>the legacy workspace-level (NULL-email) row. Emails never<br>leave the server.<br>|
|» draft_saved_at|string(date-time)|true|none|When this user's draft was last saved (`draft.created_at`),<br>surfaced in the fork modal as "Last updated".<br>|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

<h3 id="create-http-trigger-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[NewHttpTrigger](#schemanewhttptrigger)|true|new http trigger|
|» path|body|string|true|The unique Windmill path for this trigger. Must be of the form `u/<user>/<path>` or `f/<folder>/<path>`. This is the trigger object path, not the HTTP route path.|
|» script_path|body|string|true|Path to the script or flow to execute when triggered|
|» route_path|body|string|true|The URL route path that will trigger this endpoint (e.g., 'api/myendpoint'). Must NOT start with a /.|
|» workspaced_route|body|boolean|false|If true, the route includes the workspace ID in the path|
|» summary|body|string \| null|false|Short summary describing the purpose of this trigger|
|» description|body|string \| null|false|Detailed description of what this trigger does|
|» static_asset_config|body|object \| null|false|Configuration for serving static assets (s3 bucket, storage path, filename)|
|» » s3|body|string|true|S3 bucket path for static assets|
|» » storage|body|string|false|Storage path for static assets|
|» » filename|body|string|false|Filename for the static asset|
|» is_flow|body|boolean|true|True if script_path points to a flow, false if it points to a script|
|» http_method|body|[HttpMethod](#schemahttpmethod)|true|HTTP method (get, post, put, delete, patch) that triggers this endpoint|
|» authentication_resource_path|body|string \| null|false|Path to the resource containing authentication configuration (for api_key, basic_http, custom_script, signature methods)|
|» is_async|body|boolean|false|Deprecated, use request_type instead|
|» request_type|body|[HttpRequestType](#schemahttprequesttype)|false|How the request is handled - 'sync' waits for result, 'async' returns job ID immediately, 'sync_sse' streams results via Server-Sent Events|
|» authentication_method|body|[AuthenticationMethod](#schemaauthenticationmethod)|true|How requests are authenticated - 'none' (public), 'windmill' (Windmill token), 'api_key', 'basic_http', 'custom_script', 'signature'|
|» is_static_website|body|boolean|true|If true, serves static files from S3/storage instead of running a script|
|» wrap_body|body|boolean|false|If true, wraps the request body in a 'body' parameter|
|» mode|body|[TriggerMode](#schematriggermode)|false|job trigger mode|
|» raw_string|body|boolean|false|If true, passes the request body as a raw string instead of parsing as JSON|
|» allowed_origins|body|[string]|false|Origins allowed to call this route cross-origin, matched against the request's Origin header (ignoring case) and echoed back on a match. When set, the list governs both the preflight and the response, overriding any Access-Control-Allow-Origin the runnable returns via wm_headers. Use ['*'] to opt out of any restriction, including the http_route_default_allowed_origins instance setting. An empty list is not a configuration and resolves exactly as null does. When null, the instance setting applies, or Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * if it is unset. Ignored on a static website, which has no authentication of its own and so hands out public files: restricting which browsers may read them protects nothing while breaking cross-origin webfonts and fetches. A single-file static asset is not exempt, since it can carry an authentication_method.|
|» error_handler_path|body|string|false|Path to a script to run when the triggered job fails. A bare path, without the script/ or flow/ prefix a schedule error handler takes; it cannot be a flow.|
|» error_handler_args|body|[ScriptArgs](#schemascriptargs)|false|Arguments to pass to the error handler|
|» retry|body|[Retry](#schemaretry)|false|Retry configuration for failed executions|
|» permissioned_as|body|string|false|The user or group this trigger runs as. Used during deployment to preserve the original trigger owner.|
|» preserve_permissioned_as|body|boolean|false|When true and the caller is a member of the 'wm_deployers' group, preserves the original permissioned_as value instead of overwriting it.|
|» labels|body|[string]|false|none|

<h3 id="create-websocket-trigger-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[NewWebsocketTrigger](#schemanewwebsockettrigger)|true|new websocket trigger|
|» path|body|string|true|The unique Windmill path for this trigger. Must be of the form `u/<user>/<path>` or `f/<folder>/<path>`. This is the trigger object path, not the HTTP route path.|
|» script_path|body|string|true|Path to the script or flow to execute when a message is received|
|» is_flow|body|boolean|true|True if script_path points to a flow, false if it points to a script|
|» url|body|string|true|The WebSocket URL to connect to (can be a static URL or computed by a runnable)|
|» mode|body|[TriggerMode](#schematriggermode)|false|job trigger mode|
|» filters|body|[[TriggerFilter](#schematriggerfilter)]|true|Filters to match incoming messages (only matching messages trigger the script). Each entry is either a leaf `{key, value}` (top-level field) or `{path, value}` (dotted path into nested objects), or a group `{any_of: [...]}` / `{all_of: [...]}` / `{none_of: [...]}` nesting more entries. Entries at the top level are combined with `filter_logic`.|
|» filter_logic|body|string|false|Logic to apply when evaluating the top-level filters. 'and' requires all of them to match, 'or' requires any of them to match. Nested `any_of`/`all_of`/`none_of` groups carry their own logic.|
|» initial_messages|body|[[WebsocketTriggerInitialMessage](#schemawebsockettriggerinitialmessage)]|false|Messages to send immediately after connecting (can be raw strings or computed by runnables)|
|» url_runnable_args|body|[ScriptArgs](#schemascriptargs)|false|Arguments to pass to the script/flow that computes the WebSocket URL|
|» can_return_message|body|boolean|true|If true, the script can return a message to send back through the WebSocket|
|» can_return_error_result|body|boolean|true|If true, error results are sent back through the WebSocket|
|» heartbeat|body|[WebsocketHeartbeat](#schemawebsocketheartbeat)|false|Optional periodic heartbeat message configuration|
|» error_handler_path|body|string|false|Path to a script to run when the triggered job fails. A bare path, without the script/ or flow/ prefix a schedule error handler takes; it cannot be a flow.|
|» error_handler_args|body|[ScriptArgs](#schemascriptargs)|false|Arguments to pass to the error handler|
|» retry|body|[Retry](#schemaretry)|false|Retry configuration for failed executions|
|» permissioned_as|body|string|false|The user or group this trigger runs as. Used during deployment to preserve the original trigger owner.|
|» preserve_permissioned_as|body|boolean|false|When true and the caller is a member of the 'wm_deployers' group, preserves the original permissioned_as value instead of overwriting it.|
|» labels|body|[string]|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» mode|enabled|
|» mode|disabled|
|» mode|suspended|
|» filter_logic|and|
|» filter_logic|or|

|url|string|true|none|The WebSocket URL to connect to (can be a static URL or computed by a runnable)|
|server_id|string|false|none|ID of the server currently handling this trigger (internal)|

|initial_messages|[[WebsocketTriggerInitialMessage](#schemawebsockettriggerinitialmessage)]|false|none|Messages to send immediately after connecting (can be raw strings or computed by runnables)|
|url_runnable_args|[ScriptArgs](#schemascriptargs)|false|none|Arguments to pass to the script/flow that computes the WebSocket URL|
|can_return_message|boolean|true|none|If true, the script can return a message to send back through the WebSocket|

|heartbeat|[WebsocketHeartbeat](#schemawebsocketheartbeat)|false|none|Optional periodic heartbeat message configuration|
|error_handler_path|string|false|none|Path to a script to run when the triggered job fails. A bare path, without the script/ or flow/ prefix a schedule error handler takes; it cannot be a flow.|
|error_handler_args|[ScriptArgs](#schemascriptargs)|false|none|Arguments to pass to the error handler|
|retry|[Retry](#schemaretry)|false|none|Retry configuration for failed executions|
|is_draft|boolean|true|none|none|
|draft_saved_at|string(date-time)|false|none|none|
|draft_base|string|false|none|The deployed version the draft forked from, as text whatever the<br>kind (script hash, flow version id, app version id). Compare to the<br>deployed head to tell a draft that is behind. Absent when there is<br>no draft or it was never forked from a deploy.<br>|

|» path|body|string|true|The unique Windmill path for this trigger. Must be of the form `u/<user>/<path>` or `f/<folder>/<path>`. This is the trigger object path, not the HTTP route path.|
|» script_path|body|string|true|Path to the script or flow to execute when a message is received|

|» kafka_resource_path|body|string|true|Path to the Kafka resource containing connection configuration|

|» filters|body|[[TriggerFilter](#schematriggerfilter)]|true|Filters to match incoming messages (only matching messages trigger the script). Each entry is either a leaf `{key, value}` (top-level field) or `{path, value}` (dotted path into nested objects), or a group `{any_of: [...]}` / `{all_of: [...]}` / `{none_of: [...]}` nesting more entries. Entries at the top level are combined with `filter_logic`.|
|» filter_logic|body|string|false|Logic to apply when evaluating the top-level filters. 'and' requires all of them to match, 'or' requires any of them to match. Nested `any_of`/`all_of`/`none_of` groups carry their own logic.|
|» auto_offset_reset|body|string|false|Initial offset behavior when consumer group has no committed offset.|
|» auto_commit|body|boolean|false|When true (default), offsets are committed automatically after receiving each message. When false, you must manually commit offsets using the commit_offsets endpoint.|
|» mode|body|[TriggerMode](#schematriggermode)|false|job trigger mode|
|» error_handler_path|body|string|false|Path to a script to run when the triggered job fails. A bare path, without the script/ or flow/ prefix a schedule error handler takes; it cannot be a flow.|

|» retry|body|[Retry](#schemaretry)|false|Retry configuration for failed executions|
|» permissioned_as|body|string|false|The user or group this trigger runs as. Used during deployment to preserve the original trigger owner.|
|» preserve_permissioned_as|body|boolean|false|When true and the caller is a member of the 'wm_deployers' group, preserves the original permissioned_as value instead of overwriting it.|
|» labels|body|[string]|false|none|

|» filter_logic|or|
|» auto_offset_reset|latest|
|» auto_offset_reset|earliest|
|» mode|enabled|
|» mode|disabled|
|» mode|suspended|

|kafka_resource_path|string|true|none|Path to the Kafka resource containing connection configuration|
|group_id|string|true|none|Kafka consumer group ID for this trigger|

|auto_commit|boolean|false|none|When true (default), offsets are committed automatically after receiving each message. When false, you must manually commit offsets using the commit_offsets endpoint.|
|server_id|string|false|none|ID of the server currently handling this trigger (internal)|
|last_server_ping|string(date-time)|false|none|Timestamp of last server heartbeat (internal)|
|error|string|false|none|Last error message if the trigger failed|
|error_handler_path|string|false|none|Path to a script to run when the triggered job fails. A bare path, without the script/ or flow/ prefix a schedule error handler takes; it cannot be a flow.|
|error_handler_args|[ScriptArgs](#schemascriptargs)|false|none|Arguments to pass to the error handler|
|retry|[Retry](#schemaretry)|false|none|Retry configuration for failed executions|
|is_draft|boolean|true|none|none|
|draft_saved_at|string(date-time)|false|none|none|
|draft_base|string|false|none|The deployed version the draft forked from, as text whatever the<br>kind (script hash, flow version id, app version id). Compare to the<br>deployed head to tell a draft that is behind. Absent when there is<br>no draft or it was never forked from a deploy.<br>|
|no_deployed|boolean|false|none|none|
|draft|object|false|none|none|
|other_drafts_users|[object]|false|none|Other workspace users (and the legacy NULL-email row, if any)<br>with a saved draft at the same path. Populated only on the<br>authed user's "get by path" responses for kinds the editor<br>surfaces a fork banner for (script, flow, app, raw_app).<br>Empty / omitted for kinds without that UI.<br>|
|» username|string \| null|false|none|Workspace username of the draft owner. `null` represents<br>the legacy workspace-level (NULL-email) row. Emails never<br>leave the server.<br>|
|» draft_saved_at|string(date-time)|true|none|When this user's draft was last saved (`draft.created_at`),<br>surfaced in the fork modal as "Last updated".<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|mode|enabled|
|mode|disabled|
|mode|suspended|
|filter_logic|and|
|filter_logic|or|
|auto_offset_reset|latest|
|auto_offset_reset|earliest|

|error|string|false|none|Last error message if the trigger failed|
|error_handler_path|string|false|none|Path to a script to run when the triggered job fails. A bare path, without the script/ or flow/ prefix a schedule error handler takes; it cannot be a flow.|
|error_handler_args|[ScriptArgs](#schemascriptargs)|false|none|Arguments to pass to the error handler|
|retry|[Retry](#schemaretry)|false|none|Retry configuration for failed executions|
|is_draft|boolean|true|none|none|
|draft_saved_at|string(date-time)|false|none|none|
|draft_base|string|false|none|The deployed version the draft forked from, as text whatever the<br>kind (script hash, flow version id, app version id). Compare to the<br>deployed head to tell a draft that is behind. Absent when there is<br>no draft or it was never forked from a deploy.<br>|
|no_deployed|boolean|false|none|none|
|draft|object|false|none|none|
|other_drafts_users|[object]|false|none|Other workspace users (and the legacy NULL-email row, if any)<br>with a saved draft at the same path. Populated only on the<br>authed user's "get by path" responses for kinds the editor<br>surfaces a fork banner for (script, flow, app, raw_app).<br>Empty / omitted for kinds without that UI.<br>|
|» username|string \| null|false|none|Workspace username of the draft owner. `null` represents<br>the legacy workspace-level (NULL-email) row. Emails never<br>leave the server.<br>|
|» draft_saved_at|string(date-time)|true|none|When this user's draft was last saved (`draft.created_at`),<br>surfaced in the fork modal as "Last updated".<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|mode|enabled|
|mode|disabled|
|mode|suspended|

bearerAuth, cookieAuth

## create native trigger

<a id="opIdcreateNativeTrigger"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/native_triggers/nextcloud/create \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "script_path": "string",
    "is_flow": true,
    "service_config": {},
    "summary": "string",
    "enabled": true,
    "connection_path": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /w/{workspace}/native_triggers/{service_name}/create`

Creates a new native trigger for the specified service.
Requires write access to the script or flow that the trigger will be associated with.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "script_path": "string",
  "is_flow": true,
  "service_config": {},
  "summary": "string",
  "enabled": true,
  "connection_path": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-native-trigger-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|service_name|path|[NativeServiceName](#schemanativeservicename)|true|none|
|body|body|[NativeTriggerData](#schemanativetriggerdata)|true|new native trigger configuration|
|» script_path|body|string|true|The path to the script or flow that will be triggered|
|» is_flow|body|boolean|true|Whether the trigger targets a flow (true) or a script (false)|
|» service_config|body|object|true|Service-specific configuration (e.g., event types, filters)|
|» summary|body|string \| null|false|Short summary to be displayed when listed|
|» enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether the trigger starts a job when it fires. Honoured on create only, so a trigger can be registered already paused; an update ignores it and setenabled is the only way to change an existing trigger's state. Defaults to true.|
|» connection_path|body|string \| null|false|Path of the connection the trigger acts through. Honoured on create only; an update keeps the trigger's connection. When omitted on create, the caller's only usable connection for the service is used.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|service_name|nextcloud|
|service_name|google|
|service_name|github|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "external_id": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-native-trigger-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|native trigger created|[CreateTriggerResponse](#schemacreatetriggerresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

|» service_config|body|object|true|Service-specific configuration (e.g., event types, filters)|
|» summary|body|string \| null|false|Short summary to be displayed when listed|
|» enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether the trigger starts a job when it fires. Honoured on create only, so a trigger can be registered already paused; an update ignores it and setenabled is the only way to change an existing trigger's state. Defaults to true.|
|» connection_path|body|string \| null|false|Path of the connection the trigger acts through. Honoured on create only; an update keeps the trigger's connection. When omitted on create, the caller's only usable connection for the service is used.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|service_name|nextcloud|
|service_name|google|
|service_name|github|

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|native trigger updated|Inline|

bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

## create mqtt trigger

<a id="opIdcreateMqttTrigger"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/mqtt_triggers/create \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "mqtt_resource_path": "string",
    "subscribe_topics": [
      {
        "qos": "qos0",
        "topic": "string"
      }
    ],
    "client_id": "string",
    "v3_config": {
      "clean_session": true
    },
    "v5_config": {
      "clean_start": true,
      "topic_alias_maximum": 0,
      "session_expiry_interval": 0
    },
    "client_version": "v3",
    "path": "string",
    "script_path": "string",
    "is_flow": true,
    "mode": "enabled",
    "error_handler_path": "string",
    "error_handler_args": {},
    "retry": {
      "constant": {
        "attempts": 0,
        "seconds": 0
      },
      "exponential": {
        "attempts": 0,
        "multiplier": 0,
        "seconds": 1,
        "random_factor": 0
      },
      "retry_if": {
        "expr": "string"
      }
    },
    "permissioned_as": "string",
    "preserve_permissioned_as": true,
    "labels": [
      "string"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /w/{workspace}/mqtt_triggers/create`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "mqtt_resource_path": "string",
  "subscribe_topics": [
    {
      "qos": "qos0",
      "topic": "string"
    }
  ],
  "client_id": "string",
  "v3_config": {
    "clean_session": true
  },
  "v5_config": {
    "clean_start": true,
    "topic_alias_maximum": 0,
    "session_expiry_interval": 0
  },
  "client_version": "v3",
  "path": "string",
  "script_path": "string",
  "is_flow": true,
  "mode": "enabled",
  "error_handler_path": "string",
  "error_handler_args": {},
  "retry": {
    "constant": {
      "attempts": 0,
      "seconds": 0
    },
    "exponential": {
      "attempts": 0,
      "multiplier": 0,
      "seconds": 1,
      "random_factor": 0
    },
    "retry_if": {
      "expr": "string"
    }
  },
  "permissioned_as": "string",
  "preserve_permissioned_as": true,
  "labels": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-mqtt-trigger-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[NewMqttTrigger](#schemanewmqtttrigger)|true|new mqtt trigger|
|» mqtt_resource_path|body|string|true|Path to the MQTT resource containing broker connection configuration|
|» subscribe_topics|body|[[MqttSubscribeTopic](#schemamqttsubscribetopic)]|true|Array of MQTT topics to subscribe to, each with topic name and QoS level|
|» client_id|body|string \| null|false|MQTT client ID for this connection|
|» v3_config|body|[MqttV3Config](#schemamqttv3config)|false|MQTT v3 specific configuration (clean_session)|
|» v5_config|body|[MqttV5Config](#schemamqttv5config)|false|MQTT v5 specific configuration (clean_start, topic_alias_maximum, session_expiry_interval)|
|» client_version|body|[MqttClientVersion](#schemamqttclientversion)|false|MQTT protocol version ('v3' or 'v5')|
|» path|body|string|true|The unique Windmill path for this trigger. Must be of the form `u/<user>/<path>` or `f/<folder>/<path>`. This is the trigger object path, not the HTTP route path.|
|» script_path|body|string|true|Path to the script or flow to execute when a message is received|
|» is_flow|body|boolean|true|True if script_path points to a flow, false if it points to a script|
|» mode|body|[TriggerMode](#schematriggermode)|false|job trigger mode|
|» error_handler_path|body|string|false|Path to a script to run when the triggered job fails. A bare path, without the script/ or flow/ prefix a schedule error handler takes; it cannot be a flow.|
|» error_handler_args|body|[ScriptArgs](#schemascriptargs)|false|Arguments to pass to the error handler|
|» retry|body|[Retry](#schemaretry)|false|Retry configuration for failed executions|
|» permissioned_as|body|string|false|The user or group this trigger runs as. Used during deployment to preserve the original trigger owner.|
|» preserve_permissioned_as|body|boolean|false|When true and the caller is a member of the 'wm_deployers' group, preserves the original permissioned_as value instead of overwriting it.|
|» labels|body|[string]|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|

|» client_version|v3|
|» client_version|v5|
|» mode|enabled|
|» mode|disabled|
|» mode|suspended|

|server_id|string|false|none|ID of the server currently handling this trigger (internal)|
|last_server_ping|string(date-time)|false|none|Timestamp of last server heartbeat (internal)|
|error|string|false|none|Last error message if the trigger failed|
|error_handler_path|string|false|none|Path to a script to run when the triggered job fails. A bare path, without the script/ or flow/ prefix a schedule error handler takes; it cannot be a flow.|
|error_handler_args|[ScriptArgs](#schemascriptargs)|false|none|Arguments to pass to the error handler|
|retry|[Retry](#schemaretry)|false|none|Retry configuration for failed executions|
|is_draft|boolean|true|none|none|
|draft_saved_at|string(date-time)|false|none|none|

|no_deployed|boolean|false|none|none|
|draft|object|false|none|none|
|other_drafts_users|[object]|false|none|Other workspace users (and the legacy NULL-email row, if any)<br>with a saved draft at the same path. Populated only on the<br>authed user's "get by path" responses for kinds the editor<br>surfaces a fork banner for (script, flow, app, raw_app).<br>Empty / omitted for kinds without that UI.<br>|

|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|path|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[GcpTriggerData](#schemagcptriggerdata)|true|updated trigger|
|» gcp_resource_path|body|string|false|Path to the GCP resource containing service account credentials for authentication. Omit to authenticate with the instance's application default credentials, which only workspace admins may select.|
|» project_id|body|string|false|GCP project the client operates in. Defaults to the project of the credentials. Topics and subscriptions given as fully qualified names are reached whatever it is.|
|» subscription_mode|body|[SubscriptionMode](#schemasubscriptionmode)|true|The mode of subscription. 'existing' means using an existing GCP subscription, while 'create_update' involves creating or updating a new subscription.|
|» topic_id|body|string|true|Google Cloud Pub/Sub topic ID to subscribe to. Accepts a bare ID or a fully qualified name (projects/<project>/topics/<id>).|
|» subscription_id|body|string|false|Google Cloud Pub/Sub subscription ID. Accepts a bare ID or a fully qualified name (projects/<project>/subscriptions/<id>).|
|» base_endpoint|body|string|false|Base URL for push delivery endpoint.|
|» delivery_type|body|[DeliveryType](#schemadeliverytype)|false|Delivery mode for messages. 'push' for HTTP push delivery where messages are sent to a webhook endpoint, 'pull' for polling where the trigger actively fetches messages.|
|» delivery_config|body|[PushConfig](#schemapushconfig)|false|Configuration for push delivery mode.|
|» path|body|string|true|The unique Windmill path for this trigger. Must be of the form `u/<user>/<path>` or `f/<folder>/<path>`. This is the trigger object path, not the HTTP route path.|
|» script_path|body|string|true|Path to the script or flow to execute when a message is received.|
|» is_flow|body|boolean|true|True if script_path points to a flow, false if it points to a script.|
|» mode|body|[TriggerMode](#schematriggermode)|false|job trigger mode|
|» auto_acknowledge_msg|body|boolean|false|If true, automatically acknowledge messages after processing.|
|» ack_deadline|body|integer(int32)|false|Time in seconds within which the message must be acknowledged. If not provided, defaults to the subscription's acknowledgment deadline (600 seconds).|
|» error_handler_path|body|string|false|Path to a script or flow to run when the triggered job fails.|
|» error_handler_args|body|[ScriptArgs](#schemascriptargs)|false|Arguments to pass to the error handler.|
|» retry|body|[Retry](#schemaretry)|false|Retry configuration for failed executions.|
|» permissioned_as|body|string|false|The user or group this trigger runs as. Used during deployment to preserve the original trigger owner.|
|» preserve_permissioned_as|body|boolean|false|When true and the caller is a member of the 'wm_deployers' group, preserves the original permissioned_as value instead of overwriting it.|
|» labels|body|[string]|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|

|» subscription_mode|existing|
|» subscription_mode|create_update|
|» delivery_type|push|
|» delivery_type|pull|
|» mode|enabled|
|» mode|disabled|
|» mode|suspended|

|» **additionalProperties**|boolean|false|none|none|

|is_flow|boolean|true|none|True if script_path points to a flow, false if it points to a script|
|mode|[TriggerMode](#schematriggermode)|true|none|Trigger mode (enabled/disabled)|
|labels|[string]|false|none|none|
|draft_only|boolean|false|none|True when this row is a per-user draft with no deployed<br>trigger at the same path. Set by list endpoints when<br>`include_draft_only=true` synthesizes the row from the<br>draft. Frontend renders a "Draft" badge.<br>|
|is_draft|boolean|true|none|True when the authed user has a per-user draft at this path<br>(over a deployed row or a synthesized draft-only row).<br>Frontend appends a `*` to the displayed name.<br>|
|gcp_resource_path|string|false|none|Path to the GCP resource containing service account credentials for authentication. Omit to authenticate with the instance's application default credentials.|
|project_id|string|false|none|GCP project the client operates in. Defaults to the project of the credentials. Topics and subscriptions given as fully qualified names are reached whatever it is.|
|topic_id|string|true|none|Google Cloud Pub/Sub topic ID to subscribe to. Accepts a bare ID or a fully qualified name (projects/<project>/topics/<id>).|
|subscription_id|string|true|none|Google Cloud Pub/Sub subscription ID. Accepts a bare ID or a fully qualified name (projects/<project>/subscriptions/<id>).|
|server_id|string|false|none|ID of the server currently handling this trigger (internal use).|
|delivery_type|[DeliveryType](#schemadeliverytype)|true|none|Delivery mode for messages. 'push' for HTTP push delivery where messages are sent to a webhook endpoint, 'pull' for polling where the trigger actively fetches messages.|
|delivery_config|[PushConfig](#schemapushconfig)|false|none|Configuration for push delivery mode.|
|subscription_mode|[SubscriptionMode](#schemasubscriptionmode)|true|none|The mode of subscription. 'existing' means using an existing GCP subscription, while 'create_update' involves creating or updating a new subscription.|
|last_server_ping|string(date-time)|false|none|Timestamp of last server heartbeat (internal use).|
|error|string|false|none|Last error message if the trigger failed.|
|error_handler_path|string|false|none|Path to a script or flow to run when the triggered job fails.|
|error_handler_args|[ScriptArgs](#schemascriptargs)|false|none|Arguments to pass to the error handler.|
|retry|[Retry](#schemaretry)|false|none|Retry configuration for failed executions.|
|is_draft|boolean|true|none|none|
|draft_saved_at|string(date-time)|false|none|none|
|draft_base|string|false|none|The deployed version the draft forked from, as text whatever the<br>kind (script hash, flow version id, app version id). Compare to the<br>deployed head to tell a draft that is behind. Absent when there is<br>no draft or it was never forked from a deploy.<br>|
|no_deployed|boolean|false|none|none|
|draft|object|false|none|none|
|other_drafts_users|[object]|false|none|Other workspace users (and the legacy NULL-email row, if any)<br>with a saved draft at the same path. Populated only on the<br>authed user's "get by path" responses for kinds the editor<br>surfaces a fork banner for (script, flow, app, raw_app).<br>Empty / omitted for kinds without that UI.<br>|
|» username|string \| null|false|none|Workspace username of the draft owner. `null` represents<br>the legacy workspace-level (NULL-email) row. Emails never<br>leave the server.<br>|
|» draft_saved_at|string(date-time)|true|none|When this user's draft was last saved (`draft.created_at`),<br>surfaced in the fork modal as "Last updated".<br>|

|delivery_type|pull|
|subscription_mode|existing|
|subscription_mode|create_update|

<h3 id="get-an-azure-event-grid-trigger-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|path|string|true|none|The unique Windmill path for this trigger. Must be of the form `u/<user>/<path>` or `f/<folder>/<path>`. This is the trigger object path, not the HTTP route path.|
|script_path|string|true|none|Path to the script or flow to execute when triggered|
|permissioned_as|string|true|none|The user or group this trigger runs as (permissioned_as)|
|extra_perms|object|true|none|Additional permissions for this trigger|
|» **additionalProperties**|boolean|false|none|none|
|workspace_id|string|true|none|The workspace this trigger belongs to|
|edited_by|string|true|none|Username of the last person who edited this trigger|
|edited_at|string(date-time)|true|none|Timestamp of the last edit|
|is_flow|boolean|true|none|True if script_path points to a flow, false if it points to a script|
|mode|[TriggerMode](#schematriggermode)|true|none|Trigger mode (enabled/disabled)|
|labels|[string]|false|none|none|
|draft_only|boolean|false|none|True when this row is a per-user draft with no deployed<br>trigger at the same path. Set by list endpoints when<br>`include_draft_only=true` synthesizes the row from the<br>draft. Frontend renders a "Draft" badge.<br>|
|is_draft|boolean|true|none|True when the authed user has a per-user draft at this path<br>(over a deployed row or a synthesized draft-only row).<br>Frontend appends a `*` to the displayed name.<br>|
|azure_resource_path|string|true|none|none|
|azure_mode|[AzureMode](#schemaazuremode)|true|none|Azure Event Grid trigger mode.|
|scope_resource_id|string|true|none|ARM resource ID of the topic (basic) or namespace (namespace modes).|
|topic_name|string \| null|false|none|Topic name within the namespace (namespace modes only).|
|subscription_name|string|true|none|none|
|event_type_filters|[string]|false|none|none|
|server_id|string|false|none|none|
|last_server_ping|string(date-time)|false|none|none|
|error|string|false|none|none|
|error_handler_path|string|false|none|none|
|error_handler_args|[ScriptArgs](#schemascriptargs)|false|none|The arguments to pass to the script or flow|
|retry|[Retry](#schemaretry)|false|none|Retry configuration for failed module executions|
|is_draft|boolean|true|none|none|
|draft_saved_at|string(date-time)|false|none|none|
|draft_base|string|false|none|The deployed version the draft forked from, as text whatever the<br>kind (script hash, flow version id, app version id). Compare to the<br>deployed head to tell a draft that is behind. Absent when there is<br>no draft or it was never forked from a deploy.<br>|
|no_deployed|boolean|false|none|none|
|draft|object|false|none|none|
|other_drafts_users|[object]|false|none|Other workspace users (and the legacy NULL-email row, if any)<br>with a saved draft at the same path. Populated only on the<br>authed user's "get by path" responses for kinds the editor<br>surfaces a fork banner for (script, flow, app, raw_app).<br>Empty / omitted for kinds without that UI.<br>|
|» username|string \| null|false|none|Workspace username of the draft owner. `null` represents<br>the legacy workspace-level (NULL-email) row. Emails never<br>leave the server.<br>|
|» draft_saved_at|string(date-time)|true|none|When this user's draft was last saved (`draft.created_at`),<br>surfaced in the fork modal as "Last updated".<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|mode|enabled|
|mode|disabled|
|mode|suspended|
|azure_mode|basic_push|
|azure_mode|namespace_push|
|azure_mode|namespace_pull|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

|labels|[string]|false|none|none|

|publication_name|string|true|none|Name of the PostgreSQL publication to subscribe to for change data capture|
|server_id|string|false|none|ID of the server currently handling this trigger (internal)|
|replication_slot_name|string|true|none|Name of the PostgreSQL logical replication slot to use|
|error|string|false|none|Last error message if the trigger failed|
|last_server_ping|string(date-time)|false|none|Timestamp of last server heartbeat (internal)|

|retry|[Retry](#schemaretry)|false|none|Retry configuration for failed executions|
|is_draft|boolean|true|none|none|
|draft_saved_at|string(date-time)|false|none|none|
|draft_base|string|false|none|The deployed version the draft forked from, as text whatever the<br>kind (script hash, flow version id, app version id). Compare to the<br>deployed head to tell a draft that is behind. Absent when there is<br>no draft or it was never forked from a deploy.<br>|
|no_deployed|boolean|false|none|none|
|draft|object|false|none|none|
|other_drafts_users|[object]|false|none|Other workspace users (and the legacy NULL-email row, if any)<br>with a saved draft at the same path. Populated only on the<br>authed user's "get by path" responses for kinds the editor<br>surfaces a fork banner for (script, flow, app, raw_app).<br>Empty / omitted for kinds without that UI.<br>|
|» username|string \| null|false|none|Workspace username of the draft owner. `null` represents<br>the legacy workspace-level (NULL-email) row. Emails never<br>leave the server.<br>|
|» draft_saved_at|string(date-time)|true|none|When this user's draft was last saved (`draft.created_at`),<br>surfaced in the fork modal as "Last updated".<br>|

<h3 id="get-email-trigger-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|path|string|true|none|The unique Windmill path for this trigger. Must be of the form `u/<user>/<path>` or `f/<folder>/<path>`. This is the trigger object path, not the HTTP route path.|
|script_path|string|true|none|Path to the script or flow to execute when triggered|
|permissioned_as|string|true|none|The user or group this trigger runs as (permissioned_as)|
|extra_perms|object|true|none|Additional permissions for this trigger|
|» **additionalProperties**|boolean|false|none|none|
|workspace_id|string|true|none|The workspace this trigger belongs to|
|edited_by|string|true|none|Username of the last person who edited this trigger|
|edited_at|string(date-time)|true|none|Timestamp of the last edit|
|is_flow|boolean|true|none|True if script_path points to a flow, false if it points to a script|
|mode|[TriggerMode](#schematriggermode)|true|none|Trigger mode (enabled/disabled)|
|labels|[string]|false|none|none|
|draft_only|boolean|false|none|True when this row is a per-user draft with no deployed<br>trigger at the same path. Set by list endpoints when<br>`include_draft_only=true` synthesizes the row from the<br>draft. Frontend renders a "Draft" badge.<br>|
|is_draft|boolean|true|none|True when the authed user has a per-user draft at this path<br>(over a deployed row or a synthesized draft-only row).<br>Frontend appends a `*` to the displayed name.<br>|
|local_part|string|true|none|none|
|workspaced_local_part|boolean|false|none|none|
|error_handler_path|string|false|none|none|
|error_handler_args|[ScriptArgs](#schemascriptargs)|false|none|The arguments to pass to the script or flow|
|retry|[Retry](#schemaretry)|false|none|Retry configuration for failed module executions|
|is_draft|boolean|true|none|none|
|draft_saved_at|string(date-time)|false|none|none|
|draft_base|string|false|none|The deployed version the draft forked from, as text whatever the<br>kind (script hash, flow version id, app version id). Compare to the<br>deployed head to tell a draft that is behind. Absent when there is<br>no draft or it was never forked from a deploy.<br>|
|no_deployed|boolean|false|none|none|
|draft|object|false|none|none|
|other_drafts_users|[object]|false|none|Other workspace users (and the legacy NULL-email row, if any)<br>with a saved draft at the same path. Populated only on the<br>authed user's "get by path" responses for kinds the editor<br>surfaces a fork banner for (script, flow, app, raw_app).<br>Empty / omitted for kinds without that UI.<br>|
|» username|string \| null|false|none|Workspace username of the draft owner. `null` represents<br>the legacy workspace-level (NULL-email) row. Emails never<br>leave the server.<br>|
|» draft_saved_at|string(date-time)|true|none|When this user's draft was last saved (`draft.created_at`),<br>surfaced in the fork modal as "Last updated".<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|mode|enabled|
|mode|disabled|
|mode|suspended|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

## Get the concurrency key for a job that has concurrency limits enabled

<a id="opIdgetConcurrencyKey"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/concurrency_groups/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/key \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /concurrency_groups/{id}/key`

Requires read access to the job, the same as reading the run itself. Returns 403 for a workspace member who cannot see the run, and 404 when the caller is not a member of the job's workspace.

<h3 id="get-the-concurrency-key-for-a-job-that-has-concurrency-limits-enabled-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|

> 200 Response

```json
"string"
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|concurrency key for given job|Inline|

<aside class="warning">

bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

## Get intervals of job runtime concurrency

<a id="opIdlistExtendedJobs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/concurrency_groups/list_jobs \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /w/{workspace}/concurrency_groups/list_jobs`

<h3 id="get-intervals-of-job-runtime-concurrency-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|concurrency_key|query|string|false|none|
|row_limit|query|number|false|none|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|created_by|query|string|false|filter by exact matching user creator. Supports comma-separated list (e.g. 'alice,bob') and negation by prefixing all values with '!' (e.g. '!alice,!bob')|
|label|query|string|false|filter by exact matching job label. Supports comma-separated list (e.g. 'deploy,release') and negation by prefixing all values with '!' (e.g. '!deploy,!release')|
|parent_job|query|string(uuid)|false|The parent job that is at the origin and responsible for the execution of this script if any|
|script_path_exact|query|string|false|filter by exact matching script path. Supports comma-separated list (e.g. 'f/script1,f/script2') and negation by prefixing all values with '!' (e.g. '!f/script1,!f/script2')|
|script_path_start|query|string|false|filter by script path prefix. Supports comma-separated list (e.g. 'f/folder1,f/folder2') and negation by prefixing all values with '!' (e.g. '!f/folder1,!f/folder2')|
|schedule_path|query|string|false|mask to filter by schedule path|
|script_hash|query|string|false|mask to filter exact matching path|
|started_before|query|string(date-time)|false|filter on started before (inclusive) timestamp|
|started_after|query|string(date-time)|false|filter on started after (exclusive) timestamp|
|running|query|boolean|false|filter on running jobs|
|scheduled_for_before_now|query|boolean|false|filter on jobs scheduled_for before now (hence waitinf for a worker)|
|completed_before|query|string(date-time)|false|filter on started before (inclusive) timestamp|
|completed_after|query|string(date-time)|false|filter on started after (exclusive) timestamp|
|created_before_queue|query|string(date-time)|false|filter on jobs created before X for jobs in the queue only|
|created_after_queue|query|string(date-time)|false|filter on jobs created after X for jobs in the queue only|
|job_kinds|query|string|false|filter by job kind. Supports comma-separated list of values ('preview', 'script', 'dependencies', 'flow') and negation by prefixing all values with '!' (e.g. '!preview,!dependencies')|
|args|query|string|false|filter on jobs containing those args as a json subset (@> in postgres)|
|tag|query|string|false|filter by tag/worker group. Supports comma-separated list (e.g. 'gpu,highmem') and negation by prefixing all values with '!' (e.g. '!gpu,!highmem')|
|result|query|string|false|filter on jobs containing those result as a json subset (@> in postgres)|
|allow_wildcards|query|boolean|false|allow wildcards (*) in the filter of label, tag, worker|
|page|query|integer|false|which page to return (start at 1, default 1)|
|per_page|query|integer|false|number of items to return for a given page (default 30, max 100)|
|trigger_kind|query|string|false|filter by trigger kind. Supports comma-separated list (e.g. 'schedule,webhook') and negation by prefixing all values with '!' (e.g. '!schedule,!webhook')|
|is_skipped|query|boolean|false|is the job skipped|
|resolved|query|boolean|false|filter on whether a failed or canceled run has been marked as handled. true keeps only resolved runs, false hides them|
|is_flow_step|query|boolean|false|is the job a flow step|
|has_null_parent|query|boolean|false|has null parent|
|success|query|boolean|false|filter on successful jobs|
|status|query|string|false|filter on the exact completed job status. Unlike `success=true` (which also matches `skipped`), `status=success` matches only `success`.|
|all_workspaces|query|boolean|false|get jobs from all workspaces (only valid if request come from the `admins` workspace)|
|is_not_schedule|query|boolean|false|is not a scheduled job|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|status|success|
|status|failure|
|status|canceled|
|status|skipped|

## Get the workspace-wide asset &lt;-&gt; runnable graph

<a id="opIdgetAssetsGraph"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/assets/graph \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /w/{workspace}/assets/graph`

<h3 id="get-the-workspace-wide-asset---runnable-graph-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|asset_kinds|query|string|false|Filter by asset kinds (comma-separated list)|
|folder|query|string|false|Scope the graph to runnables in a single folder|
|dbt_script_hash|query|string|false|Render the dbt half of the graph as one version of a dbt script had it, rather than as the currently deployed one. Given this, `folder` no longer scopes the dbt nodes: the pinned version's own models and lineage are the answer, including models a later deploy removed.<br>|

```json
        "materialize_strategy": "string",
        "tags": [
          "string"
        ],
        "description": "string",
        "data_tests": [
          {
            "kind": "string",
            "column": "string",
            "args": {},
            "severity": "string"
          }
        ],
        "columns": {},
        "column_schema": [
          {
            "name": "string",
            "type": "string"
          }
        ],
        "freshness": {},
        "raw_code": "string",
        "original_file_path": "string"
      }
    }
  ],
  "runnables": [
    {
      "path": "string",
      "usage_kind": "script",
      "in_pipeline": true,
      "macros": [
        {
          "name": "string",
          "params": "string",
          "is_table": true
        }
      ],
      "dbt": {
        "model_count": 0
      }
    }
  ],
  "edges": [
    {
```

## Column-level lineage of a set of dbt relations

<a id="opIdgetDbtColumnLineage"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/assets/column_lineage?asset_path=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /w/{workspace}/assets/column_lineage`

The direct (`copy` / `mod`) column-to-column lineage the given relations' columns sit in — the connected component around them, from the engine's static analysis. Not their own edges, which would stop one hop out since a column trace walks transitively, and not a whole project's, which carries model families the selection cannot reach.
Several relations, answered as one union, because one selection reaches several: a script's output column can derive from columns of several dbt models. Unpinned, the component crosses projects — a relation one project produces is another's source — and the caller's access is decided again for every project it reaches, so a trace ends where their grants do. A pinned answer, by version here or by job on the run route, is one project's.
Its own endpoint rather than a field on the asset graph: the graph is folder-wide and polled by a run page, while this is rendered for one selection at a time. Empty for projects that did not opt into the analysis pass (`column_lineage: true`), which is the ordinary case. The indirect `scan` kind is stored but never served: it reaches every output column of its model.


<h3 id="column-level-lineage-of-a-set-of-dbt-relations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|asset_path|query|[string]|true|The `dbt://` relations whose lineage to return. Repeated, once per relation, and answered as one union. At least one, and at most 1000 — a request naming none, or more than that, is refused rather than answered with an empty component.<br>|
|dbt_script_hash|query|string|false|The deployed version a view is drawing, when it is drawing one — the dbt editor, which shows a single project as of a single deploy. A version-pinned answer is that version's project alone, the same as a job-pinned one, and only the unpinned answer crosses projects: a pin says which stored graph is on screen, and another project's live graph is not part of it.<br>A run's or an editor buffer's own graph is not reachable here: that pins to a job, and costs the job-read gate — see `jobs/dbt_column_lineage/{id}`.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "edges": [
    {
      "from_asset_path": "string",
      "from_column": "string",
      "to_asset_path": "string",
      "to_column": "string",
      "kind": "string"
    }
  ],
  "truncated": true
}
```

<h3 id="column-level-lineage-of-a-set-of-dbt-relations-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|the relations' column-level lineage|[DbtColumnLineage](#schemadbtcolumnlineage)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

approved projects are public, so it is optional here.

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|slug|path|string|true|hub project slug (3-50 chars, lowercase alphanumeric and hyphens, no leading/trailing hyphen)|
|folder|query|string|false|folder scoping the Hub project source (`{workspace}:{folder}`)|
|version|query|integer|false|id of a reviewed project version to export instead of the current one (see the hub's `/projects/{slug}/versions`)|

<h3 id="export-a-hub-project-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|raw Hub response body (status code is passed through from the Hub)|Inline|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

## set or clear a hub project's custom logo

<a id="opIdpublishHubProjectLogo"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/hub/projects/string/logo?folder=string' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "logo": {
      "b64": "string",
      "mime": "image/png"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /w/{workspace}/hub/projects/{slug}/logo`

Requires the caller to be a workspace admin. Sets the project's custom
logo (base64 png/svg, decoded size max 512KB) or clears it when `logo`
is null; the `logo` field itself is required so an empty body cannot
clear the logo by accident. Forwards the request to the configured Hub
scoped to the `{workspace}:{folder}` source and returns the Hub's
status code and raw response body.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "logo": {
    "b64": "string",
    "mime": "image/png"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="set-or-clear-a-hub-projects-custom-logo-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|
|slug|path|[HubProjectSlug](#schemahubprojectslug)|true|hub project slug|
|folder|query|string|true|workspace folder scoping the Hub publication: a workspace can publish<br>one Hub project per folder and the Hub-side source key is<br>`{workspace}:{folder}`<br>|
|body|body|[ProjectLogoBody](#schemaprojectlogobody)|true|none|
|» logo|body|object \| null|true|the logo to set, or null to clear the project's current logo|
|» » b64|body|string|true|base64-encoded image bytes (decoded size max 512KB)|
|» » mime|body|string|true|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » mime|image/png|
|» » mime|image/svg+xml|

<h3 id="set-or-clear-a-hub-projects-custom-logo-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|raw Hub response body (status code is passed through from the Hub)|Inline|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

## list the hub's published projects

<a id="opIdlistHubProjects"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/w/string/hub/projects \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /w/{workspace}/hub/projects`

Forwards to the configured Hub's public project catalogue and returns its
status code and raw response body. Readable by any workspace member: the
listing is not workspace-scoped, and it is proxied only because the Hub's
listing endpoint sends no CORS header. Refused with 400 when the instance
has the Hub disabled, in which case no outbound request is made.


<h3 id="list-the-hubs-published-projects-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|none|

<h3 id="list-the-hubs-published-projects-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|raw Hub response body (status code is passed through from the Hub)|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|the Hub is disabled on this instance|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, cookieAuth
</aside>

```json
{
  "assets": [
    {
      "kind": "s3object",
      "path": "string",

      "dbt": {
        "unique_id": "string",
        "resource_type": "model",

        ],

            "kind": "string",

            "args": {},

          }

        "columns": {},
        "column_schema": [
          {
            "name": "string",
            "type": "string"
          }
        ],
        "freshness": {},

        "original_file_path": "string"
      }
    }
  ],
  "runnables": [
    {
      "path": "string",
      "usage_kind": "script",
      "in_pipeline": true,
      "macros": [
        {
          "name": "string",
          "params": "string",
          "is_table": true
        }
      ],
      "dbt": {
        "model_count": 0
      }
    }
  ],
  "edges": [
    {
      "runnable_path": "string",
      "runnable_kind": "script",
      "asset_kind": "s3object",
      "asset_path": "string",
      "access_type": "r"
    }
  ],
  "triggers": [
    {
      "trigger_kind": "asset",
      "asset_kind": "s3object",
      "asset_path": "string",
      "runnable_kind": "script",
      "runnable_path": "string"
    }
  ],
  "macro_edges": [
    {
      "lib_path": "string",
      "consumer_path": "string",
      "macro_names": [
        "string"
      ],
      "via_use": true
    }
  ],
  "test_edges": [
    {
      "producer_kind": "script",
      "producer_path": "string",
      "runnable_kind": "script",
      "runnable_path": "string",
      "asset_kind": "s3object",
      "asset_path": "string"
    }
  ],
  "dbt_edges": [
    {
      "from_asset_path": "string",
      "to_asset_path": "string"
    }
  ],
  "dbt_snapshot_job": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "dbt_graph_ingested_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|assets|[object]|true|none|none|
|runnables|[object]|true|none|none|
|edges|[object]|true|none|none|
|triggers|[object]|true|none|none|
|macro_edges|[object]|false|none|Macro-library → consumer edges (deploy-recorded call detection plus `// use`). Omitted when empty.|
|test_edges|[object]|false|none|Ordering-only "must-run-after" edges — a `// data_test relationships` (or custom test reading a pipeline asset) requires the referenced asset's producer to run before the tested script. Not a data-consumption edge; fed into the cascade topo-sort so cold runs order correctly. Omitted when empty.|
|dbt_edges|[object]|false|none|`ref()` lineage BETWEEN two dbt models, in the terms the canvas draws — the relations, not dbt's node ids. Without it every model hangs off the one dbt runnable and the project reads as a flat fan-out. Omitted when empty.|
|dbt_snapshot_job|string(uuid)|false|none|The job whose own snapshot the dbt half was resolved from, when one was asked for and found. A run page polls the graph while its job runs, because a dynamic descriptor's snapshot is written mid-run, and this is what tells it to stop. Omitted when the answer came from the version's deployed graph.|
|dbt_graph_ingested_at|string(date-time)|false|none|When the dbt half on screen was parsed, for a graph pinned to a job. What the dbt editor labels its provenance with — "parsed from the editor at 14:32" against "as of last deploy" — since the two are drawn identically and the ambiguity would otherwise just move into the editor. Omitted for the unpinned workspace graph, which spans every project and so has no one time.|

<h2 id="tocS_DbtColumnLineage">DbtColumnLineage</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadbtcolumnlineage"></a>
<a id="schema_DbtColumnLineage"></a>
<a id="tocSdbtcolumnlineage"></a>
<a id="tocsdbtcolumnlineage"></a>

```json
{
  "edges": [
    {
      "from_asset_path": "string",
      "from_column": "string",
      "to_asset_path": "string",
      "to_column": "string",
      "kind": "string"
    }
  ],
  "truncated": true
}
```

The direct column-to-column lineage the asked-for relations' columns sit in — the connected component around them — in the terms the canvas draws: relations and columns, never dbt's node ids.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|edges|[object]|true|none|none|
|truncated|boolean|true|none|The component reaches further than `edges`, which holds the part nearest the asked-for relations. A trace that stops short is otherwise indistinguishable from one that ends.|

<h2 id="tocS_DbtAssetProvenance">DbtAssetProvenance</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadbtassetprovenance"></a>
<a id="schema_DbtAssetProvenance"></a>
<a id="tocSdbtassetprovenance"></a>
<a id="tocsdbtassetprovenance"></a>

```json
{
  "unique_id": "string",
  "resource_type": "model",
  "materialized": "string",
  "materialize_strategy": "string",
  "tags": [
    "string"
  ],
  "description": "string",
  "data_tests": [
    {
      "kind": "string",
      "column": "string",
      "args": {},
      "severity": "string"
    }
  ],
  "columns": {},
  "column_schema": [
    {
      "name": "string",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ],
  "freshness": {},
  "raw_code": "string",
  "original_file_path": "string"
}
```

What dbt says about the model, snapshot, seed or source that produces (or, for a source, is read at) this relation. A dbt project is one runnable node with many model assets, so per-model metadata belongs here rather than on the script.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|unique_id|string|true|none|dbt's own node id, e.g. `model.jaffle_shop.customers`.|
|resource_type|string|true|none|none|
|materialized|string|false|none|dbt's own word (`table`, `view`, `incremental`, `snapshot`).|
|materialize_strategy|string|false|none|The Windmill write strategy it maps to, absent for `view` and `ephemeral`, which have none.|
|tags|[string]|false|none|none|
|description|string|false|none|none|
|data_tests|[object]|false|none|none|
|columns|object|false|none|Declared column metadata (name -> description) — what `manifest.json` carries, which is only the columns an author wrote down. Omitted when the caller cannot read the script.|
|column_schema|[object]|false|none|Every column of the relation, typed and in the order the model produces them, from the engine's static analysis. Present only for a project that opted into it, and gated like `columns` and the model's SQL: a full column list is the shape of what the author wrote.|
|freshness|object|false|none|A source's declared freshness policy, for the staleness chip.|
|raw_code|string|false|none|The model's SQL as written, at the deploy this graph belongs to. Omitted when the caller cannot read the script.|
|original_file_path|string|false|none|Its path inside the dbt project, e.g. `models/staging/stg_orders.sql`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|resource_type|model|
|resource_type|snapshot|
|resource_type|seed|
|resource_type|source|

<h2 id="tocS_UserDraftOverlay">UserDraftOverlay</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemauserdraftoverlay"></a>
<a id="schema_UserDraftOverlay"></a>
<a id="tocSuserdraftoverlay"></a>
<a id="tocsuserdraftoverlay"></a>

```json
{
  "is_draft": true,
  "draft_saved_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "draft_base": "string",
  "no_deployed": true,
  "draft": {},
  "other_drafts_users": [
    {
      "username": "string",
      "draft_saved_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

Overlay fields added to every "get by path" response that accepts
the `get_draft` query parameter. The deployed payload is sent
untouched in the response body; the authed user's saved draft
for this path — whatever shape the editor wrote — is attached
as the sibling `draft` field when `get_draft=true` and a draft
exists. The frontend pairs the two to present diff / reset /
discard UI; the server never merges them.

When `no_deployed=true` there is no deployed row at this path —
the response body is a best-effort stand-in synthesized from
the draft, and only `draft` is canonical. Callers should disable
"diff vs deployed" UI in that case.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|is_draft|boolean|true|none|none|
|draft_saved_at|string(date-time)|false|none|none|
|draft_base|string|false|none|The deployed version the draft forked from, as text whatever the<br>kind (script hash, flow version id, app version id). Compare to the<br>deployed head to tell a draft that is behind. Absent when there is<br>no draft or it was never forked from a deploy.<br>|
|no_deployed|boolean|false|none|none|
|draft|object|false|none|none|
|other_drafts_users|[object]|false|none|Other workspace users (and the legacy NULL-email row, if any)<br>with a saved draft at the same path. Populated only on the<br>authed user's "get by path" responses for kinds the editor<br>surfaces a fork banner for (script, flow, app, raw_app).<br>Empty / omitted for kinds without that UI.<br>|

|schema|object|false|none|JSON Schema for flow inputs. Use this to define input parameters, their types, defaults, and validation. For resource inputs, set type to 'object' and format to 'resource-<type>' (e.g., 'resource-stripe')|
|on_behalf_of_email|string|false|none|Address of the account the flow runs on behalf of. Derived from on_behalf_of on read; accepted on write, where it is resolved to the account it names.|
|on_behalf_of|string|false|none|The flow runs with the permissions of this identity: u/{username}, g/{group}, or a bare email when the username is itself email-shaped. The only stored half of the identity; on_behalf_of_email is derived from it. Omit it when writing and it is resolved from that address instead.|

The flow structure containing modules and optional preprocessor/failure handlers

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|modules|[[FlowModule](#schemaflowmodule)]|true|none|Array of steps that execute in sequence. Each step can be a script, subflow, loop, or branch|
|failure_module|[FlowModule](#schemaflowmodule)|false|none|Special module that executes when the flow fails. Receives error object with message, name, stack, and step_id. Must have id 'failure'. Only supports script/rawscript types|
|preprocessor_module|[FlowModule](#schemaflowmodule)|false|none|Special module that runs before the first step on external triggers. Must have id 'preprocessor'. Only supports script/rawscript types. Cannot reference other step results|
|same_worker|boolean|false|none|If true, all steps run on the same worker for better performance|
|preserve_step_tags|boolean|false|none|If true and the flow runs on a custom worker tag, steps that declare their own non-empty tag run on it instead of inheriting the flow tag. Steps without their own tag still inherit the flow tag.|
|concurrent_limit|number|false|none|Maximum number of concurrent executions of this flow|
|concurrency_key|string|false|none|Expression to group concurrent executions (e.g., by user ID)|
|concurrency_time_window_s|number|false|none|Time window in seconds for concurrent_limit|
|debounce_delay_s|integer|false|none|Delay in seconds to debounce flow executions|
|debounce_key|string|false|none|Expression to group debounced executions|
|debounce_args_to_accumulate|[string]|false|none|Arguments to accumulate across debounced executions|
|max_total_debouncing_time|integer|false|none|Maximum total time in seconds that a job can be debounced|
|max_total_debounces_amount|integer|false|none|Maximum number of times a job can be debounced|
|skip_expr|string|false|none|JavaScript expression to conditionally skip the entire flow|
|cache_ttl|number|false|none|Cache duration in seconds for flow results|
|cache_ignore_s3_path|boolean|false|none|none|
|delete_after_secs|integer|false|none|If set, delete the flow job's args, result and logs after this many seconds following job completion|
|flow_env|object|false|none|Environment variables available to all steps. Values can be strings, JSON values, or special references: '$var:path' (workspace variable) or '$res:path' (resource).|
|priority|number|false|none|Execution priority (higher numbers run first)|
|early_return|string|false|none|Id of the step whose result a sync webhook returns as soon as that step completes, while the rest of the flow keeps running. When the step does not run, or fails while the flow has a failure module, the flow's final result is returned instead.|
|chat_input_enabled|boolean|false|none|Whether this flow accepts chat-style input|
|notes|[[FlowNote](#schemaflownote)]|false|none|Sticky notes attached to the flow|
|groups|[object]|false|none|Semantic groups of modules for organizational purposes|
