{
  "skip_if_stopped": true,
  "expr": "string",
  "error_message": "string",
  "error_include_result": true
}
```

Early termination condition for a module

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|skip_if_stopped|boolean|false|none|If true, following steps are skipped when this condition triggers|
|expr|string|true|none|JavaScript expression evaluated after the module runs. Can use 'result' (step's result) or 'flow_input'. Return true to stop|
|error_message|string \| null|false|none|Custom error message when stopping with an error. Mutually exclusive with skip_if_stopped. If set to a non-empty string, the flow stops with this error. If empty string, a default error message is used. If null or omitted, no error is raised.|
|error_include_result|boolean|false|none|When stopping with an error (error_message set), embed the stopping step's own result inside the raised error object (as error.result) instead of discarding it. The top-level result stays { error }. Defaults to false.|

A single step in a flow. Can be a script, subflow, loop, or branch

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for this step. Used to reference results via 'results.step_id'. Must be a valid identifier (alphanumeric, underscore, hyphen)|
|value|[FlowModuleValue](#schemaflowmodulevalue)|true|none|The actual implementation of a flow step. Can be a script (inline or referenced), subflow, loop, branch, or special module type|
|stop_after_if|[StopAfterIf](#schemastopafterif)|false|none|Early termination condition evaluated after this step completes|
|stop_after_all_iters_if|[StopAfterIf](#schemastopafterif)|false|none|For loops only - early termination condition evaluated after all iterations complete|
|skip_if|object|false|none|Conditionally skip this step based on previous results or flow inputs|
|sleep|[InputTransform](#schemainputtransform)|false|none|Delay after this step completes, before the next step starts (in seconds or as expression)|
|cache_ttl|number|false|none|Cache duration in seconds for this step's results|
|cache_ignore_s3_path|boolean|false|none|none|
|timeout|[InputTransform](#schemainputtransform)|false|none|Maximum execution time in seconds (static value or expression)|
|delete_after_secs|integer|false|none|If set, delete the step's args, result and logs after this many seconds following job completion|
|summary|string|false|none|Short description of what this step does|
|mock|object|false|none|Mock configuration for testing without executing the actual step|
|suspend|object|false|none|Configuration for approval/resume steps that wait for user input|
|priority|number|false|none|Execution priority for this step (higher numbers run first)|
|continue_on_error|boolean|false|none|If true, flow continues even if this step fails|
|job_token_scopes|[string]|false|none|Scopes the token of this step's jobs is restricted to (domain:action[:resource], e.g. oidc:write), on top of the flow's own restriction: a step can only narrow it. Applies to everything the step runs (loop and branch bodies, AI agent tools).|
|retry|[Retry](#schemaretry)|false|none|Retry configuration if this step fails|
|debouncing|object|false|none|Debounce configuration for this step (EE only)|

{
  "value": null,
  "type": "static"

```

Maps input parameters for a step. Can be a static value or a JavaScript expression that references previous results or flow inputs

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|[StaticTransform](#schemastatictransform)|false|none|Static value passed directly to the step. Use for hardcoded values or resource references like '$res:path/to/resource'|
|*oneOf*|[JavascriptTransform](#schemajavascripttransform)|false|none|JavaScript expression evaluated at runtime. Can reference previous step results via 'results.step_id' or flow inputs via 'flow_input.property'. Inside for loops, use 'flow_input.iter.value' for the current iteration value (in while loops it equals 'flow_input.iter.index')|
|*oneOf*|[AiTransform](#schemaaitransform)|false|none|Value resolved by the AI runtime for this input. The AI engine decides how to satisfy the parameter.|

Managed memory, stored by Windmill and replayed with each request. The memory is named by a memory id, see `memory_id`. While it is off, a step can supply its history in `previous_messages`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|No conversation memory/context|
|kind|string|true|none|none|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|Keeps the most recent messages of the memory named by the run's memory id (or the step's<br>`memory_id`). Without a memory id the agent runs without memory.<br>|
|kind|string|true|none|none|
|context_length|integer|true|none|Number of most recent messages to load and store. 0 turns memory off.|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|Keeps the whole memory named by the run's memory id (or the step's `memory_id`), replacing<br>its older part with a summary as the conversation approaches the model's context window.<br>Without a memory id the agent runs without memory, and compaction bounds the run's own loop.<br>|
|kind|string|true|none|none|
|context_window|integer|false|none|Overrides the context window looked up from the model, in tokens. Only a model<br>Windmill does not know needs one; those fall back to 128000.<br>|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|**Deprecated.** Deprecated, still read as it was written: the run's memory id, else the `memory_id` here.<br>The step's own `memory_id` is not read while this kind is set; switch the kind to `window`<br>to use it. Without a `context_length`, or with 0, it is `off` and reads `previous_messages`.<br>|
|kind|string|true|none|none|
|context_length|integer|false|none|Maximum number of messages to retain in context|
|memory_id|string|false|none|Identifier for persistent memory across agent invocations|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|**Deprecated.** Deprecated, still read as it was written. Move the step to `off` with `previous_messages` instead.|
|kind|string|true|none|none|
|messages|[object]|true|none|none|

The actual implementation of a flow step. Can be a script (inline or referenced), subflow, loop, branch, or special module type

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|[RawScript](#schemarawscript)|false|none|Inline script with code defined directly in the flow. Use 'bun' as default language if unspecified. The script receives arguments from input_transforms|
|*oneOf*|[PathScript](#schemapathscript)|false|none|Reference to an existing script by path. Use this when calling a previously saved script instead of writing inline code|
|*oneOf*|[PathFlow](#schemapathflow)|false|none|Reference to an existing flow by path. Use this to call another flow as a subflow|
|*oneOf*|[ForloopFlow](#schemaforloopflow)|false|none|Executes nested modules in a loop over an iterator. Inside the loop, use 'flow_input.iter.value' to access the current iteration value, and 'flow_input.iter.index' for the index. Supports parallel execution for better performance on I/O-bound operations|
|*oneOf*|[WhileloopFlow](#schemawhileloopflow)|false|none|Executes nested modules repeatedly until stopped. The implicit iterator is the iteration counter, so 'flow_input.iter.value' equals 'flow_input.iter.index' (0, 1, 2, ...) and never carries state. To carry state across iterations, a step reads its own previous-iteration result via 'results.<its_own_id>' with a first-iteration fallback - the loop's stop_after_if must then be on that inner step (a plain single-step body with stop_after_if on the loop module does not resolve 'results' across iterations and never terminates); plain counters can instead be derived from 'flow_input.iter.index', which works in every configuration. stop_after_if is evaluated after each iteration - on the loop module 'result' is the last iteration's result|
|*oneOf*|[BranchOne](#schemabranchone)|false|none|Conditional branching where only the first matching branch executes. Branches are evaluated in order, and the first one with a true expression runs. If no branches match, the default branch executes|
|*oneOf*|[BranchAll](#schemabranchall)|false|none|Parallel branching where all branches execute simultaneously. Unlike BranchOne, all branches run regardless of conditions. Useful for executing independent tasks concurrently|
|*oneOf*|[Identity](#schemaidentity)|false|none|Pass-through module that returns its input unchanged. Useful for flow structure or as a placeholder|
|*oneOf*|[AiAgent](#schemaaiagent)|false|none|AI agent step that can use tools to accomplish tasks. The agent receives inputs and can call any of its configured tools to complete the task|
|*oneOf*|[AiDecision](#schemaaidecision)|false|none|AI decision step: one call to a decision model (TypeSafe's Jev, Cloudflare's<br>Jev-compatible Clef, or OpenAI's Decisions API) that answers typed questions about a<br>state with calibrated probabilities, instead of generating text.<br>Prefer it over an AI agent to classify, route, score or check something: it is fast,<br>cheap and its answers are structured. Its result is { output: { <question name>: answer },<br>model, usage }, so a later step reads e.g. results.<id>.output.intent.choice. To route on<br>the answers, follow it with a branchone whose branch exprs read<br>results.<id>.output.<question>.choice. Usable as an AI agent tool, where the calling agent<br>supplies the state.<br>|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|type|string|true|none|none|
|tag|string|false|none|Worker group tag for execution routing. If not set, the AI agent step runs on the flow's tag (default `flow`)|
|omit_output_from_conversation|boolean|false|none|If true, this AI agent step does not persist its assistant or tool messages to the flow conversation when chat mode is enabled.|
|agent|string|false|none|Path of a reusable `ai_agent` resource (hybrid linking). When set, the agent brain<br>config (provider/model/system prompt/etc.) and tool set are resolved at runtime from<br>that resource; the module's input_transforms then only carry the flow-local inputs<br>(user_message, user_attachments, enabled_tools and the history inputs memory_id and previous_messages)<br>and, optionally, the `model` and `reasoning_effort` overrides of what the agent saved.<br>|
|tool_inputs|object|false|none|Host-local wiring for an agent's tool inputs, keyed by tool id then input key. Binds the<br>referenced agent's tools to this flow's context (flow_input/results) without mutating the<br>shared resource; overlaid onto the tools' input_transforms at runtime — including when<br>`agent` is unset, since a step forked for editing keeps these overrides until it is saved<br>back or unlinked.<br>|
|parallel|boolean|false|none|If true, the agent can execute multiple tool calls in parallel|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|aiagent|

<h2 id="tocS_AiDecision">AiDecision</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaaidecision"></a>
<a id="schema_AiDecision"></a>
<a id="tocSaidecision"></a>
<a id="tocsaidecision"></a>

```json
{
  "input_transforms": {
    "provider": {
      "value": {
        "kind": "openai",
        "resource": "string",
        "model": "string",
        "reasoning_effort": "string"
      },
      "type": "static"
    },
    "state": {
      "value": null,
      "type": "static"
    },
    "questions": {
      "value": null,
      "type": "static"
    }
  },
  "type": "aidecision",
  "tag": "string"
}
```

AI decision step: one call to a decision model (TypeSafe's Jev, Cloudflare's
Jev-compatible Clef, or OpenAI's Decisions API) that answers typed questions about a
state with calibrated probabilities, instead of generating text.
Prefer it over an AI agent to classify, route, score or check something: it is fast,
cheap and its answers are structured. Its result is { output: { <question name>: answer },
model, usage }, so a later step reads e.g. results.<id>.output.intent.choice. To route on
the answers, follow it with a branchone whose branch exprs read
results.<id>.output.<question>.choice. Usable as an AI agent tool, where the calling agent
supplies the state.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|input_transforms|object|true|none|Input parameters for the decision mapped to their values|
|type|string|true|none|none|
|tag|string|false|none|Worker group tag for execution routing. If not set, the step runs on the flow's tag (default `flow`)|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|aidecision|

<h2 id="tocS_VaultSettings">VaultSettings</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemavaultsettings"></a>
<a id="schema_VaultSettings"></a>
<a id="tocSvaultsettings"></a>
<a id="tocsvaultsettings"></a>

```json
{
  "address": "string",
  "mount_path": "string",
  "kv_secret_path_prefix": "string",
  "jwt_role": "string",
  "jwt_mount_path": "string",
  "approle_role_id": "string",
  "approle_mount_path": "string",
  "namespace": "string",
  "token": "string",
  "skip_ssl_verify": true
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|address|string|true|none|HashiCorp Vault server address (e.g., https://vault.company.com:8200)|
|mount_path|string|false|none|KV v2 secrets engine mount path (e.g., windmill). Empty to test the connection used for `$external:vault://` references, which checks only that Vault accepts Windmill's token.|
|kv_secret_path_prefix|string|false|none|Optional path prefix inserted between the KV data/metadata segment and the workspace id (e.g., "apps/windmill"). When set, secrets are stored at `<mount>/data/<prefix>/<workspace>/<secret>`, allowing a Vault policy scoped to exactly `<mount>/data/<prefix>/*`.|
|jwt_role|string|false|none|Vault JWT auth role name for Windmill (optional, if not provided token auth is used)|
|jwt_mount_path|string|false|none|Mount path for the JWT auth method in Vault (optional, defaults to "jwt"). Set this when the JWT auth method is mounted at a non-default path, e.g. via `vault auth enable -path=<mount> jwt`.|
|approle_role_id|string|false|none|AppRole role_id (optional). When set and no static token is given, Windmill logs in with AppRole; the secret_id is read from the `VAULT_APPROLE_SECRET_ID` environment variable of servers and workers.|
|approle_mount_path|string|false|none|Mount path of the AppRole auth method (optional, defaults to "approle").|
|namespace|string|false|none|Vault Enterprise namespace (optional)|
|token|string|false|none|Static Vault token for testing/development (optional, if provided this is used instead of JWT authentication)|
|skip_ssl_verify|boolean|false|none|Skip TLS certificate verification when connecting to Vault. Only use for self-signed certificates in development environments.|

|---|---|---|---|---|
|kind|string|true|none|`agent` runs the ai_agent resource as it is deployed when the run opens, `agent_draft` the caller's unsaved edits of it as the editor holds them (carried in `draft`), and `agent_version` one past version named by `version`. The first and last are read server-side; all three are inlined into the run, so every case of a run executes one configuration: a deploy part-way through changes what the next run measures, never this one.<br>|
|path|string|true|none|Path of the ai_agent resource.|
|version|integer(int64) \| null|false|none|The agent's per-path version number when the run opened: how many times the resource had been saved, not a resource_version row id. For `agent` and `agent_draft` it names the configuration the run read and every case executed. For `agent_version` it is the request's own, says which version to inline, and is required.<br>|
|draft|[AgentDraft](#schemaagentdraft)|false|none|The brain and tools of an agent, as the flow editor holds them. Carried by the request and present exactly when the subject kind is `agent_draft` — the edits exist only in the editor — where it is the whole definition of what ran: the run goes through the same unlinked branch of the agent executor the editor's own test uses.<br>|
|draft_hash|string|false|none|Hash of the configuration a draft run executed, stamped server-side. A draft moves without the version moving, so this is what dates a run of one. It is also what recognises a draft run whose configuration was later deployed: when it matches the agent as deployed, the run's kind and version are rewritten to that version, once, and the hash is kept as what the resolution rests on.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|kind|agent|
|kind|agent_draft|
|kind|agent_version|

<h2 id="tocS_Scorer">Scorer</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemascorer"></a>
<a id="schema_Scorer"></a>
<a id="tocSscorer"></a>
<a id="tocsscorer"></a>

```json
{
  "id": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "pass_if": 0,
  "kind": "script",
  "path": "string"
}
```

A scorer is a column of the results table, and it is always a runnable: an ai_agent resource sent the run to grade, or a script handed the run as an argument. `id` is assigned when the scorer is added to a dataset and never reused: it is what makes a column the same column across experiments when the scorer is renamed, and a delta is only ever computed between two scores carrying the same id. A scorer sent without an id is given one.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|false|none|none|
|name|string|false|none|Column header. Defaults to the last segment of the path.|
|pass_if|number|false|none|A score at or above this counts as a pass, and the column reports a pass rate beside its mean. Applied when results are read rather than when they are produced, so moving the line re-reads every score already recorded instead of invalidating them.<br>|
|kind|string|true|none|none|
|path|string|true|none|The script, or the ai_agent resource used as a judge.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|kind|script|
|kind|agent|

One run of a dataset: written once when the dataset is run, and only ever read afterwards. The case set it executed is returned by the results endpoint, not here: a listing would otherwise send the whole dataset back once per experiment.

|run_number|integer|true|none|This agent's nth run of this dataset, allocated once and never reused. What a run is called. Numbered per agent rather than per subject kind: runs of what is deployed and runs of its draft are the same agent's history.<br>|
|run_job_id|string(uuid)|true|none|The flow executing the run: one job holding every case and its scores.<br>|
|case_count|integer|true|none|none|
|scores|[[ExperimentScore](#schemaexperimentscore)]|false|none|What the run scored, one entry per scorer that produced a number. Carried on the run itself so a list of runs can say what each one scored without reading every cell of every one of them. Empty on a run whose scores have not been read yet.<br>|

|created_at|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|created_by|string|true|none|none|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|none|
|head|object|false|none|none|
|chats|[[AISessionBackupChat](#schemaaisessionbackupchat)]|false|none|none|
|images|[[AISessionBackupImage](#schemaaisessionbackupimage)]|false|none|none|
|artifacts|object|false|none|none|
|delete_chats|[string]|false|none|none|
|delete_images|[object]|false|none|none|
|partial|boolean|false|none|more parts of this session follow, in this push or a later one; the session is not listed on this one. Such a part names its push (`push`), or it is refused|
|whole|boolean|false|none|a part of a push of the session whole; the head is on the part that opens it, which replaces whatever the storage holds of the session, and every piece the browser has is on one of them. An incremental part instead rides on a session the storage lists and is refused with needs_whole when it lists none|
|push|string|false|none|a push split over several parts names itself on each with a token the browser draws; the part that opens it unlists the session and the last part lists it again, and a later part is written only while that token is the one there (refused with needs_whole otherwise)|
|opens|boolean|false|none|this part opens the push named by `push`|
|epoch|integer|false|none|the session's move count (its record's `moves`), kept with the marker that lists the session; an incremental part rides on the marker of the same count|

```json
{
  "type": "script",
  "path": "string",
  "summary": "string",
  "workspace_id": "string",
  "extra_perms": {
    "property1": true,
    "property2": true
  },
  "starred": true,
  "archived": true,
  "is_draft": true,
  "draft_only": true,
  "draft_path": "string",
  "draft_users": [
    {}
  ],
  "labels": [
    "string"
  ],
  "inherited_labels": [
    "string"
  ],
  "ws_error_handler_muted": true,
  "edited_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "hash": "string",
  "language": "string",
  "kind": "string",
  "auto_kind": "string",
  "use_codebase": true,
  "has_deploy_errors": true,
  "chat_input_enabled": true,
  "raw_app": true,
  "execution_mode": "string",
  "id": 0,
  "version": 0,
  "agent_memory": null,
  "ws_specific": true
}
```

A row in the merged runnables listing. `type` is the discriminator;
kind-specific fields (hash/language/kind for scripts, execution_mode/
version for apps, agent_memory/ws_specific for agents) are present only
for that kind. An agent is an `ai_agent` resource whose description is
reported as `summary`. `edited_at` is the unified last-updated time (a
script's created_at, a flow/app/agent's edit time).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|auto_parent|boolean|false|none|When true, the backend resolves the parent to the current deployed head for this path within the transaction (ignoring parent_hash), instead of failing with a "lineage must be linear" error when the supplied parent_hash is stale.|
|summary|string|true|none|none|
|description|string|false|none|none|
|content|string|true|none|none|
|schema|object|false|none|JSON Schema of the arguments of `main`, which is what a run form and an MCP tool offer. Omitted (or `{}`), it is inferred from `content` for TypeScript, Python, Go, Bash, PowerShell, SQL, GraphQL and Ansible scripts. For other languages, or code that does not parse, a new script gets none. A new version of an existing script also keeps what the previous version's schema says about each argument, or that whole schema when nothing can be inferred. A dbt script always takes its schema from its descriptor, whatever is sent.|

Supply this or on_behalf_of_email; when only the address is given it is resolved to the account it names, and an address naming nobody is rejected. A pair that disagrees is rejected.|
|preserve_on_behalf_of|boolean|false|none|When true and the caller is a member of the 'wm_deployers' group, preserves the original on_behalf_of_email / on_behalf_of pair instead of overwriting it with the caller's own identity.|

Jobs it starts, flow steps and AI agent tools inherit the restriction. Unset, the job token carries the full permissions of the identity the job runs as; an empty list leaves it no API access beyond its own job. Omitting the field keeps the deployed value; null clears it.|

<h2 id="tocS_GuestUsage">GuestUsage</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaguestusage"></a>
<a id="schema_GuestUsage"></a>
<a id="tocSguestusage"></a>
<a id="tocsguestusage"></a>

```json
{
  "available": true,
  "guest_count": 0,
  "window_days": 0,
  "free_allowance": 0,
  "metered": true,
  "billable_guests": 0,
  "guest_seats": 0
}
```

Guests are free up to `free_allowance` distinct emails over the trailing `window_days`. Past that an Enterprise plan meters them (`metered`, four guests to one seat: `billable_guests`, `guest_seats`); every other plan and build admits no new email until the count drops. `available` is whether this deployment can have guests at all: false on the shared cloud, where guest access requires a self-hosted or dedicated deployment, and every other field is then moot.

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|available|boolean|true|none|none|
|guest_count|integer(int64)|true|none|none|
|window_days|integer|true|none|none|
|free_allowance|integer(int64)|true|none|none|
|metered|boolean|true|none|none|
|billable_guests|integer(int64)|true|none|none|
|guest_seats|integer(int64)|true|none|none|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|path|string|true|none|The path to the variable|
|value|string|true|none|The value of the variable. For a secret, `$external:vault://<path>#<key>` stores a reference to an existing secret in the instance's external HashiCorp Vault (path as `vault kv get` takes it) instead of a value; without `#<key>` it reads the whole secret as a JSON object of its fields. It is resolved on each read, only under the path prefixes a superadmin allowed for the workspace, and is returned as-is when the secret is not decrypted.<br>|
|is_secret|boolean|true|none|Whether the variable is a secret|
|description|string|true|none|The description of the variable|
|account|integer|false|none|**Deprecated.** Ignored. A variable is linked to an OAuth account only when `createAccount` creates both.|
|is_oauth|boolean|false|none|Whether the variable is an OAuth variable|
|expires_at|string(date-time)|false|none|When to garbage-collect the variable. Used for ephemeral secrets; the variable is deleted once this is reached. Not the value's expiry — see value_valid_until.<br>|
|value_valid_until|string(date-time)|false|none|When the value stored in this variable stops working. Triggers the workspace's variable expiration handler ahead of it, by the handler's `notify_before_secs` (1 day by default); never causes the variable to be deleted.<br>|
|labels|[string]|false|none|none|
|ws_specific|boolean|false|none|none|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|path|string|true|none|The unique Windmill path for this schedule. Must be of the form `u/<user>/<path>` or `f/<folder>/<path>`.|
|edited_by|string|true|none|Username of the last person who edited this schedule|
|edited_at|string(date-time)|true|none|Timestamp of the last edit|
|schedule|string|true|none|Cron expression with 6 fields (seconds, minutes, hours, day of month, month, day of week). Example '0 0 12 * * *' for daily at noon|
|timezone|string|true|none|IANA timezone for the schedule (e.g., 'UTC', 'Europe/Paris', 'America/New_York')|
|enabled|boolean|true|none|Whether the schedule is currently active and will trigger jobs|
|script_path|string|true|none|Path to the script or flow to execute when triggered|
|is_flow|boolean|true|none|True if script_path points to a flow, false if it points to a script|
|args|[ScriptArgs](#schemascriptargs)|false|none|The arguments to pass to the script or flow|
|extra_perms|object|true|none|Additional permissions for this schedule|
|email|string|true|none|Email of the user who owns this schedule, used for permissioned_as|
|permissioned_as|string|true|none|The user or group this schedule runs as (e.g., 'u/admin' or 'g/mygroup')|
|error|string \| null|false|none|Last error message if the schedule failed to trigger|
|on_failure|string \| null|false|none|Path to a script or flow to run when the scheduled job fails|
|on_failure_times|number \| null|false|none|Number of consecutive failures before the on_failure handler is triggered (default 1)|
|on_failure_exact|boolean \| null|false|none|If true, trigger on_failure handler only on exactly N failures, not on every failure after N|
|on_failure_extra_args|[ScriptArgs](#schemascriptargs)|false|none|The arguments to pass to the script or flow|
|on_recovery|string \| null|false|none|Path to a script or flow to run when the schedule recovers after failures|
|on_recovery_times|number \| null|false|none|Number of consecutive successes before the on_recovery handler is triggered (default 1)|
|on_recovery_extra_args|[ScriptArgs](#schemascriptargs)|false|none|The arguments to pass to the script or flow|
|on_success|string \| null|false|none|Path to a script or flow to run after each successful execution|
|on_success_extra_args|[ScriptArgs](#schemascriptargs)|false|none|The arguments to pass to the script or flow|
|ws_error_handler_muted|boolean|false|none|If true, the workspace-level error handler will not be triggered for this schedule's failures|
|retry|[Retry](#schemaretry)|false|none|Retry configuration for failed module executions|
|summary|string \| null|false|none|Short summary describing the purpose of this schedule|
|description|string \| null|false|none|Detailed description of what this schedule does|
|no_flow_overlap|boolean|false|none|If true, skip this schedule's execution if the previous run is still in progress (prevents concurrent runs)|
|tag|string \| null|false|none|Worker tag to route jobs to specific worker groups|
|paused_until|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|ISO 8601 datetime until which the schedule is paused. Schedule resumes automatically after this time|
|cron_version|string \| null|false|none|Cron parser version. Use 'v2' for extended syntax with additional features|
|dynamic_skip|string \| null|false|none|Path to a script that validates scheduled datetimes. Receives scheduled_for datetime and returns boolean to skip (true) or run (false)|
|labels|[string]|false|none|none|
|draft_only|boolean|false|none|True when this row is a per-user draft with no deployed<br>schedule at the same path. Frontend renders a "Draft" badge.<br>|
|is_draft|boolean|false|none|True when the authed user has a per-user draft at this path<br>(over a deployed row or a synthesized draft-only row).<br>Frontend appends a `*` to the displayed name.<br>|
|inherited_labels|[string]|false|none|Labels inherited from the parent folder, computed at read time. Read-only — edit them on the folder.<br>|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|path|string|true|none|The unique Windmill path for this trigger. Must be of the form `u/<user>/<path>` or `f/<folder>/<path>`. This is the trigger object path, not the HTTP route path.|
|script_path|string|true|none|Path to the script or flow to execute when triggered|
|permissioned_as|string|true|none|The user or group this trigger runs as (permissioned_as)|
|extra_perms|object|true|none|Additional permissions for this trigger|
|workspace_id|string|true|none|The workspace this trigger belongs to|
|edited_by|string|true|none|Username of the last person who edited this trigger|
|edited_at|string(date-time)|true|none|Timestamp of the last edit|
|is_flow|boolean|true|none|True if script_path points to a flow, false if it points to a script|
|mode|[TriggerMode](#schematriggermode)|true|none|Trigger mode (enabled/disabled)|
|labels|[string]|false|none|none|
|draft_only|boolean|false|none|True when this row is a per-user draft with no deployed<br>trigger at the same path. Set by list endpoints when<br>`include_draft_only=true` synthesizes the row from the<br>draft. Frontend renders a "Draft" badge.<br>|
|is_draft|boolean|false|none|True when the authed user has a per-user draft at this path<br>(over a deployed row or a synthesized draft-only row).<br>Frontend appends a `*` to the displayed name.<br>|
|route_path|string|true|none|The URL route path that will trigger this endpoint (e.g., 'api/myendpoint'). Must NOT start with a /.|
|static_asset_config|object \| null|false|none|Configuration for serving static assets (s3 bucket, storage path, filename)|
|http_method|[HttpMethod](#schemahttpmethod)|true|none|HTTP method (get, post, put, delete, patch) that triggers this endpoint|
|authentication_resource_path|string \| null|false|none|Path to the resource containing authentication configuration (for api_key, basic_http, custom_script, signature methods)|
|summary|string \| null|false|none|Short summary describing the purpose of this trigger|
|description|string \| null|false|none|Detailed description of what this trigger does|
|request_type|[HttpRequestType](#schemahttprequesttype)|true|none|How the request is handled - 'sync' waits for result, 'async' returns job ID immediately, 'sync_sse' streams results via Server-Sent Events|
|authentication_method|[AuthenticationMethod](#schemaauthenticationmethod)|true|none|How requests are authenticated - 'none' (public), 'windmill' (Windmill token), 'api_key', 'basic_http', 'custom_script', 'signature'|
|is_static_website|boolean|true|none|If true, serves static files from S3/storage instead of running a script|
|workspaced_route|boolean|true|none|If true, the route includes the workspace ID in the path|
|wrap_body|boolean|true|none|If true, wraps the request body in a 'body' parameter|
|raw_string|boolean|true|none|If true, passes the request body as a raw string instead of parsing as JSON|
|allowed_origins|[string]|false|none|Origins allowed to call this route cross-origin, matched against the request's Origin header (ignoring case) and echoed back on a match. When set, the list governs both the preflight and the response, overriding any Access-Control-Allow-Origin the runnable returns via wm_headers. Use ['*'] to opt out of any restriction, including the http_route_default_allowed_origins instance setting. An empty list is not a configuration and resolves exactly as null does. When null, the instance setting applies, or Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * if it is unset. Ignored on a static website, which has no authentication of its own and so hands out public files: restricting which browsers may read them protects nothing while breaking cross-origin webfonts and fetches. A single-file static asset is not exempt, since it can carry an authentication_method.|
|error_handler_path|string|false|none|Path to a script to run when the triggered job fails. A bare path, without the script/ or flow/ prefix a schedule error handler takes; it cannot be a flow.|
|error_handler_args|[ScriptArgs](#schemascriptargs)|false|none|Arguments to pass to the error handler|
|retry|[Retry](#schemaretry)|false|none|Retry configuration for failed executions|

<a id="schema_WebsocketHeartbeat"></a>

```json
{
  "interval_secs": 1,
  "message": "string",
  "state_field": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|interval_secs|integer|true|none|Interval in seconds between heartbeat messages|
|message|string|true|none|Message to send as heartbeat. Use {{state}} as a placeholder for a value extracted from incoming messages (see state_field).|
|state_field|string|false|none|Optional. Top-level JSON field to extract from incoming messages. The extracted value replaces {{state}} in the heartbeat message.|

<h2 id="tocS_TriggerFilter">TriggerFilter</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematriggerfilter"></a>
<a id="schema_TriggerFilter"></a>
<a id="tocStriggerfilter"></a>
<a id="tocstriggerfilter"></a>

```json
{
  "key": "string",
  "value": null
}
```

Either a leaf filter, matching a field of the message (parsed as JSON) against a value by equality (or superset, when the value is an object or array) — addressed by `key` for a top-level field or `path` for a dotted path into nested objects — or a group nesting sub-filters under a boolean operator (`none_of` matches when none of its sub-filters do).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|none|
|key|string|true|none|none|
|value|object|true|none|none|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|none|
|path|string|true|none|Dotted path into nested objects, e.g. `a.b.c`. Does not traverse arrays.|
|value|object|true|none|none|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|none|
|any_of|[[TriggerFilter](#schematriggerfilter)]|true|none|none|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|none|
|all_of|[[TriggerFilter](#schematriggerfilter)]|true|none|none|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|none|
|none_of|[[TriggerFilter](#schematriggerfilter)]|true|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_WebsocketTrigger">WebsocketTrigger</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemawebsockettrigger"></a>
<a id="schema_WebsocketTrigger"></a>
<a id="tocSwebsockettrigger"></a>
<a id="tocswebsockettrigger"></a>

```json
{
  "path": "string",
  "script_path": "string",
  "permissioned_as": "string",
  "extra_perms": {
    "property1": true,
    "property2": true
  },
  "workspace_id": "string",
  "edited_by": "string",
  "edited_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "is_flow": true,
  "mode": "enabled",
  "labels": [],
  "draft_only": true,
  "is_draft": true,
  "url": "string",
  "server_id": "string",
  "last_server_ping": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "error": "string",
  "filters": [
    {
      "key": "string",
      "value": null
    }
  ],
  "filter_logic": "and",
  "initial_messages": [
    {
      "raw_message": "string"
    }
  ],
  "url_runnable_args": {},
  "can_return_message": true,
  "can_return_error_result": true,
  "heartbeat": {
    "interval_secs": 1,
    "message": "string",
    "state_field": "string"
  },
  "error_handler_path": "string",
  "error_handler_args": {},
  "retry": {
    "constant": {
      "attempts": 0,
      "seconds": 0
    },
    "exponential": {
      "attempts": 0,
      "multiplier": 0,
      "seconds": 1,
      "random_factor": 0
    },
    "retry_if": {
      "expr": "string"
    }
  }
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|path|string|true|none|The unique Windmill path for this trigger. Must be of the form `u/<user>/<path>` or `f/<folder>/<path>`. This is the trigger object path, not the HTTP route path.|
|script_path|string|true|none|Path to the script or flow to execute when triggered|
|permissioned_as|string|true|none|The user or group this trigger runs as (permissioned_as)|
|extra_perms|object|true|none|Additional permissions for this trigger|
|workspace_id|string|true|none|The workspace this trigger belongs to|
|edited_by|string|true|none|Username of the last person who edited this trigger|
|edited_at|string(date-time)|true|none|Timestamp of the last edit|
|is_flow|boolean|true|none|True if script_path points to a flow, false if it points to a script|
|mode|[TriggerMode](#schematriggermode)|true|none|Trigger mode (enabled/disabled)|
|labels|[string]|false|none|none|
|draft_only|boolean|false|none|True when this row is a per-user draft with no deployed<br>trigger at the same path. Set by list endpoints when<br>`include_draft_only=true` synthesizes the row from the<br>draft. Frontend renders a "Draft" badge.<br>|
|is_draft|boolean|false|none|True when the authed user has a per-user draft at this path<br>(over a deployed row or a synthesized draft-only row).<br>Frontend appends a `*` to the displayed name.<br>|
|url|string|true|none|The WebSocket URL to connect to (can be a static URL or computed by a runnable)|
|server_id|string|false|none|ID of the server currently handling this trigger (internal)|
|last_server_ping|string(date-time)|false|none|Timestamp of last server heartbeat (internal)|
|error|string|false|none|Last error message if the trigger failed|
|filters|[[TriggerFilter](#schematriggerfilter)]|true|none|Filters to match incoming messages (only matching messages trigger the script). Each entry is either a leaf `{key, value}` (top-level field) or `{path, value}` (dotted path into nested objects), or a group `{any_of: [...]}` / `{all_of: [...]}` / `{none_of: [...]}` nesting more entries. Entries at the top level are combined with `filter_logic`.|
|filter_logic|string|false|none|Logic to apply when evaluating the top-level filters. 'and' requires all of them to match, 'or' requires any of them to match. Nested `any_of`/`all_of`/`none_of` groups carry their own logic.|
|initial_messages|[[WebsocketTriggerInitialMessage](#schemawebsockettriggerinitialmessage)]|false|none|Messages to send immediately after connecting (can be raw strings or computed by runnables)|
|url_runnable_args|[ScriptArgs](#schemascriptargs)|false|none|Arguments to pass to the script/flow that computes the WebSocket URL|
|can_return_message|boolean|true|none|If true, the script can return a message to send back through the WebSocket|
|can_return_error_result|boolean|true|none|If true, error results are sent back through the WebSocket|
|heartbeat|[WebsocketHeartbeat](#schemawebsocketheartbeat)|false|none|Optional periodic heartbeat message configuration|
|error_handler_path|string|false|none|Path to a script to run when the triggered job fails. A bare path, without the script/ or flow/ prefix a schedule error handler takes; it cannot be a flow.|
|error_handler_args|[ScriptArgs](#schemascriptargs)|false|none|Arguments to pass to the error handler|
|retry|[Retry](#schemaretry)|false|none|Retry configuration for failed executions|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|mode|enabled|
|mode|disabled|
|mode|suspended|
|filter_logic|and|
|filter_logic|or|

|script_path|string|true|none|Path to the script or flow to execute when triggered|
|permissioned_as|string|true|none|The user or group this trigger runs as (permissioned_as)|
|extra_perms|object|true|none|Additional permissions for this trigger|
|workspace_id|string|true|none|The workspace this trigger belongs to|
|edited_by|string|true|none|Username of the last person who edited this trigger|
|edited_at|string(date-time)|true|none|Timestamp of the last edit|

|gcp_resource_path|string|false|none|Path to the GCP resource containing service account credentials for authentication. Omit to authenticate with the instance's application default credentials.|
|project_id|string|false|none|GCP project the client operates in. Defaults to the project of the credentials. Topics and subscriptions given as fully qualified names are reached whatever it is.|

|subscription_id|string|true|none|Google Cloud Pub/Sub subscription ID. Accepts a bare ID or a fully qualified name (projects/<project>/subscriptions/<id>).|
|server_id|string|false|none|ID of the server currently handling this trigger (internal use).|
|delivery_type|[DeliveryType](#schemadeliverytype)|true|none|Delivery mode for messages. 'push' for HTTP push delivery where messages are sent to a webhook endpoint, 'pull' for polling where the trigger actively fetches messages.|
|delivery_config|[PushConfig](#schemapushconfig)|false|none|Configuration for push delivery mode.|
|subscription_mode|[SubscriptionMode](#schemasubscriptionmode)|true|none|The mode of subscription. 'existing' means using an existing GCP subscription, while 'create_update' involves creating or updating a new subscription.|

|error|string|false|none|Last error message if the trigger failed.|
|error_handler_path|string|false|none|Path to a script or flow to run when the triggered job fails.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|path|string|true|none|The unique Windmill path for this trigger. Must be of the form `u/<user>/<path>` or `f/<folder>/<path>`. This is the trigger object path, not the HTTP route path.|
|script_path|string|true|none|Path to the script or flow to execute when triggered|
|permissioned_as|string|true|none|The user or group this trigger runs as (permissioned_as)|
|extra_perms|object|true|none|Additional permissions for this trigger|
|workspace_id|string|true|none|The workspace this trigger belongs to|
|edited_by|string|true|none|Username of the last person who edited this trigger|
|edited_at|string(date-time)|true|none|Timestamp of the last edit|
|is_flow|boolean|true|none|True if script_path points to a flow, false if it points to a script|
|mode|[TriggerMode](#schematriggermode)|true|none|Trigger mode (enabled/disabled)|
|labels|[string]|false|none|none|

|publication_name|string|true|none|Name of the PostgreSQL publication to subscribe to for change data capture|

|replication_slot_name|string|true|none|Name of the PostgreSQL logical replication slot to use|

|last_server_ping|string(date-time)|false|none|Timestamp of last server heartbeat (internal)|

Resource usage of the jobs of one runnable on one worker group. Memory and CPU are only known for jobs run as a subprocess; memory is the peak of the job's main process.

|total_duration_ms|integer|true|none|none|
|max_memory_peak|integer|true|none|highest peak memory of a job, in kB|
|sum_memory_peak|integer|true|none|sum of the peak memory of the jobs that have one, in kB|
|memory_sample_count|integer|true|none|number of jobs that have a peak memory reading|
|total_cpu_ms|integer|true|none|none|

|shared_ducklakes|[string]|false|none|Lake names the fork SHARES with the parent (reads and writes the parent's lake directly). Every lake not listed gets the default isolated fork namespace with read-defer to the parent.|
|shared_storages|[string]|false|none|Workspace storages the fork SHARES with the parent (`_default_` for the primary one): it reads and writes the parent's objects directly. Every storage not listed is isolated: the fork writes under its own prefix and reads through to the parent's objects.|

|lock_prod_deploy|boolean|false|none|When creating a dev workspace, lock the parent (prod) against direct deployment|
|lock_prod_forking|boolean|false|none|When creating a dev workspace, prevent forking the parent (prod)|
|copy_members|boolean|false|none|Copy the parent's members (users + group memberships) into the fork so the team can work in it|
|dev_workspace_label|string|false|none|Environment label for the dev workspace: its badge text and the branch it deploys to. Ignored for non-dev forks. Omitted defaults to 'dev'|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|summary|string|true|none|Short description of what this flow does|
|description|string|false|none|Detailed documentation for this flow|
|value|[FlowValue](#schemaflowvalue)|true|none|The flow structure containing modules and optional preprocessor/failure handlers|
|schema|object|false|none|JSON Schema for flow inputs. Use this to define input parameters, their types, defaults, and validation. For resource inputs, set type to 'object' and format to 'resource-<type>' (e.g., 'resource-stripe')|
|on_behalf_of_email|string|false|none|Address of the account the flow runs on behalf of. Derived from on_behalf_of on read; accepted on write, where it is resolved to the account it names.|
|on_behalf_of|string|false|none|The flow runs with the permissions of this identity: u/{username}, g/{group}, or a bare email when the username is itself email-shaped. The only stored half of the identity; on_behalf_of_email is derived from it. Omit it when writing and it is resolved from that address instead.|
|path|string|true|none|none|
|tag|string|false|none|none|
|ws_error_handler_muted|boolean|false|none|none|
|priority|integer|false|none|none|
|dedicated_worker|boolean|false|none|none|
|timeout|number|false|none|none|
|visible_to_runner_only|boolean|false|none|none|
|on_behalf_of_email|string|false|none|none|
|on_behalf_of|string|false|none|Authorization identity to run as: u/{username}, g/{group}, or a bare email when the username is itself email-shaped. Supply this or on_behalf_of_email; when only the address is given it is resolved to the account it names, and an address naming nobody is rejected. A pair that disagrees is rejected.|
|preserve_on_behalf_of|boolean|false|none|When true and the caller is a member of the 'wm_deployers' group, preserves the original on_behalf_of_email / on_behalf_of pair instead of overwriting it with the caller's own identity.|
|labels|[string]|false|none|none|
|job_token_scopes|[string]|false|none|Scopes the token of every job of this runnable is restricted to (domain:action[:resource], e.g. oidc:write). Jobs it starts, flow steps and AI agent tools inherit the restriction. Unset, the job token carries the full permissions of the identity the job runs as; an empty list leaves it no API access beyond its own job. Omitting the field keeps the deployed value; null clears it.|

  ],

    {
      "s3_path": "string",
      "resource": "string"
    }
  ],
  "execution_mode": "viewer",
  "on_behalf_of": "string",
  "on_behalf_of_email": "string",
  "sandbox": true,
  "frontend_sdk_scopes": [
    "string"
  ]

```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|triggerables|object|false|none|none|
|triggerables_v2|object|false|none|none|
|s3_inputs|[object]|false|none|none|
|allowed_s3_keys|[object]|false|none|none|
|execution_mode|string|false|none|Who may open the app, and who its runnables execute as. Optional, and what omitting it means depends on the operation: creating an app defaults it to `publisher` (runs on behalf of the app's publisher and requires an authenticated viewer), while updating one keeps the mode the app is already deployed under. Neither `anonymous`, which makes the app publicly executable, nor `guest`, which opens it to anyone the identity provider authenticates, is ever assumed. Widening an app to `guest` is gated by the `RestrictGuestAppDeployment` protection rule|
|on_behalf_of|string|false|none|The user or group the app runs as in anonymous or publisher mode (e.g. 'u/admin' or 'g/mygroup'). The authority for the app's identity.|
|on_behalf_of_email|string|false|none|Address of `on_behalf_of`, written through from it on every save and returned as stored. Optional; when absent it is derived from `on_behalf_of`. Sending it is optional too; it must name the same account as `on_behalf_of`, and a pair that disagrees is rejected.|
|sandbox|boolean|false|none|Publisher opt-in to app sandbox isolation (alpha). When true the app is isolated from each viewer's Windmill session. When false/absent the app runs same-origin with the viewer's full session (the default, pre-isolation behavior).<br>|
|frontend_sdk_scopes|[string]|false|none|Raw apps: author-declared scopes for the frontend SDK token. Takes effect only when `sandbox` is also true — an unsandboxed bundle runs with the viewer's own session, so no token is advertised or minted for it and this list stays inert. On a sandboxed app a non-empty list lets viewers mint (after consenting) a short-lived token carrying their own identity restricted to these scopes, handed to the app bundle so `windmill-client` calls run as the viewer. Must be a subset of the server's curated allowlist (jobs:run, jobs:read, users:read, resources:read, variables:read, flow_conversations:read, flow_conversations:write). Every such token can call whoami without consent, whether `users:read` is declared or not.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|execution_mode|viewer|
|execution_mode|publisher|
|execution_mode|guest|
|execution_mode|anonymous|

What a deploy of an existing app answers with. `version` is the one this call wrote, which is what an editor pins as the fork base of the draft it starts next: reading the head back afterwards cannot tell it from a deploy that landed beside it.   "raw_app": true,
  "sandbox": true,
  "app_path": "string",

    "string"
  ],
  "viewer_email": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|token|string \| null|false|none|Scoped token for the app. For sandboxed low-code apps this is the embed token handed to the opaque iframe. For a raw app it is the viewer-scoped frontend SDK token, returned only when the app is sandboxed, its policy declares frontend_sdk_scopes, and the request carries sdk_consent=true. Absent for anonymous viewers and whenever no token is needed.<br>|
|expiration|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|Expiration of the embed token.|
|raw_app|boolean|true|none|Raw apps render single-iframe and skip the opaque-viewer indirection and the embed token entirely. A sandboxed one may still carry a token here: the viewer-scoped frontend SDK token, which is a different credential from the low-code embed token.<br>|
|sandbox|boolean|true|none|Publisher opted this app into sandbox isolation. When false the viewer runs the app same-origin with its full session.|
|app_path|string \| null|false|none|The resolved app path; the embedder uses it to scope the app's backing localStorage per app.|
|workspace_id|string \| null|false|none|The resolved workspace; pairs with app_path so apps at the same path in different workspaces don't share a localStorage store.|
|sdk_scopes|[string]|false|none|Sandboxed raw apps: scopes the app policy declares for the frontend SDK token. Null when the app is unsandboxed, however the policy reads. The viewer renders these in the permission prompt; token stays absent until the endpoint is re-called with sdk_consent=true.<br>|
|viewer_email|string \| null|false|none|The caller's own email, returned alongside sdk_scopes so the viewer can key its stored "do not ask again" per person.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_DeployEventKind">DeployEventKind</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadeployeventkind"></a>
<a id="schema_DeployEventKind"></a>
<a id="tocSdeployeventkind"></a>
<a id="tocsdeployeventkind"></a>

```json
"write"
```

What a deploy event did to the path it is recorded against: `write` (the path holds an item
after the event), `delete` (it does not), or `rename_from` (the path was vacated by a rename
to another path). Create and update are not distinguished. Omitted when no such event has
been recorded for that side, which counts as no evidence.

<h2 id="tocS_DeployEventOrigin">DeployEventOrigin</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadeployeventorigin"></a>
<a id="schema_DeployEventOrigin"></a>
<a id="tocSdeployeventorigin"></a>
<a id="tocsdeployeventorigin"></a>

```json
"authored"
```

Who caused a deploy event: `authored` (written in that workspace by the requester) or `sync`
(applied there by a git-sync pull or a workspace-to-workspace deploy). Only an authored
removal is evidence that the workspace dropped the item on purpose. Omitted when no such
event has been recorded for that side.

  "script_path": "string",
  "table_path": "string",
  "kind": "measure",
  "name": "string",
  "expr": "string",
  "filter": "string"
}
```

One `// measure` or `// dimension` declaration, as catalogued from the
script that materializes the table. `expr` and `filter` are the author's
own SQL: a reader renders a measure as `expr` plus, when `filter` is set,
a trailing `FILTER (WHERE filter)`.

|name|string|true|none|none|
|expr|string|true|none|none|
|filter|string|false|none|Row predicate from a measure's trailing `where`|

|kind|dimension|

  "asset_path": "string",

  "expected_type": "string",
  "found_type": "string",
  "schema_version": 0,
  "captured_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "message": "string"
}
```

One save-time schema-contract warning: a consumer reference that does
not match the referenced asset's latest captured schema.
`schema_version`/`captured_at` identify the capture the check ran
against (as-of the producer's last run, not its latest save).
